entries.name: Black Knight (Crossbow)
entries.description:
The crossbow is the ranged preference of the Black Knight, mainly thanks to its stopping power. An avernic demon will rush a target at distance and then slash in close quarters. Having a crossbow stops a demon from getting to that troublesome second stage.

Our assumption is that you are not a demon, but the sentiment still applies. You will want to avoid a crossbow-wielding Black Knight at distance, and instead move in for a spot of slashing. You need to search for the demon inside yourself.

entries.name: Black Knight (Melee)
entries.description:
Insurance coverage as a Black Knight must be inordinately expensive. You'd need indemnities against demon attacks, dragonfire, magi and even your own leader, the Black Knight Titan. That's before you get into the intangible stuff: madness, demonic infestation, the Withering.

Imagine surviving that gauntlet of threats, only to see adventurers arriving on boats. Adventurers love killing knights: it's a genetic predisposition. 

Spare a thought for the Black Knight, weathered by life's challenges. Consider letting them live today. The Champions' Guild have even cooked up an initiative: GAKAB month. It stands for 'Give a Knight a Break' month.

entries.name: Black Knight Titan
entries.description:
The Dreaming Stone had been shattered. 

Lord Rasmodel, on his knees, heard no voices. For the first time in too, too long, he could hear his own breath. His heart played a welcome beat. For decades, he had felt like he floated above the world. Now he was part of it again.

Footsteps. Lord Rasmodel lifted his head wearily. Who would interrupt this moment?

Ringing around him was his family. The Rasmodels. They were all there - all the ones he knew, loved and had met. They were dressed as the finest nobility, the Rasmodels at their height. They had regained their standing - the name meant something again. 

His father knelt down and lifted Lord Rasmodel's bloody chin. Their eyes met. "Rest", his father said. "We will take it from here."

Milliburn Rasmodel, twenty-fifth Lord of Rasmodel, took his retirement.

entries.name: Black Knight Warrior
entries.description: Lord Rasmodel rarely entrusted the rookies with any meaningful work. He found that they arrived with chaos in their hearts: they weren't old enough to realise that chaos is an ideal and rarely works in the day-to-day. So, he would give them the role of 'Warriors', and would loosely allocate them an area of the Reach to wander. "Let their cynicism grow", Rasmodel would say. "If the demons or magi don't kill them first, they might harden into one of the good ones."

entries.name: Colossal Vault Guardian Melee
entries.description:
Weakness: Crush
Resistance: None
Immune: Poison, Bleed, Burning

A pride of Brakka’s ingenuity, the Vault Overlord towers over the other vault guardians as a shiny example of one dragonkin’s ego. Larger and more physically powerful than the other guardians, the Overlord was a siege engine put to work as a bodyguard. 

It was set to guard Brakka’s most prized treasures. Objects he kept in the vaults, so that none but he might gaze upon their beauty. 

In time the other dragonkin learned of the Overlord and created versions of their own, setting them to guard their secrets against any that might dare pilfer them. 

In the time of the dragon uprising, the Overlords could have proved a useful soldier against Kuldra’s brood. Yet the arrogance and shortsightedness, of their dragonkin masters, meant that these walking siege weapons would never see the light of day.

entries.name: Colossal Vault Guardian Ranged
entries.description:
Weakness: Crush
Resistance: None
Immune: Poison, Bleed, Burning

Rasthin was never fond of just leaving things to chance. She always saw a need to create bigger, deadlier, weapons with which to destroy her foes. With the dragons she encouraged Lacrussa’s experiments, searching for ways to make them into a more potent force. With the vault guardians she pushed them further still.

The archon is a marvel of dragonkin science. Infused with enough magical force to level a small village, if left uncontained. The magic that runs through its circuits acts as a connection to all the other guardians, motivating and animating them by the archon’s will.

At the height of their power, these creatures could out-strategise the most cunning generals. Fortunately, time has dulled this wits and their reflexes, reducing them to a strength only deadly to a village, rather than a nation.

entries.name: Delrom
entries.description:
This is not Delrom's first summoning rodeo. He was summoned once before into ScapeRune - a twisted, upside-down version of RuneScape. 

To his dismay, he was the subject of a quest called 'Demon Lover'. Let's just say that the only demon rings were the ones that adventurers wanted to put on his finger.

In the end, he managed to unsummon himself by wielding Darklight and saying the magical phrase Reba Melrac Muhtniremac Odnibag Iahcrup. It was a close call.

entries.name: Dragon Fuzan
entries.description:
Youngest of Kuldra’s brood, Fuzan grew up spoilt and childish. Where other dragons sought strategy, family, or some loftier goal, Fuzan only cared about the next dopamine hit brought on my mindless destruction. We’ve all known kids like that.

As he grew older, he began to seek experiences in more dangerous places. He picked fights with other dragons. Bullied the monsters roaming the lands. He brought chaos everywhere he went, in the hopes that it might mildly alleviate some of his boredom.

In the heart of a volcano, as he gazed into the purest fires, he found something other than amusement to cling onto.

He found faith.

Faith in a being not of this world: born of celestial fire so bright that it made Fuzan’s own mighty flames seem like mere candlelight in comparison. This being spoke through flames. Her words were flickering embers. Her laughter the crackle of flames. Her platitudes swirled in the air, carried aloft by ashes.

She claimed to be a god, and she promised him that Fuzan would burn hotter, shine brighter, and ignite the world under his own light—rather then spend his life in his mother’s shadow. It was an offer too enticing to refuse.

Under her tutelage, Fuzan learned to better wield his own flames and the flames of others. He seized control of the gentle KotHaar and he began marking the garou, igniting their souls as kindling and taking their strength for his own.

It is better that he is dead. For everyone’s sake.

entries.name: Fellhollow Imaru
entries.description:
Once, Imaru was a gentle creature. She and her mate, the black dragon Xikotal, would dance through the air together, lost in their love. Although the dragon’s rage still burned inside her, the cooling power of the water she was infused with, calmed her and brought the reason and clarity that she enjoyed.

Dragonkin experiments had robbed her of the one thing she craved, to be a mother. So when the humans came to the region, she convinced Xikotal that they should take them under their wing, becoming protectors and, perhaps, even parents to the fragile things.

Together they built a society with peace and cooperation at its core. The villagers thrived, and Imaru and her mate thrived with them. She used the magic within her to bless her new pets, making sure that she could protect them wherever they were.

How cruel a thing is fate? Once protector, Imaru became the threat. After being slain by Kuldra, Imaru became a blighted thing. She refused to pass into the afterlife and wedged herself within the river of souls, feasting on the dead of Fellhollow in search of power. Once the guardian of her beloved adopted children, Imaru was lost to everything but the rage and the grief. She would have torn apart the world for one more shot at Kuldra.

Fortunately, that won’t be an option.

entries.name: Fellhollow Lost Soul
entries.description: A wandering spirit, desperately clawing at any hint of life. Pity them and move on, you cannot help them.

entries.name: Fellhollow Soulstone Sentinel
entries.description: Once guardians of souls, they have become twisted by Imaru’s fury into something else. They wait behind spectral doors, ready to add more soulstones to their collection, by murdering any living being that intrudes upon their realm.
pages: Once guardians of souls, they have become twisted by Imaru’s fury into something else. They wait behind spectral doors, ready to add more soulstones to their collection, by murdering any living being that intrudes upon their realm.

entries.name: Fellhollow Zombie
entries.description:
The dead should not move like this, yet these creatures don’t seem to have gotten that message. Undead are normally animated by magic, though some are motivated by stranger things.

These undead are animated by hunger, and the desperate final moments of what is left of their soul. Regrets, need and pain drive muscle, sinew and bone into motion, creating this most pitiable of creatures.

entries.name: Garou Berserker
entries.description:
Weakness: Ranged
Resistance: Air

The garou berserker is a force to be reckoned with. Before each battle, they feast on a freshly killed animal and ingest a concoction that alters their perception. This turns their world into kill or be killed, and nothing can persuade them otherwise. 

Druids control berserkers with subtle magic. They manipulate the air around them so that they don’t give off a scent. To the fury-addled mind of the berserker, this makes them practically invisible, and at the very least, it confirms that they are not a threat. 

Once in their battle state, a berserker will hurl themselves at an opponent, regardless of the enemy’s might. Fighting tooth and nail, as if each breath is in desperation.  In the dragon wars, they were known to charge at the great beasts, becoming little more than snacks in their recklessness.

entries.name: Garou Hunter
entries.description:
Weakness: Air
Resistance: Crush

The lower-born garou can never rise to the role of king. Many have tried, but all have failed. The highborn are simply stronger and wield magic that the lowborn cannot match. They are not mistreated by their kin. There are no garou slaves or servants, but a lowborn garou can never rule.

Most accept their place and find a way to be useful, a means to enjoy the most important thing to their kind—the hunt. 

Nothing ignites the blood of a garou more than the hunt. It reaches into a primal part of their being and gives them a reason to live. All worries are cast aside. All responsibilities forgotten. There is nothing but the thrill of the chase and the anticipation of the kill. 

It is no surprise, therefore, that lowborn garou often take up the hunter's mantle. Their precision with a bow is practically unmatched, and they delight in nothing more than seeing their quarry draw its last breath.

entries.name: General Velgar
entries.description:
Weakness: None
Resistance: None
Immune: Poison, Burning

General Velgar was one of Kuldra’s most trusted allies in the dragon rebellion. In the years that led to her betrayal of their dragonkin masters, she would seek Velgar’s advice on how to best handle the situation. His answer was always clear, brutality was the only language that their masters would understand.

He had been Brakka’s beast of burden. A mighty warrior, forced to be little more than a pack mule for the arrogant architect of the dragonkin. When the war against the goblins and the humans brought the dragons into the conflict, Velgar was finally allowed to join the battle. He slaughtered without mercy, obliterating settlements and entire platoons with barely a sweat.

Brakka rewarded his brutality with yet more chains. When the conflict dulled, Velgar was made to haul stone and metal, so that Brakka could rebuild damaged fortresses.

It is perhaps no wonder, therefore, that he accepted Kuldra’s scheme without hesitation. The first to join her war, aside from her own child. She taught him to absorb the power of the anima font, transforming him into a dragon infused with the might of the earth itself.

entries.name: Goblin Archer
entries.description:
Weakness: Stab
Resistance: None

A goblin archer is swift and merciless. They have no sense of honour to hold them back, no morality to keep their hand. To a goblin, battle for battle’s sake is the purest endeavour, and a clean kill is the most noble act. 

Archers possess a trait rarely found in goblinkind, patience. They wait out their prey, lining up that perfect shot to send their target to the afterlife. Despite this, they are often looked down on by other goblins for their cowardice. The warriors mock them for hiding in the rear lines and attacking from the safety of distance. 

It’s an insult that goblin archers hear often, though rarely from the same goblin twice. This is mainly because the warriors don’t tend to live long enough to repeat it.

entries.name: Goblin Bruiser
entries.description:
Weakness: Fire
Resistance: None

Might makes right and these goblins are never wrong.

The leaders of the goblin tribes by strength alone, the bruisers enjoy nothing more than a life of bullying other goblins around. They are assumed to be the smartest, because if you tell them they’re wrong, you’ll get a fist in the face. They’re the most charismatic, because if you don’t like what they’re saying… well… fist and face return once more. In fact most of their skillset consists of fists approaching faces at high velocity.

They are one of the few goblins with brains enough to wedge a large sheet of metal between their vulnerable internal organs and the person poking at them with a sharp object. So in goblin society that makes them an unrivalled genius.

entries.name: Goblin Warrior
entries.description:
Weakness: Fire
Resistance: None

Goblins were once the minions of the war god, Bandos, until his death at the hands of Armadyl, the god of justice. Raised on the brutal world of Yu’Biusk, goblins have known no other existence than one of constant battle and bloodshed. Their religion and society decries education and self-improvement in favour of conflict for conflict’s sake. To run from battle is the greatest sin to goblinkind. 

Goblins reproduce quickly and grow up fast. Many of their wars have been won by sheer attrition, as there are always more goblins to hurl at the enemy.   

The goblins of Ashenfall have turned away from Bandos, putting their faith in the dragon that circles Ghornfell. Velgar is a cruel and uncaring master, yet the goblins live longer lifespans under his watch than they ever did under Bandos.

entries.name: Hookworm
entries.description: The insides of Kuldra are filled with more than just flesh. She has gorged herself on anima and her blood contains the last remnants of a fallen goddess. Kuldra herself is close to divinity, held back by dragonkin safeguards that prevent her from achieving her full potential. Yet, that power must flow somewhere and within her flesh crawl the vile heartworms: warped parasites empowered by this excess of magic. These strange creatures are filled with Kuldra’s rage and hatred, and will happily obliterate anything they encounter that isn’t the queen’s anima-infused flesh.

entries.name: Kalphite Guardian
entries.description:
The queen is all that matters. Protect the queen at all costs.

Those are the only thoughts within the guardian - the only drive, the only reason for living. All their energies, every cell in their bodies, fixated on that singular command.

Perhaps this is why they fight with such fervour. When your entire existence is reduced to a single focus, a single command, everything must get a little frustrating. The kalphite do not aspire, they do not dream. They have their place in the hive and they accept it completely.

Avisk was fascinated by this. As one of the Aughra, he was always obsessed with the mind and the potential within it. Whereas the other Aughra sought to escape the curse by transferring their consciousness to a single new body, Avisk dreamed of becoming the swarm. The kalphite fascinated him. He saw them as a single entity comprised of multiple individual moving parts and the potential of that structure became his new obsession.

When he stole some of the royal eggs from the Kharidian Desert’s hive, he was forced to battle several guardians who were protecting the nest. While they were no match for the power of a dragonkin, they nonetheless earned what passes for Avisk’s respect and he made sure to encourage his new queen to create as many guardians as possible so he could study them further.

entries.name: Kalphite Soldier
entries.description:
There are many people who argue that the military is “in their blood”, and aside from those who were part of secret, medical conspiracy theories, this is not a biological truth. While you can dedicate your life to the military machine, it is a choice, not a certainty.

For the kalphite soldier it is a literal reality. They have the military in their blood. Their very genetic structure is designed with the singular purpose – battle. They are pure warriors, with minds that think of nothing else other than the defence of the hive.

The queen creates the soldier with intent. When she lays her eggs, she releases certain chemicals harvested from ingested metal ore, in this case adamantite, and it bonds with the growing larvae, becoming something stronger. That is why the soldiers' shells are harder and their mandibles more dangerous, because they are forged in the embryonic sac to be killers.

Fun fact, friend: soldier eggs are revolting. This is true of all fried eggs, but the soldier ones taste particularly bad.
pages:
There are many people who argue that the military is “in their blood”, and aside from those who were part of secret, medical conspiracy theories, this is not a biological truth. While you can dedicate your life to the military machine, it is a choice, not a certainty.

For the kalphite soldier it is a literal reality. They have the military in their blood. Their very genetic structure is designed with the singular purpose – battle. They are pure warriors, with minds that think of nothing else other than the defence of the hive.

The queen creates the soldier with intent. When she lays her eggs, she releases certain chemicals harvested from ingested metal ore, in this case adamantite, and it bonds with the growing larvae, becoming something stronger. That is why the soldiers' shells are harder and their mandibles more dangerous, because they are forged in the embryonic sac to be killers.

Fun fact, friend: soldier eggs are revolting. This is true of all fried eggs, but the soldier ones taste particularly bad.

entries.name: Kalphite Worker
entries.description:
You could easily mistake the kalphite worker for a dumb bug, and for the most part you’d be right. But, that’s only because you are thinking with a human mind, one comprised of neurons and hard-wired for self-preservation. The kalphite mind is a different beast entirely.

Whilst they are individual entities, with their own complex set of neurons, axons and other complicated sciency sounding words, their consciousness is also a collection of pheromone trails, high-frequency chittering, and the strange sort of nonsense only insects understand.

The result is an individual that is connected to a great whole. Like an arm that can think by itself… which is a horrible thought - let’s not dwell on it.

The worker is the lowest caste of the kalphites, though it’s not really a status thing. Their entire existence is to gather food, harvest materials, and construct bigger and better hives for the queen’s delectation.

Unfortunately, that does not mean they won’t attack you if you threaten their hive. They will with as much vigour as they can manage. They care little for themselves: only the hive matters, and they will defend it with their lives.

entries.name: Mage of Zamorak
entries.description:
You have three masters. The first is Zamorak. The carpet we lay for him is red and frilled with chaos. 

The second is to me. As your archmage, my word is pact. Every conversation we have is signed with your soul. 

The third master is Dowdun Reach. It vibrates with our power. It fills with our works. Should anyone compromises it, friend or foe, I give you leave to destroy them.

entries.name: Revenant Knight
entries.description:
Hate is more than just an emotion: it’s a chain. It holds onto us, grasping our thoughts, reshaping our memories and driving our actions. Hate lasts longer than it should, and sometimes that hate lingers long after the hater has passed.

These revenants are echoes of those who foolishly attempted to battle Kuldra. In their dying moments, they were grasped by their hatred for the dragon queen and that hatred latched onto them and stitched them to the world.

Now, they cannot tell the difference between friend or foe, and are driven only by a hateful need to destroy every living thing in their path.

entries.name: Rotsworn Marauder
entries.description:
The Scalesworn were heroes. Only the strongest, most skilled and powerful marauders would be chosen by Xikotal to act as guardians of the dragons. They would guard the great beasts as they slept, standing strong against any force that might try to do them harm.

They were blessed with the mark of the dragon, granting them some of the power of their draconic masters.

These marks would be their undoing, when Imaru refused to stay dead. They became the first of the infected, inflicted with a terrible withering curse that would drag the souls of any they touched into Imaru’s hungry maw.

entries.name: Rotsworn Warrior
entries.description:
Foul creatures, warped by Imaru’s terrible hunger. They were once convicts and criminals, now cursed to serve as Imaru’s claws.

In the ages past those who had committed the gravest sins were given to Xikotal for conversion. He would breathe into them a new way of thinking, draconic magic creating a fog in their minds that erased their wicked past and offering them a newer future.

Some would be farmers. Others might live their lives in service of the village, even taking roles as priests or healers. The strongest would be given new identities, soldiers to stand as the dragon’s forces.

They were closest to Imaru when she died and as she drew in the souls around her they were the first to be afflicted. Withered and rotten, these tragic creatures remember nothing but a desire to infect and destroy.

entries.name: Rotsworn Zombie
entries.description:
What is worse than a shambling corpse that years to feast on all your precious fleshy parts? A shambling corpse that’s infected with a terrible rot that will tear your soul apart if you let it.

These zombies were once the most faithful followers of Imaru, her chosen servants. Each of them was branded with a special mark that would allow her to gift them a small semblance of her power. As humans they were healthier, lived longer and they thrived under her care.

Yet when Imaru’s hunger spread from the underworld, it was these unfortunates that fell first to this terrible affliction. Now they act as extensions to her hunger, sharing the rot with any unfortunate enough to cross their path.

entries.name: Skeleton Mage
entries.description:
Power is a corrupting force, it can turn reasonable people into monsters. Have you ever noticed how a seemingly reasonable person can go mad with power in the silliest of roles? That’s what happened to the necromancers of Fellhollow.

At first they were mages, of varying skill. Some were scholars of the arcane. Others priests in training. But each of them was obsessed with the mystery of the dead. They would learn secrets in strange places. In strange whispers on the wind, in ancient tomes stolen from the mainland. Some even learned of the necromantic arts in their dreams.

They had sought to command the dead, but now they have become them. Their powers turned only to spreading their affliction, the last vestiges of their souls trying to claim some semblance of meaning when there is none left for them to take.

entries.name: Skeleton Melee
entries.description:
Perhaps these were once guards, or soldiers. Wild Knights protecting the balance of the land. It is impossible to say who these creatures once were, because now all they are is merciless dead.

The tragic truth is that many of these people fought as hard as they could against the tide of undead. They stood at the gates to the village holding back the ravening horde. They walled themselves up in the keep, protecting their allies. They stood at the gate into Fellhollow and said “you will go no further!”. Yet, now, they are the monsters they fought so hard against.

entries.name: Skeleton Melee 2H
entries.description:
There were once warriors in Fellhollow that wielded great weapons with tremendous force. They were boastful, proud and dangerous people – yet they were beloved.

A tradition among these great hulking figures, was to seek out a far smaller person and act as their shield. They became the guardian angels of the bullied and the protectors of the abused. Wielding their great blades to fight against cruelty or unkindness, making the world happier by force.

Now that instinct is gone.

These skeletal creatures remember only that a sword must be swung, and that a blade needs to cut into flesh. They remember only that bone must be cleaved and that the living must be turned into the dead, swelling their armies with each swing of the blade.

entries.description:
By the time you’ve heard their creaking bones, it’s already too late. Despite their lack of sinew, sensory organs, or anything that should make them this dead, the skeletal archer is surprisingly deft.

In life they were scouts, hunters or Wild Knight archers, in death they’re simply something best avoided.

entries.name: Skeleton Wither Mage
entries.description:
Hatred guides these creatures, a vitriolic disgust at a world too cruel to function. They were once mages who had delved into the secrets of necromancy, desperate for power they were too foolish to wield.

The power within them has twisted and rotted, infected by Imaru’s vengeful rage. Their souls have been long hollowed out and now they are driven by a need to infect and corrupt, raising the dead in further service of vengeance.

entries.name: Sw Black Dragon Hatchling
entries.description: Like all dragon hatchlings, the black dragons are prone to violence from the moment they break through the shell. Indeed, some of them take shards of sharpened shells and use them to stab their siblings with it. Some survive, some don’t, but those that do are stronger and deadlier for it: something their mother, Kuldra, is very pleased with.

entries.name: Sw Green Dragon Hatchling
entries.description:
You would be forgiven for uttering the words “cute” at the sight of one of these baby dragons - a sentiment that lasts for the few picoseconds before they attempt to eat your face. Make no mistake, these are Kuldra’s broodlings, and they are filled with as much rage and hatred as she is. From the moment they hatch, these dragons are instilled with a violent need to destroy any that might breach Kuldra’s lair.

They may be cute, but you should cast aside that word in favour of a much better hyphenated one: self-preservation.

entries.name: Sw Kuldra
entries.description:
Kuldra’s tale is tragic really. An innocent child, raised by monsters: tormented, tortured, and forced to create legions of children who were all taken from her and then either weaponised or dissected for future study.

She found comfort in the gentle warmth of a lover’s embrace, only to see him taken from her by those same cruel parents.

Only one dragonkin ever showed her warmth, but their mind was distracted by a thousand different timestreams and they could never give Kuldra the love that she deserved. A lack of love is like a poison: it seeps into one’s soul and infects it with malice. You find yourself unable to believe that love could be real, and from it all the other positive emotions, such as charity, kindness, or hope.

Kuldra wasn’t born a monster, but she chose to become one and she was determined to be the worst monster she could be.

For centuries she has gorged herself on the anima of Ashenfall, building her own power so that she might turn the region’s Wellspring into a weapon that would decimate the rest of the world. Why? Because the rest of the world is happy, and she needs to see that stopped.

Now, she is dead - although her legacy will scar the world for generations to come. Hate breeds only hate, and Kuldra has had plenty of children.

entries.name: Sw Lesser Black Dragon
entries.description:
If you thought the red dragons were bad, you’re in for a rude awakening. The black dragon is a powerhouse of destruction. Every fibre of its being is bred to defend Kuldra and obliterate all threats that get remotely near.

Xikotal was the exception. He was a creature of empathy and he struggled with the violence that Kuldra bade him inflict on the world. When the first of the dragon wars ended, he nestled in with Imaru and the two of them tried to turn tragedy into something beautiful; a gentle utopia, where all life was sacred.

This disgusted Kuldra, and she has made sure that none of her black-scaled brood ever suffer the same weakness.

entries.name: Sw Red Dragon Hatchling
entries.description: Whereas the blue dragon hatchlings favour mischief, the red ones only care for blood. They revel in the tearing of flesh and the burning of skin. They unleash their flames on anything that moves, even their siblings who are slower to hatch from the eggs. Of course, for a dragon, this is the same thing as a warm hug, so it’s almost sweet if you think about it.

entries.name: Vault Guardian Melee
entries.description:
Weakness: Crush
Resistance: None
Immune: Poison, Bleed, Burning

It was the scientist, Lacrussa, who discovered the properties of rune essence, when properly prepared. It could be refined into a powder and then inscribed across stone and metal, to create complex magical effects. The vault guardians were one of her proudest achievements. Reflections of living beings, a power belonging only to the Elder Gods.

Though slow of wit, they made up for it with an excess of muscle. Their attacks were powerful and deadly, capable of toppling almost any threat. In the early days of their creation, thousands of years ago, there were no living beings that could have withstood their power.

During the dragon rebellion, it was Lacrussa’s greatest regret that she could not send the guardians beyond the magical enchantments of the vaults. The magic that animated them only worked within those walls, and dragons had no need of dragonkin secrets.

entries.name: Vault Guardian Ranged
entries.description:
Weakness: Crush
Resistance: None
Immune: Poison, Bleed, Burning

It was Avisk who raised the question of whether the vault guardians had souls. They weren’t intelligent and were useful for little more than manual labour and defence. Yet, they possessed a spark of creativity that Avisk argued was a sign of something more profound.

Lacrussa dismissed him; of course, they were tools, nothing more. Still, there were moments when even she doubted. When she found her sibling, the seer Viika, laughing with one, she questioned everything, especially since Viika had never laughed with her.

She studied them carefully for years afterwards, trying to figure out what Viika saw in them. Yet, there was never enough there to make her believe. Viika was, after all, prone to behaviour that Lacrussa could not understand. She loved her sibling dearly; breaking them free of the gilded prison they’d been raised in was what had made her an outcast to her people. Yet she knew that, deep down, she would never truly understand them.

The vault guardians were a tool and a mystery that would haunt her until her final moments.

entries.name: Zamorakian Acolyte
entries.description:
Are you sure you want to be an acolyte? It's long hours, thankless, and the Staff of Subjugation will be constantly whipping your shins. People don't usually volunteer for the position. 

You'd be doing yourself a favour. Even the life-expectancy of a demon summoners is longer than an acolyte. You might even make it into your thirties.

entries.name: Abyssal Demon
entries.description:
Weakness: Slash
Resistance: Air

The Abyssal Demon is a nightmare incarnated. Appearing suddenly out of nowhere and capable of tearing a man to shreds in a single swing.

No one knows how the demons arrived on Ashenfall, as they are not native to this plane. They dwell, as their name suggests, in the Abyss, the realm between worlds. They were cast out from their homeworld by the god Zamorak when he led the demon uprising on Infernus, and they have remained hateful ever since. Unable to strike at the god that banished them, they turn their fury on every living thing, existing for nothing more than to perpetuate suffering.

A necromancer and her Wild Knight ally were the first to encounter the beast. She had been investigating one of the dragonkin ruins, a vault buried deep into the soil, and when they broke the seal, the foul beast emerged.  At least, that’s what she claims. None have been able to venture deep enough into the vaults to confirm the truth of her words.

She and her companion vanished from the area soon after, their whereabouts unknown.

entries.name: Carnivorous Chinchompa
entries.description: Nature can often miss a punchline. Carnivorous chinchompas do not, in fact, like to chomp on chins. They aim a smidge lower and prefer jugulars.
pages: Nature can often miss a punchline. Carnivorous chinchompas do not, in fact, like to chomp on chins. They aim a smidge lower and prefer jugulars.

entries.name: Chinchompa
entries.description:
Weakness: Ranged
Resistance: Fire

The chinchompa is a nature’s bad joke, a weird branch of evolution that makes very little sense. The creature contains, within its body, a number of organs containing various chemicals and, when the creature feels its life is in danger, it combines these chemicals and immediately explodes.

It is assumed that these creatures must have some sort of communal sense of responsibility, martyring themselves for the sake of their herd. Yet chinchompas will happily explode when they’re the only one present, making it a somewhat pointless moment of self-sacrifice.

Most sane creatures avoid chinchompas where possible, for very obvious reasons.

They are, however, worryingly cute. A fact that has caused trouble for many Brynmoor children. It can be very upsetting when the family pet explodes, taking most of the house with it.

entries.name: Cow
entries.description:
Weakness: None
Resistance: None

To err is human, to moo bovine. So the adage goes. The cow is a poor, lamentable creature. Slaughtered in droves by fledgling adventurers seeking an easy start to their heroic lives, a cow’s life is brief and brutal. Those that survive, the swarms of merciless warriors, are ready to defend one another from their destroyers. 

They also taste delicious with roast potatoes, gravy and just a smidgeon of horseradish.

entries.name: Desert Goat
entries.description:
Goats should have thrived all over Ashenfall, and yet they seem to have migrated exclusively to the desert. It’s strange, because they aren’t really well suited to the region. They have thick fur, so overheat easily. Their little feet sink into the sand, and quicksand devours a great many of them every day. Yet, no matter how hard you explain to the goats of Ashenfall that they’d enjoy much happier lives elsewhere, the Umbral Sands is where they choose to stay.

There is no reason for this. Trust us,  we’ve asked.

Still, over the years, where they’ve failed to adapt physiologically, they’ve adapted mentally and socially. There are few creatures as stubborn as a goat. They are utterly unwilling to back down from a dangerous area, preferring to power through no matter what the cost.

There’s probably some life lesson or metaphor in there, but I’m not sure it’s one worth learning.

entries.name: Dragon Lesser Red
entries.description:
These red dragons are only lesser when compared to Fuzan, the strongest red dragon currently active in the region.  Despite their weaker stature to their draconic overlord, the lesser red dragons are still some of the deadliest creatures in the region.

Like Fuzan, the red dragons here are fuelled by a desire to destroy. The fire that rages in their bellies yearns to be unleashed upon anything that moves - or doesn’t move (as some poor cacti have discovered). They torment the locals, and delight in their suffering.

A few red dragons give themselves grandiose names, in an attempt to claim their own legacy. One dragon, known as The Radiant, torments the Manafem Moon Garou. For years now, The Radiant has destroyed caravans, eaten travellers and brought suffering to the camp, for no reason other than their capacity to do so.

Cruelty is a deeply embedded trait in the red dragons of Ashenfall, and they view mercy as a weakness to be exploited.

entries.description:
The unholy fusion of dragon and beast, creations of twisted dragonkin science. These creatures seem somehow resistant to the cursed nature of the region, but they refuse to sit still long enough for anyone to ask them why.

Not that they would answer, they have a wolf’s mind, not a dragons.

entries.name: Fellhollow Cow Zombie Withered
entries.description: Once gentle creatures, the rotridden cows were the few cows that hadn't been filled with an ancestral rage against humanity, for the slaughter of their kin back on the mainland. Unfortunately, this gentle nature made them carriers for the cursed hunger of Imaru and now these cows seek to damage the very souls of their victims, rotting them from within.

entries.name: Fellhollow Dragon Lesser Green
entries.description: Lesser green dragons are weaker than the generals, but that doesn’t make them easy to defeat. Their cruelty is almost as great as Velgar’s, but they fortunately lack the ambition and tactical thinking that would elevate their threat to greater heights.

entries.name: Fellhollow Nature Spirit
entries.description:
Nature spirits are part of a natural cycle, they are both the hunter and the hunted and death is as important a part of their essence as living is. In death, they rise again, like plants growing from the nutrients of fallen beasts, only to be hunted and slain again and again. 

On paper it’s a tragic existence, but this cycle of life and death is vital for the wellbeing of any ecosystem.

entries.name: Gnasher
entries.description: Of the two sisters, Fido and Gnasher, Gnasher is the menace. She will come crawling out from a magma swim and then shake the lava out. She gets the 'zoomies', crashing through bookcases in the library. Sometimes, she dreams about eviscerating foes in her sleep, gouging clumps out of the wall with her twitchy feet. She is, as Houndmaster Rexiton puts it, a little scamp.

entries.name: Gyr Falcon
entries.description:
Weakness: None
Resistance: None

The gyrfalcon is an agile predator. They silently dart through the air, seeking out small game to hunt. Giant rats are their favourite prey, though their flesh is stringy, they are comparatively large meals, compared to the kebbits and voles of the region.

Some Wild Knights would forge bonds with the falcons. They’re raise them from eggs and carefully train them to assist with scouting and hunting. This symbiotic relationship would allow both hunter and falcon to thrive in Ashenfall’s dangerous environment.

entries.name: Infernal Eel
entries.description:
In truth this is not a demonic fish, but rather the result of strange magic and infernal energies. The eel is naturally a magically attuned fish, some generate small thunderstorms within their flesh, others blend with shadows becoming almost entirely invisible. These eels, infused as they were with the abundant anima of Ashenfall, became changed by the energies of Downdun Reach’s demonic rites.

Fortunately, the transformation, while a little disconcerting, only really serves to give them a slightly spicy aftertaste.

entries.name: Kebbit
entries.description:
Weakness: None
Resistance: None

Kebbits are rodent-like creatures that are hunted for their pelts. The kebbits of Ashenmoor are more aggressive than most, though they remain at the bottom of the food chain.

They were first brought to the continent by Guthixian settlers, sometime in the first age, and have thrived in their absence. The kebbits of Brynmoor seem uniquely resistant to the effects of the Anima Twist phenomenon.

Legend says that following a kebbit under the full moon will lead you to your one true love. This has been definitively disproven by scholars from the Wizard’s Tower. However, their papers have been rebuked on the grounds that “they clearly have too much time on their hands”.

Coming from members of the Wizard’s Tower, that’s quite the statement.

entries.name: Kebbit Desert Devil
entries.description:
The kebbit of the sands have a strange name, one that implies a connection to the fiery realm of Infernus. This is, weirdly, not actually that far from the truth, because the desert devil is not native to the Umbral Sands, but rather the result of poor security at Dowdun Reach.

Originally, they were brought to the Reach as a rapidly reproducing source of meat. Sadly, the once peaceful and vegetarian chinchompas of the region discovered that their meat was delicious and consumed them voraciously, becoming the carnivorous chinchompas the region is currently overrun with.

A few of the kebbits escaped to the desert, where they survived by feeding on cacti and small insects that lived within the sands. Now, while their meat is no longer as delicious, they’ve adapted to survive in the desert and can be found running round the sands without a care in the world.

entries.name: Lesser Blue Dragon
entries.description:
Lacrussa, the creator of the lesser blue dragons, saw life in a different way to you or I. While we might approach a new creature with wariness or curiousity, Lacrussa would approach it with an intellectual hunger. The creature would be mentally dissected for its physical suitability, it's cognitive capacity, or its magical resonance. She would turn it in her mind, this way and that, determining how it might factor into her experiments. 

Then came dissections of a more physical nature. She would cut and dice and drain. She was an expert in biological reaction, forcing revulsion and attraction out of living matter. She would take the results of those combinations and cycle them through the same experiments. Cut and dice and drain. 

Knowing that experimentation begat experimentation, it's hard to pinpoint the materials that gave us the lesser blue dragon. If there is one certainty, it is that Lacrussa herself is part of them.

There are indications that, around the time that the blue dragons moved to Dowdun, Lacrussa was experimenting with lightning. It is possible that Lacrussa found a means to bottle it in a lesser blue dragon.

entries.description: Lurch tends to sleep most of the day. It's her metabolism that does the hard work, producing wind that will empty an entire barracks. Considering she will accidentally ignite that flatulence, she's often left to sleep on her own.

entries.name: Magpie
entries.description:
Weakness: None
Resistance: None

One for sorrow, two for joy, yet these little tricksters are rarely found in pairs. The magpie is well known as the thief of the bird family, delighting in stealing objects that glitter. It is said that if you can find a magpie’s nest, it will be full of tiny treasures. The results of testing this theory are often underwhelming.

A member of the corvid family, the magpie pretends to have no affiliation with the more sinister members of the genus.

The magpie’s feathers are much prized by fletchers due to their sleek and elegant design.

entries.name: Pristine Salmon
entries.description: The life of a salmon is one of great journey and strife. They swim back over great distances, leaping upstream in search of a cementing their legacy. It is tragic then, perhaps, that such journeys become the happy lunchtimes of bears and other animals.

entries.name: Pristine Sardine
entries.description:
There is a popular game among children, where they hide themselves around the house and then other children join them once their hiding place has been discovered. It was a game clearly invented by very tired parents, who wanted to make sure their kids were well behaved and contained in a well-known location. After all, where else can you fit seventeen children if not for the wardrobe?

Sadly for Gielinor’s fisherfolk, the creature with the namesake of said children’s game, do not possess the same desire to make their captor’s life easier. Fortunately, however, they are numerous enough that one need not worry themselves too much about the difficulty of catching them.

There is little exciting one can say about trout, they have few advocates and fewer fans. Yet, they do taste delicious with a little lemon and a few herbs, so perhaps we should thank them for not being awful.

One trout was awful. A villain. A monster who rose from the depths to bring terror to us all.

Nah, just kidding – they’re trout… I got nothing.

Resistance: None

Ashenfall’s sheep are wilder than most, running free through the woodlands without a care in the world. Their fleeces are thicker and sturdier than their domesticated counterparts, and there’s barely any danger that one of them might be two penguins in disguise. It happens.

entries.name: Terrorbird
entries.description:
Weakness: Stab
Resistance: Air

The terrorbird lives up to its name with both it’s violent tendencies and the nightmarish cries it makes in the shadows. There are few who can look into the eyes of a terrorbird and not regret every decision in their lives, leading to this moment.

Early garou tried to tame the creatures, but the terrorbird’s wild nature prevented them from accepting the yoke of domestication. Instead, they turned on their would-be masters, leading to an even the garou would forever refer to as “the night of green feathers”.

Best taken out from range, the terrorbird makes itself known by it’s distinctive war-warble, that strikes fear into the heart of any sane creature.

entries.name: Vulture
entries.description:
The poor vulture gets a bad rap. We see them as omens of death; scavengers circling around us, waiting for us to die. This image is fair, but ask yourself why they do this and what good it brings the world.

Would you rather the desert was filled with the rotting corpses of those who have succumbed to the Scorch? Or, is it not better to find picked-clean skeletons, in which disease and corruption cannot thrive?

Countless lives may be saved by a vulture’s feeding habits, but you never think about that, do you?

entries.name: Wolf
entries.description:
Weakness: Fire
Resistance: None

The wolves of Ashenfall are dangerous creatures. Their anima-infused muscles make them faster. Their razor-sharp teeth would pierce the armour of the Brynmoor villagers. It would be the job of the Wild Knights to hunt them down and prevent them from attacking the human settlements.

They did this by culling the leaders of the packs, as well as to lure larger groups away from human settlements, with fresh deer kills.

One year, an alpha wolf, known as Shatterfang, ignored the lures and followed his nose to Bramblemead. The resulting confrontation was an unmistakable bloodbath, with villagers locking themselves in their homes, praying to Guthix that the wolves wouldn’t break through the door.

The Wild Knights sent in their hunters, but Shatterfang was as clever as he was cruel. He used the urban structures against the hunters, avoiding their arrows and escaping their wrath. He was finally felled when an unlikely ally used dark magic to lock the wolf’s bones in place, while her companion struck from the shadows with blades forged from the wolf’s kin.   

The villagers offered any reward to their saviours. Money, weapons, gems, yet the pair asked only for Shatterfang’s skull in return.

entries.name: Wolf Alpha
entries.description:
Weakness: Fire
Resistance: None

Dire wolves are the apex of their species. They have absorbed more of the ambient anima of the region, making them stronger and more powerful than their smaller kin. Their attacks rend the flesh, leaving lasting damage that their foes might never recover from.

They lead their packs with absolute authority, refuting any challenges with only a glance.

The Wild Knights respected the dire wolves, preferring not to kill them if there was any other choice. They believed that if the dire wolves could be deterred from a particular course of action, the other wolves would follow. Invariably this was true, but there were always exceptions.

There are legends of a silver wolf among the garou.  Some of them whisper that it is a goddess reincarnated. That she is rebuilding her power, to challenge their new High Queen again.

entries.name: Irit
entries.description:
It is unsurprising that irit grows in Fellhollow, considering it has such a close association with the dead. Whereas normal irit grows around graveyards and near the temples of death deities, the irit in Fellhollow grows everywhere.

Yet, unlike its leafier version, the irit here is twisted and sharp. It is formed of thorny roots that writhe out of the ground and must be cut down to access the herb beneath. After all, the dead in Fellhollow refuse to stay buried without a fight, why wouldn’t the irit react the same?

They're little Big Bangs in a seed format, distributing mass and foliage from a dense centre.

They seem strange without faces, don’t they?

When carved it acts as a ward against dangerous spirits and when mixed with spices and added to warm drinks, it acts as a lure for ex-girlfriends, distracting them as it gives you time to escape.

entries.name: Ruby Vine
entries.description:
This offshoot of the wild jade vine has been mutated by the power of the Lens and the terrible Scorching sun. Whereas most vines require water, the ruby vine requires heat. Their chlorophyl has been replaced with embers and their stalks and stems burn internally, creating an incinerator that they use to ignite their prey.

Fuzan thinks they’re pretty, and makes sure to cultivate them all over the desert.

entries.name: Seeds Cabbage
entries.description:
Hail Brassica Prime, lord of deliciousness and nutrition! Within these tiny seeds rest all the power of creation, ready to burst forth into spherical orbs of crisp deliciousness.

Guthix once encountered Brassica Prime when he wandered the moors of Ashenfall. On a strange outcrop, beneath a waterfall that reflected the silver moonlight, he spied a cabbage so large and so full of nutrition that he was briefly stunned at its magnificence.

When the cabbage spoke, the god of balance found himself quite at a loss. According to the cabbage, he was the lord of all vegetables, and keeper of the ancient secrets of a balanced diet, seeing some small kinship in Guthix’s search for harmony. They spoke long and strange conversations, deep into the night, about the nature of magic, divinity and, of course, food.

Brassica’s stories changed every night. Each moonrise offered a new excuse for his divinity, and new lessons on how he had supposedly shaped creation itself, by mixing together the base vitamins needed for the universe to thrive.

Mad, perhaps, or just composed of an alien way of thinking, Guthix took some small comfort in his strange new friend. As such, he made a point of having his druids sow cabbage seeds in every field, and around all his settlements, so that Brassica might be honoured in some small way.

entries.description:
Sometimes you just want to fill your garden with deadly berries. This was certainly true of Agnes DeWithlington-Smithe, a self-proclaimed “witch” with zero magical talent. She delighted in filling her garden with strange and dangerous herbs and flowers. The more poisonous, the better.

Locals would claim that she was a retired assassin, trying to hone her craft. In truth she just found something about the plants that she admired, and, ultimately, she thought they were pretty.

entries.description:
Sometimes you just want a way to make everyone around you cry. Onions have always served this purpose, and I often bring one with me to slice into at social gatherings when I feel everyone is being just a little too happy.

With these seeds, you can avoid scavenging for onions across the dangerous plains and instead produce a steady supply with them to torment your friends and family. Or you could eat them, I guess, if you’re weird.

entries.name: Seeds Potato
entries.description:
Know this secret, child, the potato is a source to foods both delicious and dangerous. They can be baked, roasted over the fire to create a delicious fluffy centre encased within a crisp and tasty core. Or they can be combined with butter and milk to craft a small mountain of creamy extravagance that can serve both as meal and sculpture tool.

These seeds, small and unremarkable, can be transformed into meals of such exquisite flavour, that they can end wars. Or, as was the case of the feud between the Sherrydoe and Nab families, start one -- that ended up in a house burning to the ground, three failed marriages and a cow being briefly elected mayor. It’s best not to ask.

entries.name: Wild Jade Vine Poison
entries.description:
Weakness: Fire
Resistance: None
Immune: Poison

The jade vine is an unusual plant, that likes to attack anyone that gets too close. With a maw full of thorns and a stem full of hatred, the jade vine has been the bane of many a hunter.

They aren’t actually native to Ashenfall, at least not originally. They were brought to the continent by the druid Hokistix, who had a terrible taste in houseplants. He was forced to live on the edge of the village, until he disappeared.

It’s not really a mystery as to where he vanished to, but suffice to say his plants were very well fed.

entries.description: Legends say that willow trees house the weeping spirits of those who died in the woods. Anywhere but Fellhollow this would be nonsense, but in a land so heavily infused with the dead, you can’t rule it out.

entries.name: Willow Tree Seed
entries.description: Did you know that a willow seed is called a 'salix', and looks a bit like the stuffing out of a toy bear? Now, we appreciate that doesn't reconcile with the icon we have chosen for the willow seed, but we would have got complaints that 'the willow seed icon looks like the stuffing from a toy bear'. Honestly, there was no good option here. If you're a botanist, close your eyes and imagine the fluff.

entries.name: Yew Sapling
entries.description: A little version of one of the only pieces of vegetation to bloom in the desert. They say that yew trees come into the world full of innocence and wonder, but this is a lie. They come into the world full of malice and mischief, if you turn your back on them for too long...well... nothing will happen, because they're trees, but they will say horrible things about you behind your back.

entries.name: Yew Tree
entries.description:
Towering over the oasis, the yew tree might seem a strange addition to the desert sands, yet it has a deep-rooted place in the lore of the region. 

Unfortunately, the trees are very secretive and delight in upsetting lorehounds, so they won’t share what that secret is. 

Just another excuse to cut them down, really.

entries.name: Avantoe
entries.description: Everything about the avantoe is quickfire. It grows quickly, blooms fast, and is a superb catalyst, reacting quickly in potion-making. It's a plant in a rush, eager to germinate and get the next avantoe on its way. Meanwhile, I can spend an hour trying to work out what to eat today, and can stare at an empty space where a journal should be for even longer.

entries.name: Blurite Deposit
entries.description: A rock containing the most blue ore you've ever seen.
pages: A rock containing the most blue ore you've ever seen.

entries.name: Clay Deposit
entries.description: Clay can be found in deposits around Ashenfall and can be recovered with just a few pickaxe swings. It is said that the Elder God created the universe out of clay, albeit of a more interesting vintage, and the unwanted remains hurled into the abyss. The truth of this claim is hard to establish as the Elder Gods are rarely prone to a friendly chat. Not least because, were you to hear them speak, your head would explode. This makes conversation tricky.

entries.name: Copper Deposit
entries.description: On its own copper is useful but not great for weapons or armour and must be combined with tin to create the sturdier bronze.

entries.name: Gold Deposit
entries.description: Few metals are as beloved as gold. Its glistening nature has attracted countless pursuers, and those who find a viable vein need never work again. Sadly, on Ashenfall, the economy is not quite so well established and gold is merely another crafting component. Still, remember where you found it, because once all this dragon malarky is dealt with you might make a tidy sum selling the location to prospectors.

entries.name: Granite Boulder
entries.description: These great lumps of rock are sturdier than normal stone and are excellent materials for construction.
pages: These great lumps of rock are sturdier than normal stone and are excellent materials for construction.

entries.name: Iron Deposit
entries.description: Do you know the riddle of iron? No, me neither, asking for a friend. Iron is a durable metal, capable of creating some of the strongest arms and armour available.
pages: Do you know the riddle of iron? No, me neither, asking for a friend. Iron is a durable metal, capable of creating some of the strongest arms and armour available.

entries.name: Limestone Rock
entries.description:
If you like the look of this rock, imagine what it could like in your house. Carve off a few chunks with your pickaxe and save up for a fetching limestone interior. The white will complement your eyes.

You might be surprised to learn that Vannaka refuses to use limestone in any capacity. Someone told him that you can contract lime's disease from it, a rash that pains the joints and nerves. "Can't be spoiling these reflexes", he'd say, swinging an axe.

Don't try to correct the man - it's not worth it.

entries.name: Mithril Deposit
entries.description:
Doric is peeved that mithril is predominantly in Zamorakian territory. Dwarves feel a kinship to the ore: it means a little more to them than the other metals. In his view, Zamorakians don't deserve it.

He won't admit it if you confront him, but it's a big reason that you can find him in Dowdun Reach. One eye on the mithril. If he had it his way, he'd be laying minecart tracks all the way from Dowdun Reach to Temple Woods. Then he'd have to fight the urge to make mithril platebodies until the end of his days.

entries.name: Rune Essence Geyser
entries.description:
This strange material absorbs magical energy, causing it to defy gravity, among other things. It is best known for the creation of runes, powerful little stones that can be used to cast spells. A pickaxe is needed to harvest the essence. 

The floating essence rocks can be knocked out of orbit, with a little effort, making them easier to mine.

entries.description: Large sandstone deposits can be mined for this useful crafting material.

entries.name: Silver Deposit
entries.description: They say that silver is touched by the moon, explaining why the lycanthropes are so affected by it. Silver makes for an exceptionally good magical conductor, making it highly prized by enchanters everywhere.

entries.name: Stone Boulder
entries.description: Large boulders can be found just about anywhere. With even the most basic pickaxe they can be reduced to little more than pebbles, which are much more useful for crafting. It is perhaps humbling to see theses centuries old stones reduced to nothing.

entries.name: Swamp Tar
entries.description: Once this tar was some living creature, perhaps and ancient dragon or other colossal beast. Time and pressure refined it down into this sticky substance that can be used for a variety of crafting purposes.
pages: Once this tar was some living creature, perhaps and ancient dragon or other colossal beast. Time and pressure refined it down into this sticky substance that can be used for a variety of crafting purposes.

entries.name: Tin Deposit
entries.description: Tin and copper are the classic double act, combining their essence to make the superior bronze.
pages: Tin and copper are the classic double act, combining their essence to make the superior bronze.

entries.name: Adamant Bolt
entries.description:
Sturdy bolts of one of the most durable metals. Capable of piercing most armours with relative ease.

Have you considered what else those metal bars could be used for? You could create tools that would grow plants in these desolate lands. You could craft beautiful sculptures to bring joy to all who see them.

But, no, you went with murder spikes instead.

Though there are ruddy great dragons around the place, so I suppose it’s a fair plan.

entries.name: Astral Rune
entries.description: Astral runes borrow resonance from the stars, that silent hum when looking up at the night sky. They embody the power of distance and displacement, action from inaction, movement in the dark. Astral runes are used primarily in spells designed to summon an object to the caster’s location, making it a very popular rune with the lazier magicians.

entries.name: Bone Bolt
entries.description: Special bolts whittled from bones, whilst only of use for a very specific crossbow, these bolts pack a surprising amount of punch.

entries.name: Bronze Arrow
entries.description:
Bronze arrows offer greater armour piercing than their non-metallic counterparts. Copper and tin were relatively uncommon in Brynmoor, so using the resources on arrows seemed like a waste of money. One faction of bandits delighted in this premise; their leader, a man known as the Auburn Ocelot—for reasons he would never explain—took great amusement in their use. 

The Auburn Ocelot would laugh as his bandits hurled expensive arrows at the villagers, pilfering coins worth far less than the ammunition used to corral them. To him, it wasn’t about the money but the look of confused terror on their faces and the knowledge that no one could stop him. 

He was above it all. Better than everyone. 

It was a rat that killed him. Not even a giant one. Just a tiny creature carrying a virulent plague. Money could not save him, no matter how much he flaunted it. He was cremated, and his ashes buried in the middle of nowhere so that no one might risk catching the infection that cost his life. 

Now, he’s almost completely forgotten.

entries.name: Bronze Barbed Arrow
entries.description:
The barbed bronze arrow was the ammunition of choice for the hunting party of Lord Gawurin, the regent of Ashenfall. He and his hunting party would head out into the woods alongside a small contingent of White Knight bodyguards. The lord would hunt deer, boars and other game there, but he wasn’t the most accurate shot. 

This arrow was designed for bloodletting, meaning he only needed any hit to begin the prey’s downfall. A single strike would start them bleeding, slowing them down and making them easier to hunt. The hunt outcome was all but inevitable. Poor sport, some would whisper, but the lord cared only for the end result. 

It’s perhaps fitting, then, that Lord Gawurin would be hunted with his own arrows on the night of Falling Embers.

entries.name: Bronze Bolt
entries.description:
Not a lot can be said about small spears of metal to be launched at high speeds into your opponent. They do exactly what you think they’ll do to the target, and it’s rarely pretty.

Guards would buy crossbow bolts in bulk from the village blacksmiths, giving him a steady income. This sadly had the side effect of making the village blacksmith the number one most regularly broken into location.

entries.name: Earth Rune
entries.description: Imbued with the harmony of soil and dirt, the earth rune stands firm in a world of mercurial change. Predominantly used to manipulate or control natural elements associated with, soil and rock, it can also be used to reference the permanence of things.

entries.name: Enchanted Adamant Bolt
entries.description:
Adamant is a special metal, responding well to magic and allowing it to be shaped into durable and deadly forms. Adamant bolts are the bane of many creatures, their sharpness and their hardiness lets them pierce through almost any defence.

Yet, what if you didn’t stop the magic in the crafting process? What if you added more and more, creating bolts enchanted with murderous wrath? The answer to that is in these enchanted bolts, that sap your life in order to deal greater damage to your foe.

Sacrifice for vengeance, the gods would approve. 

Except Guthix, but his opinion is somewhat moot these days.

entries.name: Enchanted Blurite Bolt
entries.description:
No one is entirely sure who thought to enchant blurite crossbow bolts in Brynmoor. The earliest references talk about Ignatius Wormwood, a failed apprentice wizard with too much time on his hands.

The story goes that he was challenged by one of the Knights to a duel, over some spat about a maiden or other. Evidently Ignatius may have been a failure in his robes, but worryingly successful out of them, if you get my gist.

Now, the knight was a large and imposing man -- referred to by his compatriots as the immovable boulder -- and angry as he was, he had no intention of killing Ignatius, so he gave him a simple challenge instead. If Ignatius could knock him down, he’d win the duel, otherwise the Knight would claim victory and see Ignatius punished for his mischiefs.

When Ignatius pulled the crossbow from his robes, the knight was concerned but knew that his armour and shield could stand against them. Yet, when the bolt impacted the knight’s pristine iron armour, he found himself hurled to the floor and the wind knocked out of him.

Gracious in defeat the knight let Ignatius go, only for the wizard to wander into the next person he had wronged.

entries.name: Enchanted Bronze Bolt
entries.description:
Magic was never enough. Oh, sure, you could change bones into delicious peaches, you could summon water out of thin air, you could call down fire upon your foes and laugh as their flesh turns to ash (if you’re that way inclined). Yet, even so, it was never enough. There was always more death to deal, more damage to inflict, more pain to spread and the priests of Brynmoor wanted more of it.

They wanted to see the garou crushed. Wanted to see them begging as the last of their pups expired beneath Saradomin’s purifying flame. So, they commissioned the wizards and alchemists to find new and innovative ways to summon suffering.

Crossbow bolts proved to be an interesting revelation. By affixing gemstones to the tips of these weapons, not only could they inflict deadly wounds on their enemies, but they could also inflict debilitating pain so powerful that the opponent would be stunned, making the next attack much easier.

The priests were very happy with this discovery. The so called “heretics” within Brynmoor were less so.

entries.name: Enchanted Iron Bolt
entries.description:
Stone remembers, wood forgets, iron holds a grudge. So goes the Imcamdo saying. A reference to how much stronger metal weapons were than wood and stone. Still, with magic, this adage can become painfully true.

The first enchanted iron bolts on Ashenfall were crafted by Lina Hesperian, one of the Amalgamated. She had hair that flowered like a waterfall down her spine. Her eyes were crystalline lakes, sparkling in the light, and her smile was as refreshing as any spring. She enchanted the bolts so that they might carry the gift of water, washing away infection for a clean and gentle kill. She made them for the hunters, so that they might claim their quarries with as little suffering as possible.

She met the end that far too many Amalgamated suffered. Alone, frightened, in the cold and the dark of an alley, her blood seeping from the knife wound in her chest. As she gave her last breath, she cursed the world for it’s cruelty, and the iron listened.

Now, each enchanted iron bolt taps into that grudge, inflicting a reminder of her suffering on any that feel the bolt’s sting.

entries.description: Goodness, you must really want to kill someone. As if punching through their armour with a crossbow bolt wasn't enough, you want to magically scupper them too. Remind me not to get on your bad side.

entries.name: Fang Arrow
entries.description:
For a short time, a necromancer arrived on Ashenfall. She had found her way here by boat, fleeing pirates who wanted revenge for her misdeeds. Her skills were limited; she could not raise undead legions, but she had a knack for controlling simple fangs and bones. 

She fled into the forests – pirates having found Ashenfall and hunting her down –  where she would unleash fang arrows against her foes in the hope of stopping their chase. It didn’t work. Broken, lost and without hope, she prepared herself for death. 

But death never came for her. 

Instead, a Wild Knight, who wore a mask made from the skull of a wolf, rescued her. He pushed back her assailants and brought her to safety. Their fellowship after that was unbreakable, though no bond of romance flowed between them. She made the arrows, he fired the bow, and together, they feasted on their victories and kept the woods safe from unwanted intrusion. 

Even now, there are signs of their friendship. Hidden across the forest, miniature carvings of a wolf skull and a bat can be found in places that meant something to them.

entries.name: Fire Rune
entries.description:
Guthix created runes in the first age, here on Ashenfall. He found a way of capturing the ambient wild anima, of the continent, in the floating rune essence around the region. He would then give these runes to his druids, teaching them the fundamentals of magic.

Fire runes contain enough magical fire to light a campfire. Battlemages prize them for the ability to lob that small fire at an enemy instead. Either way, they’re a very handy resource.

entries.name: Iron Bolt
entries.description:
One sad part of human nature is that they will constantly strive to craft deadlier and deadlier weapons. Iron crossbow bolts were harder than their bronze counterpart, capable of penetrating the toughest garou armour.

Obrimex, of the garou, once tried to replicate these weapons. He crafted little sharpened tubes of iron that he felt would match their power. Alas, the garou hadn’t yet crafted crossbow technology, and throwing these little metal darts largely proved to be irritating rather than dangerous.

entries.name: Iron Fire Arrow
entries.description:
Rasthin was the master of fire. It was the gift she had stolen from the “soul of the world” as she called it. She could use the inner flame to inspire confidence or rouse people into a great fervour. The fire could reveal secrets, forcing truth from those who stood before her. But, more practical than all of that was one simple truth, that fire could burn.

There were many a dragon that tried to battle Rasthin directly, believing their dragonfire could destroy her. Their bones litter Ashenfall. It was only Queen Kuldra herself who could challenge the dragonkin, and theirs was a battle that left scars in the lands for centuries.

These arrows borrow a piece of Rasthin’s power. Able to inspire only by the fear they kindle in the wielder’s enemies. Yet, kindle they do, for those who face these flames will surely feel echoes of the fury wrought by the dragonkin lord of fire.

entries.name: Law Rune
entries.description: The law rune is an odd sort of power, it embodies not some elemental force, but instead it represents the rigidity of reality. The rules in which all of creation operates, are conceptually encapsulated within this small stone. Gravity, movement, location, all these things are bound within, and when the rune is used in magic, these rules may be altered for a time. entries.description: Mithril is an attractive metal, shimmering and chromatic. If you ever get peppered with mithril arrows, you can look down and admire the constellation on your chest.

entries.description: Demons are hardy creatures. The Black Knights had a habit of calling them 'Rackers', as they'd often require a whole bolt rack to bring down.

entries.name: Nature Rune
entries.description: Contrary to popular belief, the nature rune does not solely govern plants, roots and the natural world. That is only part of its design. Instead, nature is about the connection of things, threading together the way things could be, rewriting them to a state more desirable. Favoured by wizard’s for their ability to adjust the flow of time to an entity, dragging it back to a point when it was in a more preferable state.

entries.name: Poisoned Bronze Arrow
entries.description:
The Wild Knights were not above poison, any edge in a battle was worth having. Poison meant that you could take down a dangerous beast, even if your initial shot wasn’t a mortal one.

The druids among the order felt little concern over its use either, after all nature is filled with wielders of poison and so the Wild Knight archers were simply emulating nature’s tools.

entries.name: Poisoned Iron Arrow
entries.description:
Lougrim abhorred the use of poison on arrows, she felt it cheapened the hunt. The mages could wield it in their spells, but a hunter should produce smooth, quick kills, creating as little suffering as possible.

Most garou, in turn, would at first refuse to use poisons on their arrows. They followed her teachings, and they hunted swiftly and cleanly. After Lougrim’s fall it became clear just how foolish it was to seek such a merciful path, their new High Queen had made it clear that they should use all tools at their disposal.

entries.name: Poisoned Steel Arrow
entries.description:
What’s better than sharpened pieces of wood with super strong metal made into even sharper points, firing at your enemies with unreasonable speed? Why, the very same thing, but coated with a deadly toxic poison!

I’d say your enemies complain about you doing this, but they’re too dead to fill in the forms. So you’re good.

entries.name: Steel Arrow
entries.description:
Traditional wisdom says that to kill a zombie, you must destroy the brain. This is disappointingly untrue in Fellhollow, the animating force of Imaru’s hunger needs no thought to drive it forward.

No, a far better plan is to destroy the bones and muscles with sharp metal-tipped spikes launched at the creatures with as much force as you can manage. Steel arrows perform this task very nicely.

Steel arrows are nasty enough, but covering them in deadly barbs that will rend the flesh and empty the liquid lifeforce of a person onto the forest floor? That’s just overkill.

entries.name: Steel Bolt
entries.description:
Sharpened bolts of steel projected at great speed is a formula for your target to have a very bad day.

Although it was cheaper and quicker to forgo the coal and craft iron bolts, the relentless nature of the undead hordes required a more practical approach. Steel was stronger than iron, and was more likely to put the ravenous undead back in the dirt where they belonged, making it very popular in the last few years of Fellhollow’s resistance.

entries.name: Water Rune
entries.description: Water is a strange thing, required by all living things, yet capable of ending civilisations. Rain is vital to the survival of a kingdom, yet its citizens lament the grey clouds forming overhead. Mages understand that water is a special sort of power, capable of being shaped in a multitude of ways. Water runes embody this fluidity of concept, finding use in many different types of spell.

entries.name: Wooden Arrow
entries.description:
Druids dislike violence but understand its place. The natural world is full of blood, murder and death. The strong consume the weak. Predator against prey. This they understand, though they seldom like it. When they must resort to violence, they choose the simple approach. Man’s strength comes not from their muscles but from their creativity and ingenuity. Just as a wolf has claws, a hunter has a bow. 

When a bow must be drawn, the druids prefer arrows made of simple wood. Gathered twigs and branches, whittled down to sharp points. They see it as the forest giving them the blessing to go on the hunt. Traditionally, feathers are gathered from around the forest floor, taken when dropped or from a bird’s moulting. This keeps the number of arrows low, forcing a hunter to be accurate and precise, lest they run out of chances. 

Thus, death is swift at the hands of a bow, and balance isn’t damaged. This the druids preached to the villagers.

entries.name: Adventurer's Leggings
entries.description:
You brought simple cloth trousers with you from the mainland. They barely qualify as armour, but they’re better than no armour at all. 

These clothes have seen you across the oceans, keeping you warm in the cold sea breeze. Now starched with sea salt and weathered by labouring away on the ship deck, these clothes are a testament to how far you’ve come. This is the furthest you’ve ever been from home, and perhaps it’s a chance to craft a new one.

entries.name: Adventurer's Tunic
entries.description:
A simple tunic brought with you from the mainland. It barely classes as armour, but it’s better than no armour at all. 

When you joined the expedition, you had nothing but the clothes on your back. All your worldly belongings were lost, and all your gold drained away. Debt collectors would appear out of the shadows, swarming toward you like rats seeking cheese. What choice did you have but to leave? 

The expedition offered you a chance away from all your troubles. An opportunity to escape the cruel hand that fate has dealt you. These clothes once represented everything you ever lost, but now they represent the threadbare start of a new beginning.
