entries.name: Apprentice Robe
entries.description:
Prized for its lightweight and nimble nature, linen armour finds favour among apprentice wizards and those who value agility. Composed of layered cloth, it forms a rudimentary defence capable of withstanding minor assaults. 

At first, acolytes would spend time at the wizard’s tower to learn about the magic the armour would protect the wearer against. It was common for young priestly acolytes to become enamoured with the mysterious life of the apprentice wizards. They would see them hurling spells with skill and panache, making their lives of quiet contemplation seem awfully dull in response. Many young acolytes would make linen armour for themselves, practising spellcasting in secret.

The priests soon discovered their numbers dwindling, while the wizard’s guild gained more members. So, the decree was given that robes were to be crafted in silent contemplation, far away from those who would later wear them. This would keep fewer acolytes from being lured away, but the defensive prowess of the armour diminished in return.

The high priests considered this a reasonable exchange.

entries.name: Ava's Accumulator
entries.description:
Ava is the apprentice to Dr Oddenstein, an eccentric scientist who lives in Draynor Manor, and a skilled inventor in her own right. She whiles away her limited free time by studying the lesser-known field of necroballistics, and creating strange and wonderful gizmos to further her studies. 

Perhaps her proudest achievement, is the invention of the attractor. By harnessing the energies of an undead chicken to the harmonic frequencies of a common bar magnet, her device can snatch grounded projectiles and bring them back to the quiver before they can be lost. This money saving experiment is not only great for hunters, but for anyone looking for an excuse to fill their enemies full of sharp sticks of wood. 

Always the generous sort, but one with little head for marketing, Ava has decided to pass on her genius invention to others. Rather than publishing a paper, or passing the methodology onto the Varrock library, she has instead written the instructions in a bottle and sent it adrift in the ocean for anyone to find. Fate, she believes, will draw it to where it is meant to go. Like magnets, probably.

entries.name: Bag Of Noggin
entries.description:
Noggin was never the best looker in Ashenfall, or so others claimed. He lived his life ashamed of his appearance and wore a sad-looking sack across his face so that none would fall ill from his hideous features.

He found himself an outcast. Mocked and jeered at by the locals of Bramblemead, so he hid himself away in the forests, but kept wearing the sack.

One day, while he was standing in a field scaring birds away, just for the fun, he met a lost villager who had wandered too far. She was frightened, at first, and fearful of the strange figure with a face of itchy cloth, but as they talked and laughed together that fear fell away.

In time, they would grow closer with one another. Developing feelings that Noggin never believed he would feel. On the day they were to be wed, Noggin finally let her see the face beneath the sackcloth, but there was no face to be found.

Instead, when the sack was removed, Noggin’s clothes went limp and fell to the floor in a pile and the woman screamed as the silence engulfed her.

Now Noggin’s face appears on scarecrows and training dummy’s all across Ashenfall, and on cold, dark nights, you could swear they are watching.

entries.name: Black Adventurer's Cape
entries.description:
Capes are stylish and protect against the weather. They can be elaborate symbols of stature, or simple cloth to act as a ward against the cold. This cape is the latter.

Simple, elegant, and functional. Worn by adventurers and explorers across Gielinor’s mainland and beyond.

After the dragon attack, there are few of these capes worn on Ashenfall. The rest sink beneath the ocean waves, are torn to pieces on the cliff rocks, or have long since burned to ash beneath draconic hate.

entries.name: Bloodblight Cape
entries.description:
The Bloodblight swamp was once a pleasant place. Golden fields of wheat, rustling in the breeze. Life here was simple yet fulfilling.

Until Velgar took it all away.

He fought the mighty god of war, Bandos, and he should have lost. Dragons are powerful, and Velgar is stronger than most, but even in his most arrogant days he was no match for a god.

Yet, arrogance is not a mortal taint and the war god reeked of it. Bandos cast aside his wards. He refused to don his armour. The god pressed into the lair of the great dragon, and tried to wrestle him to the grave.

He nearly succeeded. Bandos wrapped his arms around the dragon’s serpentine neck and dug his fingernails beneath the scales. Velgar, in his writhing fury, called down a poison-filled rock from the heavens and cast it at Bandos, striking him in the temple. As the god reeled, he released Velgar, allowing the dragon to breathe a jet of anima-infused poison, at the unsteady god. Still wavering from the blow, Bandos breathed in the toxins and felt weakness for the first time in centuries.

A smart tactician, Bandos retreated. Better to face the shame of retreat, than risk the oblivion of death.

In his jubilant rage, Velgar spilled his blood on the once fertile plains, corrupting them with his hate-filled poison. The fields wilted. The crops blackened and then collapsed into venom.

This cloak, is reminder of that blighted day.

entries.name: Body Wild Archer
entries.description:
The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt, putting even the garou to shame.

Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. They would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning.

Archers of the Wild Knights were quick, silent and deadly. A joke their more melee focused companions used to raise on those rare occasions that the knights would gather. Drink and company lead to banter and poor jokes, which created much missed laughter that the Wild Knights always enjoyed.

Archer, warrior or mage, the Wild Knights would hurl jibes at once another, without a moment’s thought. Yet, when needed, there was no stronger camaraderie and they would all die for one another.

entries.name: Bramblemead Cape
entries.description:
The heart of Bramblemead village was never really the castle, which came much later to the party. It wasn’t the town hall. It wasn’t the druid huts. It was the windmill. Grain heaped by the village was brought here and milled down into flour. The flour became bread, pastry and batter, turning village meals into something that helped people to live, rather than simply survive.

Food, becomes a banner around which everyone can gather. To break bread with one’s enemy was a way to settle old scores, and forge new connections. More good has been done over the dinner table, than on any throne. Flour, turned Bramblemead from a settlement, into a thriving village.

Now, the windmill lies dormant and still. The foundations warped by the centuries, despite the magic holding the rot at bay in the ancient timber, and the stone cracking from time. When humanity fell, it was rats and goblins that claimed the heart of the village, though they had no use for the swirling sails.

To the goblins it was a place where food could be hidden. Supplies sealed up from rival tribes. For the rats, it was a restaurant full of goblin supplies that were never well sealed.

The sail no longer turns. But, perhaps, in the fullness of time, this village heart might beat again.

entries.name: Bronze Platebody
entries.description:
Bronze was once a secret held by the ancient dwarves. It is a more robust metal forged from an alliance of two others. 

The alliance of two different faiths had its own warrior force to defend its shared ideals. Clad in polished bronze armour, these warriors stood out against the stark green of Brynmoor’s fields. They upheld traditions and punished those who blasphemed against either faith. 

The bronze advisors, as they were known, would offer advice from both a Saraodminist and a Guthixian viewpoint—order and balance side by side. Such was the intention, but the scales were already tipped. Policies began to slip more and more in favour of the Saradominist approach until the Guthixian faith slowly dwindled as the Saradominist view took centre stage.

entries.name: Bronze Platelegs
entries.description:
Bronze was once a secret held by the ancient dwarves. It is a more robust metal forged from an alliance of two others. 

As the Saradomin faith became more popular, the bronze-clad inquisition enforced Saradomin’s laws, even when they conflicted with the Guthixian faith. It was a slow change, but they went from clearing shrines of monsters to clearing shrines of the Guthixian heresy. 

When the druids finally rebelled, the bronze-clad enforcers were called against them, not the White Knights. The cruel irony of being arrested by the force created to protect them.

entries.name: Bronze Shield
entries.description:
While heavier than other materials, there’s little argument that a bronze shield is a superior defence to wood and leather materials. The metal turns aside almost any blow, protecting the wielder behind its mass. 

Even the Wild Knights, who usually shunned metal weapons, would don bronze shields into battle. Their philosophy was that a life is worth more than a principle. 

Before the peace treaty with their goddess, Lougrim, the garou would often get into conflict with travelling villagers. They saw the humans as prey, willfully intruding on their land and therefore consenting to be hunted. The humans, of course, saw things differently. 

Garou weapons were powerful and delivered by creatures of unnatural strength. Yet bronze would defend against these attacks, and it gave the garou pause, for they had yet to battle foe with such intriguing technology. Battles that would previously have been a slaughter became skirmishes as the garou tested their might against these new bronze defences. 

This comparative peace did not last long.

entries.name: Dark Mage Hood
entries.description:
Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. 

The first set of dark mage robes were so named because the technique to craft them required cloth that had been dyed by a unique alchemical mixture. As the years passed and Guthix introduced runes, the mixture was replaced with subtle enchantments, though the appearance was kept the same for tradition’s sake. 

Naturally, many practitioners of magic preferred this armour because of its darker aesthetic. Indeed, many rogue “dark wizards” would don this armour and use magic to engage in sinister undertakings, earning this armour’s moniker a more sinister meaning.

entries.name: Dark Mage Robe Legs
entries.description:
Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. 

The most infamous dark wizards became a fairytale for the people of Brynmoor, a cautionary tale about greed and the desire for power. They sought power in the darkest of places, and it turned them into something monstrous. 

They appeared in the village in the dead of night as twisted versions of themselves—mindless creatures infused with a shadowy essence. Those who found themselves in their path had their lives ripped out of them until nought but an empty husk remained. 

It took all the visiting Wild Knights to take them down. Arrow after arrow, spell after spell, the task seemed almost insurmountable until the light of the sun made the creatures vulnerable. In their death throws, it was as if some horrible chill fell across the world as if a door somewhere had been opened into somewhere it shouldn’t.

entries.name: Dark Mage Robes
entries.description:
Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. 

Brynmoor had a string of so-called “dark wizards.” Most were little more than bandits with a penchant for magic. The guards were enough to deal with most troublemakers, but a small group of them caused real trouble. 
They were members of the “Children of Shadows”, a Zamorakian cult that began to spread through the population. The cult fed on distrust, paranoia and greed, some very human traits. Among this number were three apprentices of the wizard’s guild, who were frustrated that they were not given the promotions they felt they deserved. 

In their quest for power, the ‘Children of Shadows’ stumbled upon ancient vaults, repositories of the dragonkin’s long-forgotten secrets. Here, they discovered the remnants of a forbidden text, a relic of immense power. Driven by their arrogance, they chose to follow its instructions, unaware of the horrors they were about to unleash.

entries.name: Dragonbane Cape
entries.description:
A seer once dreamed about brave warriors who walked across Ashenfall in another time. An age both past and present, where the rules of the world were different. These great heroes challenged and slew an echo of Velgar, saving a land that never was. 
While the seer’s memory of that dream fades with each passing moment, she was able to embroider the event into a cape, so that all might know of these legends from another time.

entries.name: Dragonblight Shield
entries.description:
Strange magics have transformed the head of a tyrant, into a mystical adornment to this powerful shield. It is still strong, still durable and resists the fury of dragons, but now the shield seethes with Velgar’s wrath.

The magic of the shield is twisted into a bitter poison. One that yearns to strike and rage against any in its path. In battle, it’s possible to turn this poison on one’s enemies, afflicting them with a dragon’s hate.

Sometimes, in the dark, when the night is silent, it’s as if the shield whispers angry curses into the darkness. As if the last vestiges of Velgar’s fury are carried on the wind as hateful poison.

entries.name: Fallen Hoplite's Aspis
entries.description:
The hoplites of Emberwood named themselves after Saradomin’s forces in the holy scripture. The legendary hoplites were warriors on the world of Hallow, who were trained from farmers and artisans, rather than military families or nobility, and the Emberwood hoplites came from similar stock.

They were best known for their fighting style using spears and shields, with the shield being the defining feature. These shields were designed to be worn for longer periods of time, resting against the shoulder for more comfortable carrying.

The hoplites may have been raised from peasant stock, but their camaraderie made them a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.

As the withering took them, the hoplites retained the rote memory of their training and remained a deadly threat to all who faced them.

entries.name: Farmer's Hat
entries.description:
There are those who spend years studying the magic of druids, to try and find a way to bend nature to their will. They go on long pilgrimages, solve complicated riddles and have arduous conversations with nature spirits about the fundamentals of reality. 

They needn't have bothered. For, you see, there are already those who understand how to reshape the land to serve them. People who cultivate rows of plants, each of them focused on providing food, medicine or some other benefit to their agricultural master. The farmer may be the greatest nature wizard in all of Gielinor, though they need never utter a single spell. 

This hat was once worn by the farmers of Bramblemead as a sign of their status. It was created by one Abigail Potterington, age 6, who had been taught the basics of embroidery by her mother, who had been taught it by her mother, and she by her mother and so on. The flower was said to represent a great towering oak – Abigail was not good at art.

entries.name: Fellhollow Cape
entries.description:
Fellhollow could have been a new utopia, were it not for the cruelty of the godeater. Imaru and Xikotal adored their human neighbours and dreamed of a society where both dragon and human could thrive together in peace.

Now the land, like that dream, has broken. A hateful hunger from beyond the grave has consumed all the life, love and joy in the land. The dead roam desperately seeking to tear the tiniest threads of life from any living thing that crosses their path, and the afterlife itself, here, is poisoned by Imaru’s grief.

Yet, once, long ago, this land was beautiful. A myriad of colours danced in the breeze, the anima twist turning the region into a kaleidoscopic wonder. The now ruined streets were once filled with laughter, joy and song. And the dragons danced across the skies in loved-laced poetry.

This cape is a burieal shroud for a world that could have been.

entries.name: Fractured Cape
entries.description:
Brakka’s hubris was a marvel to behold, perhaps more impressive than any monument of his construction. When Rasthin shared with him the elemental power she had wrung from Ashenfall’s mysterious vents, Brakka became a master of the earth itself.

With the power to shape stone and soil, by will alone, Brakka could have created great villages. He could have constructed aqueducts and watermills that could brought Ashenfall into a new, golden age. Instead, he made a tower.

A single tower that rose as far as the eye could see. Forged through his own power, and the blood, sweat and tears of garou slaves. It is, perhaps, fitting, that this is where he died. Kuldra, the godeater, crushed him beneath her great claw and feasted on his anima-rich soul. Stealing Brakka’s power for herself.

She gifted Velgar, her most trusted general, with the elemental mastery of the fallen Nodon architect, and, to mock the dragonkin further, Velgar took Brakka’s monument as his new lair.

Now the tower stands for all to see, as a reminder of dragonkin hubris, and rightfully deserves its new moniker; Brakka’s folly.

entries.name: Goblin War Banner
entries.description:
To most goblins, war is like breathing. Every action a precursor to conflict. Every morning they wake with a focus on picking a fight. They rarely kill one another, it would be counterproductive, but they enjoy finding someone different enough that they can justify a spat.

This is what Bandos engineered them for. When the god arrived on Yu’Biusk, he urged the population into constant conflict. Nations became states, that were ground down into tribes. An entire civilisations reduced to platoons and squadrons.

This cape bears the symbol of Bandos, a weapon known as the kyzaj – a brutal blade designed to eviscerate an opponent.

Once this was a banner, praising the war god, but now it lies forgotten and the other banners defiled to worship a new Big High War God. Velgar, who defeated a god in single combat.

entries.name: Green Adventurer's Cape
entries.description:
Capes are stylish and protect against the weather. They can be elaborate symbols of stature, or simple cloth to act as a ward against the cold. This cape is the latter.

Simple, elegant, and functional. Worn by adventurers and explorers across Gielinor’s mainland and beyond.

After the dragon attack, there are few of these capes worn on Ashenfall. The rest sink beneath the ocean waves, are torn to pieces on the cliff rocks, or have long since burned to ash beneath draconic hate.

entries.name: Green Dragonhide Body
entries.description:
Wear the skin of your enemies, so that they know to fear you! This is the ranger way, to dress themselves in the outer layers of weaker dragons so that they larger dragons know not to mess with them.

Love makes fools of all of us. Infatuation more so, especially one-sided. Bilar was in love, so he claimed. He spoke of her beauty. He spoke of her acumen. He spoke of… well, he spoke a lot about things that you do not repeat in polite society. He wanted her and he wanted the ultimate gift to win her affection: a dragon’s heart.

Yet, dragons are unwilling to part with such a vital organ, and Bilar had to get creative. He found a dead dragon, one that had been slain in battle with a rival, and he decided to skin it. With it’s scaley hide in his possession he spent weeks fashioning powerful armour from the remains, until he had an outfit that resembled the creature he hunted.

So dressed, he set out towards the great stone circle near Emberwood, knowing that a dragon had recently made it its home. He would slay it, claim its heart and present it to the woman he loved and she would surely agree to be his forever.

entries.name: Green Dragonhide Chaps
entries.description:
Wear the skin of your enemies, so that they know to fear you! This is the ranger way, to dress themselves in the outer layers of weaker dragons so that they larger dragons know not to mess with them.

The funeral of Bilar Amaris was not a particularly popular one. A few fellow hunters stopped by to pay the briefest of respects, and a drunk great uncle turned up and got the name wrong. His death would have passed into complete obscurity, except for the clothes he was wearing when he died.

Despite the mauled condition of his corpse, the villagers that found him noticed the surprisingly supple and yet sturdy armour. Barely a scratch covered the dragonhide, and they remarked that if only he’d covered the neck a bit better, then he might not have ended up in the state he did.

The villagers brought the armour back and leatherworkers set to work on repeating it and improving it. Soon the best hunters in Emberwood would be wearing green dragonhide armour, and matched with better common sense, it kept them alive much longer.

This was partially done in a misguided attempt to win the affections of the “black-haired beauty” that had set up a little potion shop in the village. Like many idiots, he had convinced himself that all a woman could ever want was a strong man that was capable of killing something bigger than he was.

He was, unsurprisingly, deeply mistaken.

entries.name: Hard Leather Body
entries.description:
Hardened leather is a sturdier defence, able to turn away more powerful attacks. Favoured by hunters and rangers, who like the defence it offers without the reduction in mobility brought on by sturdier armour.

During the schism and the inner conflicts between ‘pure’ humans and the Amalgamated, Wild Knights would sneak into the village and rescue persecuted Amalgamated under the dead of night. Their armour was silent enough to allow them to move through the village quietly, and they had enough mobility to make a quick escape if caught.

Those who captured Amalgamated were rarely well-equipped soldiers, and their knives were often turned away by the hardness of the leather. During those dark times, this simple armour saved many lives.

entries.name: Head Paladin
entries.description:
The knights of Saradomin had many names over the years. White Knights. Temple Knights. In Ashenfall they were called Paladins. Brave, and faithful, members of noble families that took up the sword.

They were the second, third and fourth children of Brynmoor’s “nobility” – a title given to those families that were most loyal to the priesthood, and the most obedient were raised the highest.

This helm was a symbol of pride to the respectable families of Brynmoor. A sign that the bearer had been chosen to stand as the guardian of Saradominist faith for all of Brynmoor to see. It earned them favour, it earned the status, it earned them the ire of those who followed a different faith.

entries.name: Head Wild Archer
entries.description:
The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt, putting even the garou to shame.

Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. They would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning.

The helm is designed to focus the wearer’s vision, so that their target receives all their attention. Distractions are cut out of the picture. entries.name: Iron Shield
entries.description:
When Glass Knife was caught, she had no concerns about safety. She was well armed as a blacksmith, better than most hunters who tracked her down. She wielded a dagger in one hand and an iron shield in another, and she snarled defiance at those who tried to condemn her for her crimes. 

She was, after all, protecting humanity. Purging impurity. Ridding them all of the Amalgamated stain on their bloodlines. In her mind she was doing the whole village a service. A worrying number of villagers agreed with her. 

As the wife of one of the elders, her sentence was small. An act of community service, doing what was already her job. She wasn’t imprisoned. She wasn’t executed. She wasn’t publicly condemned for her crime. She laughed off over a dozen murders with a cruel, smug-filled smile. 

While she carried an iron shield with her, and it weathered the reprisal of many an Amalgamated enraged at the lack of justice, her real shield was the status she held. Wife of an elder, blacksmith of the town, proof that when an Amalgamated was a victim, justice had its limits.

entries.name: Leather Shield
entries.description:
A leather shield consists of a thick piece of leather stretched across a wooden frame. Wooden shields are bulky and heavy, making them more unwieldy. In contrast, a leather shield’s relative lightness makes it much easier to move into position. 

Leather shields were popular with the villagers of Bramblemead since the materials were comparatively easy to gather. Young warriors often wielded them as they accompanied druids into the woods, where the druids gathered the herbs for their medicines and rituals. 

The Children of Shadows also enjoyed leather shields, which they decorated with Zamorakian symbols, hoping to intimidate anyone who saw them.

entries.name: Legs Lightness
entries.description:
A cousin to the better-known Boots of Lightness, popular on the Gielinor mainland. These leggings were created by Shana, a Bramblemead villager who hated the cold. While the boots were functional, and useful, making it easier to carry things round the village, she always felt the winds chill no matter what she wore.

Her solution was simple. Since enchantment created an excess of energy, at least when she did it – she was never going to become a wizard – she laced the leggings with the lightness charm.

The effect was twofold. Firstly, she could carry things around the town as easily as if she were wearing the boots. Secondly, the enchantment kept her legs nice and warm.

Fortunately, the designs for these leggings improved over the years, removing the overheating problem that Shana had been so fond of. Although she was doubtless less fond of it after her house caught fire.

Progress demands sacrifice.

They all met the fate they deserved, in the end.

entries.name: Mithril Shield
entries.description:
Doric insists that you should be able to see your face in a mithril shield. That's the mark of quality: if you can check for rock cakes in your teeth before battle, then you've made a good one. 

There's at least a little science behind that. The more tempered mithril is, the more it reflects. Doric isn't being a narcissist here: he knows what he is doing.

entries.name: Mystic Robes
entries.description:
A long-held frustration of the Zamorakian magi, the magical sect of the Children of Shadows, was that Zamorak never came to them. At no point did Zamorak ever set foot on the shores of Ashenfall. This fact is key to understanding the resentful mentality of the shadow mage: they feel a constant undercurrent of abandonment. It also explains why they believe that mystic cloth 'came from Zamorak himself'.

Mystic cloth was only for use by the Archmage and his council. It was not only a sign of standing within Dowdun Reach; it was a sign that you should probably get on with your work. If you heard the hum of mystic cloth behind you, you had better not be doing something untoward.

The role of mystic cloth changed when Archmage Alric and Lord Rasmodel agreed to meet an attaché of Imaru and Xikotal. It was some cleric from Emberwood, looking to renew an annual trade agreement. 

It was to be a routine meeting, and Alric thought nothing of it. He planned to look at the cleric with disdain and sign the contract provided. But to Alric's scorn, the envoy turned up in mystic cloth. A mystic cloth waistcoat, and a mystic cloth cap, jauntily worn. She was good-natured and jovial, which only made the interaction more painful for Alric.

Alric dared not look at Rasmodel, but he knew that there would be a smirk on that smug face. Alric burned the contract and blasted the envoy off the top of Dowdun Reach. The contract would have to wait.

From that point on, mystic cloth was not reserved for the greatest magi. It was free for any common magi to wear. Alric resolved to wear a different cloth.

entries.name: Necromancer's Crown
entries.description:
Those who wield the power over life and death have a tendency to crave control. They need to manage things in their life on a pathological level, and this need often grows into a desire to manage the lives of everyone else.

The most well known necromancer in Fellhollow was a man called Calius Waithe. He was one of the Children of Shadows until he decided that their policies of peaceful evil wasn’t what he was looking for. He was more an overtly evil sort of guy.

He decided, on one fateful autumnal eve, to raise an army of the undead and march them on Emberwood. He imagined the village cowering before him as he named himself their new king.

entries.name: Paladin Platelegs
entries.description:
The knights of Saradomin had many names over the years. White Knights. Temple Knights. In Ashenfall they were called Paladins. Brave, and faithful, members of noble families that took up the sword.

They were the second, third and fourth children of Brynmoor’s “nobility” – a title given to those families that were most loyal to the priesthood, and the most obedient were raised the highest.

These platelegs were exceptionally well made. Sturdier and stronger than the armour worn by Brynmoor guards, and other members of Ashenfall’s human soldiers. It was certainly stronger than the helms of the Guthixian aligned knights, or the druids they guarded.

Paladins were a righteous force, noble and true to the priest’s teachings. They brought order from chaos, and discipline to sloth. Remaking Bramblemead according to the church’s designs.

entries.name: Ranger Tights
entries.description:
It was on a cold winter night, that Nightingale and Moragrin finally met. The assassin had given up on interrogating the villagers and worked instead to lay a trap for the highwaywoman. A caravan, loaded with gold, made its way from village to castle under the cover of night, and Nightingale arrived to claim her bounty.

It was a short, but brutal battle. Arrows whistled through the air, making music like an orchestra. Daggers glinted in the moonlight, in a dance of death that would have shredded the life of any normal person. But Nightingale and Moragrin were evenly matched, until an errant magpie brought it all to an end.

Confused by the battle, the magpie had woken from its sleep in a mad panic and dived down at the fighting pair. The distraction was just enough for Moragrin’s blade to pierce the Nightingale’s heart and as she pulled her mask from her victim, Moragrin’s world shattered as she saw the moment the life left the eyes of her younger sister.

entries.name: Ranger Tunic
entries.description:
The Nightingale was the bane of the nobility, and they became obsessed with her destruction. Not just her capture, they needed her obliterated – gone from the memories of the population forever. But this was a tricky task indeed, because the wealth the Nightingale harvested, was given back to the people of Bramblemead, rather than lining her own coffers, making her a local hero.

So they hired Moragrin the hunter to track her down. Moragrin was a cruel and merciless assassin, trained in multiple weapon techniques. She delighted in little more than seeing the look in her victims eyes the moment they transition from living to dead.

For days she followed stories of Nightingale, wandering through the village, adopting multiple disguises that she might uncover Nightingale’s real name. In all that time she learned only one thing, that the villagers loved Nightingale and would never knowingly give her up.

entries.name: Shadowscale Cape
entries.description: This cape is all that remains of the once proud archers of Fellhollow. Hunters and scouts who would stalk the forests and woodland hunting game to feed the other villagers. As the time dragged on their flesh and clothes have rotted away, leaving only this cape as a reminder of their existence.

entries.name: Shadowscale Hood
entries.description:
The last hunter in Fellhollow hid in the trees for as long as he could. Beneath him the dead shambled and stumbled and clawed at the bark, yet he remained in the trees safely out of reach.

He fed himself on nuts and berries, stealing form the treasure troves of squirrels and birds, occasionally risking a trip to the ground to hunt a passing animal. He gave up on cooking the meat he hunted, as he could not stay on the ground long enough before the dead rose up to face him, so he tore into the carcasses of deer, sheep and rats, trying his best not to vomit.

He barely noticed when his appetite changed, since he was so used raw flesh and the sickly cold taste of blood pooling in his mouth. So, when the withering began to take him, he hardly noticed.

Sometimes, if you’re quick enough, you may catch a glimpse of a skeleton in the tree branches. Even in death he fears the monsters on the ground.

entries.name: Shroud Of Noggin
entries.description:
Poor old Noggin found no peace in death, because even the gods forgot him. When he reached the River Noumenon, there was no guide to usher him through to the Afterlife. No radiant light to beckon him forward into the loving arms of those he'd lost. instead, there was silence and it went on and on. 

Always quiet and forgettable, the universe simply failed to recall him. His name was recorded in no books of the dead. The various creatures that prey on lost souls, never once thought he seemed like a pleasant meal. Instead they did nothing, except to leave him to his wandering, forgotten and alone. 

Then four people went digging where they shouldn't, and that made Noggin mad. Forgettable as he was, he had always made a point of preserving the status quo and to see these four ruffians blindly digging into the soil that had never done anyone a disservice, why that was unforgivable – he couldn't let it stand. So he crept into their camp, and found the treasure they coveted, and secreted himself within the gold and silver, waiting to be found. Found he was, for when they opened the chest they saw no treasure, no jewels, no trinkets of worth – because Noggin had eaten all of them, swallowed the pieces down into the void – they found only a ghostly sackcloth head glaring back at them, with nothing but hate in its eyes. 

This is that piece of sackcloth, and it's not happy to see you.

entries.name: Splitbark Body
entries.description:
Not all druids follow the notion that one must live a life of peaceful coexistence. After all, the animal kingdom is full of conflict and conquest, predator and prey, as well as battles for dominance. Some druids feel, therefore, that to truly emulate nature one must do so fully, including tooth and claw. The problem there is that druids are, by nature, generally on the squishier side and so they needed armour that would protect their vital areas better than their normal robes.

Soon, many druids began wearing these robes made from the bark of Ashenfall trees. The first incarnations were deeply unwieldy, taking on an ungainly and unfashionable cylindrical shape – little more than tree trunks with holes for the arms and legs. They were effective insomuch that attacks rarely got through, but they made it somewhat difficult to retaliate.

Later the wizard Lavernius realises that with a few tweaks, the addition of some elegant fine cloth, one could fashion the splitbark armour into a far more glamorous form. She took to decorating her robes with glittering gemstones and silver filigree, making her stand out from the crowd. An excellent distraction in magical duels, but a terrible spotlight for local thieves.

entries.description:

On Ashenfall, it was the druid Pikenmix who first tried to break out of the peace-loving mould. They learned magic that would allow them to hurl flame from their fingertips hoping it might be enough. Yet, as the enemies got too close, she soon learned that she needed stronger defence than her meagre hood would allow.

It was when she was lost in thought, that she found the solution – by walking straight into a tree. Her nose broke in several places and her entire body screamed in pain, yet the tree remained unaffected by her violent interaction.

So it was that she crafted herself a helm made from the very same tree. Partially in revenge, but mostly because she knew how strong the bark could be.

entries.name: Steel Full Helm
entries.description:
It was late in the development of Fellhollow that the people needed armour. They made do with old hand me down leather and bronze gear, brought with them from Bramblemead, for the most part, because what need was there for armour when you were protected by dragons.

Kuldra would put a stop to that mindset in the end, but it was the Children of Shadows who forged the first steel gear in Fellhollow. One member, in particular, Sadia Vulketra, began to feel that the order lacked the strength it may one day need to defend against the Saradominist forces.

There was no war. No conflict like that in Emberwood, indeed the four major faiths got along rather well with one another. Yet, the history books told Sadia exactly what the priests of Saradomin would do to the worshippers of the god of chaos.

She forged a helm first, with the assistance of one of her many lovers, a blacksmith Amalgamated called Vesk. The first helmet was styled with great curling horns, stained black by the forge’s flames.

Naturally, this style didn’t prove popular with the rest of the village, as they began crafting steel helms of their own, favouring a more simplistic approach, and a feathered plume, to look fancy.

entries.name: Steel Platelegs
entries.description:

When Kuldra arrived it was as if the air had grown heavy, pressing down on everyone. A whole village fell silent as the Godeater turned her gaze upon them. As Imaru and Xikotal rose to face her, villagers instinctively ran to don their heirloom steel armour, hoping that they wouldn‘t have to use it, but knowing in their hearts that they would.

Yet, it wasn’t Kuldra that found a use for the armour. After Xikotal’s death, Kuldra left the region, leaving Imaru to her grief. And it would be that grief and the rage that came with it that would ultimately lead to the rising dead and the sad and sorry need to fight against them.

entries.name: Steel Shield
entries.description:
There are few things as good at shielding you from harm, as a great slab of metal between you and your foe. The steel shield is more durable than its iron kin, capable of resisting greater and more deadly blows.

It was popular among Fellhollow locals, who would play a game that indicated an intelligence shortage among the population. The game consisted of one player being equipped with a crossbow and other players would hide around the area carrying steel shields. The crossbow wielder would then hunt the other players and try and fire a bolt into their shields, marking them as out of the game.

Unsurprisingly the injuries caused by this game were large and common place. Even the death of some of the players wouldn’t cause the activity to be banned. “It’s tradition”, “it’s just good fun”, “hardly anyone gets hurt”, these were the arguments made even as parents grieved the loss of their child from the game.

entries.name: Studded Leather Body
entries.description:
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for the mixture of agility and defence. 

Dealing with the armour’s distinctive scent soon became a training tool for more dangerous hunters. It taught them to use the wind as a weapon. They would always walk against it, the wind in their faces, meaning that the garou could not smell them coming. When the weather didn’t help them, the Wild mages would cast constant subtle air spells, changing the breeze’s direction.

One wild mage and her friend, a strange boy who wore a wolf’s skull as a mask, got the tactic down to an art. She used strange, sinister magics to enchant bones to maintain air spells, allowing her to precisely control the wind’s direction. She used this to lead the garou into traps, where her ally leapt from the shadows, taking out the unfortunate garou warriors.

entries.name: Studded Leather Chaps
entries.description:
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for the mixture of agility and defence. 

While the design of studded leather made it excellent for hunters and invaluable in battles against the garou, it fell short against those who knew its construction. Betrayal is a constant foe, and once the garou war had come to a close, the Wild Knights found themselves at the mercy of it. 

Though there were more dangerous threats, with the dragons that appeared out of nowhere, there were always some that prioritized power and persecution over common sense. Daggers emerged from the shadows and drove between the plates sewn into the leather. The poison on the tips of these blades ended the life of more than a few Wild Knights. 

The assassins called themselves the “Glass Knives” in memory of the serial killer that took the lives of so many Amalgamated. To them, the strangeness of the knights was a greater threat than the dragons, and they were happy to pay the terrible price that their actions would cost.

entries.name: Studded Leather Cowl
entries.description:
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for the mixture of agility and defence. 

Most Wild Knights favoured studded leather armour over the more durable metal plate. Moving through the forests required as much grace as guts, and stealth is always a hunter’s friend. 

When they were brought into the war against the garou, the leather armour proved less popular at first. While durable and agile, leather has a strong and distinctive smell. The garou’s olfactory senses were much stronger than humans were prepared for, capable of tracking down the leathery smell from a disturbing range. Wind magic helped to keep the scent away from them, but it wasn’t enough to eradicate it.

entries.name: Whispering Cape
entries.description:
It is said these swamps are haunted. Those who wander it at night, tell stories of whispering that bubbles up from the fetid water.

There is a coldness to these swamps, that is more than just temperature. It reaches beneath the warmest clothing and presses itself into bone and blood. Heartbeats slow and bravery breaks beneath its touch.

The trees here are old and spiteful, their roots wrapped around the bones of adventurers, villagers, and warriors alike. They care not for goblin, human, or garou, they will strangle the remains of any within their reach.

Occasionally tiny stones will bubble from the surface, black as midnight and cold as the darkest winter night. A villager once tried to craft jewelry from these stones, thinking them beautiful. It took twelve village guard to put an end to her murder spree.

This cape is woven from the fibres of swamp plants, and shields its wearer from the swamp’s whispers. Or so the old wives tales claim.

entries.name: White Adventurer's Cape
entries.description:
Capes are stylish and protect against the weather. They can be elaborate symbols of stature, or simple cloth to act as a ward against the cold. This cape is the latter.

Simple, elegant, and functional. Worn by adventurers and explorers across Gielinor’s mainland and beyond.

After the dragon attack, there are few of these capes worn on Ashenfall. The rest sink beneath the ocean waves, are torn to pieces on the cliff rocks, or have long since burned to ash beneath draconic hate.

entries.name: White Platebody
entries.description:
Sir Percival Lateef only had a short moment of wonder, before the horror struck. The beach he had arrived on was surrounded by cliffs, meaning his only options were to climb or to swim, and since he was wearing the heavy armour of the White Knights, he decided that sinking wasn’t an option.

It took him many hours and several near falls, but he eventually made his way up and down the cliffside, only to encounter a region filled with the ravenous undead.

As a White Knight he trained to fight such evils and he fended them off as best he could, yet there were too many for him to face alone. He was forced to retreat, to a shrine, atop a rocky island, displaying the symbol of Saradomin, and there he prayed.

entries.name: White Platelegs
entries.description:
Trapped by a shrine that stood atop a rocky island, surrounded by the hungry dead, Sir Lateef prayed to Saradomin with all his strength. He begged for salvation, for a miracle that might free him, but silence was his only answer.

He barricaded himself atop the monument, the dead scrabbling at his defences, their unholy growling keeping him from even a moment’s sleep.

As time drew on, and hunger and thirst took him, he turned to the symbol of Saradomin in defeated rage. Where was his god? Why was he abandoned? Had he not spent his life in service of the lord of light?

Enraged, he took his sword and cleaved Saradomin’s symbol from its plinth, causing it to crash to the floor. Filled with guilt, he hid the fallen piece from his sight. His last act was one of blasphemy, but perhaps an act justly performed.

entries.name: Wizard Robes
entries.description:
These blue robes are the signature clothing worn by every respectable mage. Apprentices look forward to the day they first wear these, as it shows they have graduated to full wizard status. The wizard's tower, in particular, uses these robes as a uniform, signifying their magical power and fealty to the god of order, Saradomin.

Despite the antagonistic intentions of the White Knights' arrival in the Wizard’s Guild, the two factions got along well. Apprentices would often prank low-ranked knights, using small spells to make them appear foolish. The knights would respond with more practical reprisals, which led to an escalation of shenanigans until the highest-ranking members of both orders got involved. Then things got really out of hand.

entries.name: Wooden Shield
entries.description:
The children of Bramblemead loved nothing more than to craft themselves wooden shields and swords and then challenge one another to single combat. They would play the roles of brave heroes against dastardly villains, whacking one another with their wooden toys. It gave the local healers constant work. 

Yey, a wooden shield is no toy and has saved the lives of countless warriors. As a beast’s claws slice against you, having a hunk of wood between you and the creature is much appreciated. Wood splinters, but flesh bleeds, and blood is less easily replaced than timber.

entries.name: Yellow Adventurer's Cape
entries.description:
Capes are stylish and protect against the weather. They can be elaborate symbols of stature, or simple cloth to act as a ward against the cold. This cape is the latter.

Simple, elegant, and functional. Worn by adventurers and explorers across Gielinor’s mainland and beyond.

After the dragon attack, there are few of these capes worn on Ashenfall. The rest sink beneath the ocean waves, are torn to pieces on the cliff rocks, or have long since burned to ash beneath draconic hate.

entries.name: Ava's Attractor
entries.description:
Ava is the apprentice to Dr Oddenstein, an eccentric scientist who lives in Draynor Manor, and a skilled inventor in her own right. She whiles away her limited free time by studying the lesser-known field of necroballistics, and creating strange and wonderful gizmos to further her studies. 

Perhaps her proudest achievement, is the invention of the attractor. By harnessing the energies of an undead chicken to the harmonic frequencies of a common bar magnet, her device can snatch grounded projectiles and bring them back to the quiver before they can be lost. This money saving experiment is not only great for hunters, but for anyone looking for an excuse to fill their enemies full of sharp sticks of wood. 

Always the generous sort, but one with little head for marketing, Ava has decided to pass on her genius invention to others. Rather than publishing a paper, or passing the methodology onto the Varrock library, she has instead written the instructions in a bottle and sent it adrift in the ocean for anyone to find. Fate, she believes, will draw it to where it is meant to go. Like magnets, probably.

entries.description: In your hands is dragon material that was likely forged by the dragonkin themselves. An ancient race, older than the current revision of the universe, made some crossbow limbs and now you're manhandling them. There's not much you can do with that information, but it's fascinating nonetheless.

entries.name: Golden Scorned Wilderness Cape
entries.description: We originally imagined an agility course that got you hopping from one Kuldra head to another. Imagine that! Would you be standing there with a Golden Scorned Wilderness Cape if that was the case?

entries.name: Healing Potion (Expired)
entries.description:
Hold a healing potion in your hands and doubt might enter the mind. Do you drink it? Do you apply it directly to the wound? Is it a suppository? Well, allow us to clarify: it is taken orally. 

A healing potion won't just address your egregious malady. It will help with minor nuisances, too. If you've got a spot on the inside of your nostril, it will tidy that up nicely. An armpit itch? Gone in seconds. Ingrowing toenail? Consider it done.

entries.name: Large Wardstone (Inactive)
entries.description: A more powerful and refined wardstone, this one allows you a much greater return on investment. When activated, it draws energy from the soul more cleanly and efficiently, reducing the impact of Soulscourge on the user.

entries.name: Medium Wardstone (Inactive)
entries.description: Some materials are better at resonating with souls than others. This is why a home made of better quality stones feels more comfortable than one made from pebbles. When used in wardstones, they allow for more powerful effects at no greater cost to the soul itself. Drawing out more of the ambient anima within a person, whilst minimizing the damage done.

entries.name: Small Wardstone (Inactive)
entries.description:
Wardstones are handy tools for anyone working with wards. Armour, when created on an anima-rich continent like Ashenfall, is infused with threads of enchantment that harness natural magic to provide an extra layer of protection for the wearer.

This protection depletes upon use, as the energy within the ward is expended on the effect. But the wardstone can rectify this situation… for a price.

The stone around the wardstone is hollow and more brittle than it seems, and the rune essence is carefully laid within it along with a final ingredient – a drop of the creators own blood. This blood, and the rune essence formation, creates a sort of harmonious connection between the bearer of the wardstone and the stone itself.

When the stone is broken, it activates the rune essence and draws anima in from the nearest pure source – the soul of the user.

Souls are containers of pure anima. They grow over time from experience and adventure, the more the bearer of said soul enriches their life with activity, the stronger the soul. This means that the damage the wardstone creates, whilst not insignificant, is easily repaired through the simple passage of time. Especially on Ashenfall, where merely surviving to the next hour is an adventure.

Wardstones are great in a pinch, but one must be careful not to use too many, less the damage they deal to themselves becomes too great.

entries.name: Snake Leather
entries.description: Snakes have a terrible deal in life. They must crawl along the floor, in the filth everyone else steps over. They suffer hate, fear and aggression from everyone who sees them and worst of all, if they bite their tongue, they're doomed. This snakeskin leather is gathered exclusively from the latter snakes, those who chomped down inefficiently and became their own undoing. This makes the leather both ethical and comparatively easy to gather. Waste not, want not, after all.

entries.name: Snake Skin
entries.description:
Blacksmiths hate this one simple trick. They spend their lives mastering interlocking chains and plates, only for dragons to be born with them. A third of the blacksmith's punters are now gone, hunting for dragons rather than dropping some coin at their forges. It's enough to make a blacksmith sob into their anvil. 

Blue dragons hate that one simple trick too, of course. Their venn diagram overlaps with the blacksmith's: they'd rather people got their armours from somewhere other than dragons.

entries.name: Weak Healing Potion (Expired)
entries.description:
Alchemists have long strived to create potions to rid mankind of all their ills. Normally these potions are regeneratives, that boost the body’s ability to repair itself by drawing in the ambient anima and infusing it into the blood and tissue of the drinker. On the mainland this changes healing from a matter of days, to a matter of hours. On Ashenfall the results are far more pronounced.

The ambient anima of the region is so strong, that wounds heal in moments. Cuts vanish as if they never were, the wounds healing so quickly that even scars cannot form. The weaker potions burn themselves out before they can heal massive injuries, but the results are impressive none the less.

entries.name: Clean Water
entries.description: Boiling the water separates the tainted elements in the liquid, allowing you to scrape it off and enjoy a more pleasant beverage.
pages: Boiling the water separates the tainted elements in the liquid, allowing you to scrape it off and enjoy a more pleasant beverage.

entries.name: Dirty Water
entries.description: This water will quench your thirst a little, but it contains a faint residue of a cataclysmic event that afflicted Ashenfall. As a result, there are traces of a tainted substance in the water that will damage the soul of anyone who drinks it, if they’re not a native that’s adapted to it.

entries.name: Dwellberry Infusion
entries.description: The delicious dwellberry infuses the water with a delightful flavour. It’s easier and far more refreshing than normal water. You’ll find this hydrates you much better than normal water.
pages: The delicious dwellberry infuses the water with a delightful flavour. It’s easier and far more refreshing than normal water. You’ll find this hydrates you much better than normal water.

entries.name: Evasive Infusion
entries.description: The smaller creatures can be annoyingly good at getting out of harms way. When boiling water infused with a small fang, belonging to one of these critters, this evasive essence can be pulled into the clean water, allowing the drinker to benefit from it.
pages: The smaller creatures can be annoyingly good at getting out of harms way. When boiling water infused with a small fang, belonging to one of these critters, this evasive essence can be pulled into the clean water, allowing the drinker to benefit from it.

entries.name: Ferocious Infusion
entries.description: Boiling away the tainted material, in the water, while infusing it with an animal bone, causes the mixture to draw in some of the primal resonance of the bone. Drinking the infusion temporarily allows the drinker to feel some of that animalistic ferocity.
pages: Boiling away the tainted material, in the water, while infusing it with an animal bone, causes the mixture to draw in some of the primal resonance of the bone. Drinking the infusion temporarily allows the drinker to feel some of that animalistic ferocity.

entries.name: Fleet-Footed Infusion
entries.description: The deer of Ashenfall are quick and nimble, able to dash across entire regions at the drop of a hat. By boiling the tainted water of Ashenfall combined with a deer’s antlers, some of this essence of swiftness is drawn into the clean water, granting anyone who drinks it a measure of that fleet-footed nature.

entries.name: Maple Infusion
entries.description: The distilled strength of a maple tree, pumped straight to your dietary tract. You might fell a rising fury whenever you stare at a logging axe, however.
pages: The distilled strength of a maple tree, pumped straight to your dietary tract. You might fell a rising fury whenever you stare at a logging axe, however.

entries.name: Pumpkin Spice Infusion
entries.description:
Across dimensional rifts this drink calls out to a part of us we try and hide. That piece of us that wants a touch of whimsy, when the world turns darker than we feel comfortable with. As the approaching shadow of winter looms, its cold chill reaching into our souls, drinks like these offer a little warmth against the oncoming frost.

Still, its allure can be overwhelming. There are some who succumb too heavily to its charms, becoming thralls to the flavour. Their entire personality clasps onto this mixture with frightening zeal.

It is tasty… but at what price?

entries.description: The juice of the berries infuses the water with a pleasant flavour. It’s easier and more refreshing to drink, offering greater hydrating properties than normal water.

entries.name: Baked Potato
entries.description: The simplicity. The elegance. Few things in life are quite as dependable as a good old baked potato. Crispy exterior, fluffy interior, and it goes well with just about anything.
pages: The simplicity. The elegance. Few things in life are quite as dependable as a good old baked potato. Crispy exterior, fluffy interior, and it goes well with just about anything.

entries.name: Beef & Tomato Stew
entries.description: Tomatoes go well with just about everything. They enhance the flavours of anything they’re paired with and a nice beef stew is no exception. The combined flavours are comforting as well as filling, and almost make you forget that you’re a long way from home, on a continent filled with murderous dragons.

entries.name: Cadavaberries
entries.description:
Don’t eat them. No, seriously, don’t. At least not raw. Cadavaberries are poisonous and deadly, often used in sinister ceremonies of ritual sacrifice. The cadavaberries on Ashenfall are equally toxic, but can be coaxed into good behaviour with the judicious addition of fire.

The toxins can be burned away, providing a surprisingly pleasant tasting berry beneath. But, one must be careful, for preparing them wrong is the last mistake someone is likely to make.

entries.name: Cauterised Undead Steak
entries.description:
Despite the appearance of their former owners, and the deeply unpleasant smell emanating from it, undead meat is not rotten. It, like the nature of its former owners, is preserved in a state between life and death, as if it’s on the cusp of souring, but never quite getting there.

This unique nature gives it some very interesting properties, but sadly taste isn’t one of them.

entries.name: Dried Cadavaberries
entries.description: The heat makes them edible, but only just. A once popular snack among the people of Fellhollow, who seemed overly cavalier about the consumption of deadly poisons.

entries.name: Dried Dwellberries
entries.description: Delicious berries. They make a great snack. Very popular among garou druids as a seasoning with their latest quarry.
pages: Delicious berries. They make a great snack. Very popular among garou druids as a seasoning with their latest quarry.

entries.name: Dried Redberries
entries.description: Easier, than standard redberries, to eat on the go, tastier too.
pages: Easier, than standard redberries, to eat on the go, tastier too.

entries.name: Dubious Meat Pie
entries.description:
The smell from this pie is strange. Undertones of gamey meats, the tantalising touch of subtle herbs and spices. The pastry is crip, inviting…and yet, beneath the crust, hidden behind the pleasantries, is the scent of something otherworldly.

Death has touched this pie.

entries.name: Dwellberries
entries.description: Pretty blue berries, go well in a cheesecake.

entries.name: Dwellberry Crunchies
entries.description: Dwellberries on Ashenfall are heartier than their mainland counterparts and make for excellent ingredients. The Wild Knights were particularly fond of this combination, though they referred to them as “Dwellberry splats” because Olis, their inventor, wasn’t a particularly good chef.

entries.name: Dwellberry Glazed Roast Flank
entries.description: A thick and juicy steak, combined with a rich and sticky dwellberry sauce. Each mouthful is like a taste explosion, and it can be difficult to hold yourself back. Orik the Bear was a Wild Knight who excelled in this dish, and other Wild Knights would seek him out at the gatherings for his culinary expertise.

entries.name: Dwellberry Glazed Roast Meat
entries.description: Dwellberries boiled down into a sticky sauce and liberally trailed across the meat. At first you might expect the combination wouldn’t work, but as you take that first mouthful, you find your tastebuds writhe in delight for this delicious combination.

entries.name: Fillet
entries.description: These fillets go surprisingly well with most side dishes. The texture is pleasant, the flavour is subtle and not too overpowering. They go particularly well with garlic.
pages: These fillets go surprisingly well with most side dishes. The texture is pleasant, the flavour is subtle and not too overpowering. They go particularly well with garlic.

entries.name: Flank Steak
entries.description: Thick and juicy, the flank steak is more filling than you might first expect. The dense meat means each mouthful makes you fuller for longer.
pages: Thick and juicy, the flank steak is more filling than you might first expect. The dense meat means each mouthful makes you fuller for longer.

entries.name: Forager's Sandwich
entries.description:
Brassica Prime approves of this sandwich.

Although, the mushrooms are a little much: they could probably have been thinned out. Maybe removed? Yes, remove them. The bread, too. Is it needed? Would you perhaps consider removing the envelope of bread that houses the sweet cabbage missive? Your dribbly jowls will thank us.

entries.name: Fortifying Soup
entries.description: It is said that Guthix created the first fortifying soup, as a gift for his chief druids. While the first few attempts created terrible food poisoning -- Guthix was a god, not a chef -- the perfected recipe soon became a favourite once he mixed in mushrooms. This was because the mushrooms absorbed much of the toxins, making it much more palatable.

entries.name: Fried Cabbage
entries.description:
Brassica Prime – the god of cabbages – gifted the world with this delicious vegetable, to lead the faithful on the noble path of nutrition. In his infinite, leafy, wisdom, he taught the early settlers about how one might fry the leaves, so that they would be even more delicious.

Now these fried cabbages offer those who consume them, the strength and stamina needed to brave the hardships of Ashenfall.

entries.name: Fried Onions
entries.description: Although the preparation leaves you weeping, and the smell makes it worse, fried onions are a delicious meal to get you through a difficult day.
pages: Although the preparation leaves you weeping, and the smell makes it worse, fried onions are a delicious meal to get you through a difficult day.

entries.name: Fruit Pie
entries.description:
Grannies everywhere are masters of this dish. Delicious fruits, a touch of sugar, some delightful pastry and that final ingredient – a dark blessing to ancient gods.

Or love, that works too.

With the pact complete, these pies allow you those fond memories, of comfort, hope and family. Something much needed out in the wilds of Ashenfall.

entries.name: Glazed Pumpkin Sandwich
entries.description: Not only is the roast pumpkin sandwich 'glazed' because it is doused in delicious maple syrup; it is also 'glazed' in the modern parlance, since it is 'showered with excessive, unwarranted or exaggerated praise'. Which makes it double-glazed. Like a window.

entries.name: Grilled Mushrooms
entries.description:
A great meal for a real fun guy… sorry.

Popular with terrible pun writers and villagers alike, roasted mushrooms were a staple diet across much Ashenfall. Wild Knights would forage for the best mushrooms to enjoy on their long hunts.

For those braving the poison filled Bloodblight Swamps, the fortifying effect of mushrooms made them even more popular.

entries.name: Hearty Fortifying Soup
entries.description: The Wild Knights would prepare this soup before heading into the poisonous Bloodblight swamp, or when facing venomous monsters. The mushrooms would absorb some of the toxins they encountered, and the soup would be filling enough to last them through the long journeys.

entries.name: Hearty Soup
entries.description: As the Bramblemead villagers discovered heartier vegetables, their recipes improved just as much. The simple soup now felt richer, tastier and more fulfilling. A nice, hearty, meal to get them through the tough jobs on the farm.
pages: As the Bramblemead villagers discovered heartier vegetables, their recipes improved just as much. The simple soup now felt richer, tastier and more fulfilling. A nice, hearty, meal to get them through the tough jobs on the farm.

entries.name: Hearty Stew
entries.description: A thick and tasty stew, rich in flavour and nutrients. Bramblemead’s head chef, Leander, use to say that eating this stew is like sitting around a warm fire with friends, the aroma of the rich gravy filling your nostrils makes you feel like you’re home. Villagers would gather when he made a big cauldron of the stew, each of them ready for an evening with friends.

entries.name: Kebab
entries.description: The Drunken Dwarf delights in the humble kebab, offering it to any that might grab his attention. The delicious combination of spices and subtle flavourings, makes it a marvellous meal. For those afflicted, or self-inflicted, with particular poisonings, the kebab is a time-honoured remedy.

entries.name: Maple Syrup
entries.description:
We are yet to find something that maple syrup does not elevate. Pancakes and bacon are the obvious ones, but try it out on things that are more left-field. Rat meat? Elevated. Terrorbird meat? Elevated. Undead eel? Eelevated. 

So, thank you, humble maple tree. You are a true wonder of the culinary and apothecary world. It won't stop us woodcutting you, but know that each cut comes with a maple syrup-sized dollop of guilt.

entries.name: Meat Pizza
entries.description:
A delicious pizza, covered in juicy tender pieces of meat, and seasoned with a delicious sauce. You might ask yourself where the cheese comes from, but it’s best not to think too hard about it. Ashenfall has many secrets and those who survive here must do many strange things. No one judges you for this “cheese”, it’s fine.

Just enjoy the delicious flavours and try not to have an existential crisis.

entries.name: Meat Stew
entries.description: A classic meal across multiple realities. The aviansie enjoy a version of this using insects called Tobi’it. Goblins make their meat stews out of anything they can find… results vary.
pages: A classic meal across multiple realities. The aviansie enjoy a version of this using insects called Tobi’it. Goblins make their meat stews out of anything they can find… results vary.

entries.name: Meat Twist Sandwich
entries.description: The 'twist' in the meat twist is a delightful redberry jus. The 'twist' in the Anima Twist is not, unfortunately, a delightful redberry jus.

entries.name: Mixed Grill
entries.description: For the carnivore in you, a plate of meat mixed with meat.
pages: For the carnivore in you, a plate of meat mixed with meat.

entries.name: Pumpkin Soup
entries.description: A taste of autumn reduced to slurry and warmed over the fire. In Fellhollow, pumpkin soup was a popular dish when the temperature started to drop. Locals would gather together and share enormous cauldrons full of soup, as a way to build bonds with their community. It is said that once the villagers created an enormous cauldron, so that Imaru and Xikotal could join in the tradition, though for the great dragons it was barely an appetiser.

entries.name: Pungent Omelette
entries.description:
Get a nose peg for this one. The aroma that wafts from this culinary creation is almost unholy in its sensation. It reaches down from your nostrils into your throat, then it winds its way into your mouth and twists your tastebuds in ways that must surely be illegal.

Still, if you can fight through the stench, then this eggy abomination is surprisingly tasty and helps fortify your body against toxic elements.

The “if” is doing a lot of work in that statement though.

entries.name: Rat Roast
entries.description: First discovered by a Lumbridge chef after a kitchen fire burned his mentor to ashes. Beneath the master chef’s hat was a deliciously roasted rat. Sure, it may not be the greatest delicacy of all time, but it’ll keep hunger at bay.

entries.name: Redberries
entries.description: These simple berries might be the gap between life and death, if eaten at the right time. A favourite treat for the villagers of Bramblemead, who would mix the berries into various desserts to enjoy. The red berry pie was particularly popular with visiting Wild Knights.

entries.name: Redberry Crunchies
entries.description: Although a crude facsimile of gnomish cooking, the redberry crunchy is a pleasant snack that will get you through the day.

entries.name: Redberry Glazed Roast Flank
entries.description: A thick, delicious and juicy flank steak, glazed with subtle redberry tones. Delicious and nutritious.

entries.name: Redberry Roast Rat
entries.description: Delicious roasted meat, with a redberry glaze. The fruit flavour combines with the meat in a sublime manner that makes it hard to eat this slowly.
pages: Delicious roasted meat, with a redberry glaze. The fruit flavour combines with the meat in a sublime manner that makes it hard to eat this slowly.

entries.name: Roast Dinner
entries.description:
Imagine it. You gather around the table, the warm smell of a freshly cooked roast wafts across the room. Your mother places a bowl of roast potatoes, so divinely crisp that you wonder if they’re even real. Your sibling places a tray of freshly cooked vegetables, a kaleidoscope of colourful foods waiting to be consumed. Your father, doggedly sticking to traditional gender roles as if the past is an anchor weighing him down, slices into the roast serving each of you juicy cuts of meat that make your mouth water.

And what are you doing in all of this? Hrmm? Nothing, that’s what! Pull your life together Stanley!

If your name is not Stanley, you can ignore that above message.

Here on Ashenfall you do not have those smiling faces to reflect upon, only the memories elucidated by the roast meat before you. As you tuck in, you’ll recall those moments of happier times, before you got stranded here with nothing.

entries.name: Squeaking Sausage
entries.description:
Sausages are proof that ignorance is bliss. When you bite into the juicy banger, you are best served not to think about its contents. Nor about the origins of the skin that contains the meat so well.

Although simple, and lacking in much needed herbs and spices, these sausages manage to curb your hunger well enough to help you avoid thinking too much about what they’re made from.

Ignore the squeak… and the whiskers.

entries.name: Steak
entries.description: Sizzling on the grill, there is little that has united middle-aged villagers than a steak seared to perfection. Brynmoor villagers would gather around grills to discuss hunting, village politics and anything else that came to mind, all as an excuse to silently judge the way the current chef prepared this simple meal.

entries.name: Steak 'N' Eggs
entries.description: Some meals require silence. As you chew each mouthful, you reminisce on times past. On loved ones lost. On friends remembered. On moments that bring a smile to your face – simple and uncomplicated, without the weight of the world’s burdens crushing down on you. This is one of those meals.

entries.name: Steak Sandwich
entries.description:
Steak, if you ask me, is infinitely diminished by putting it between two slices of bread. Steak should stand proud on its own, garnished with salt and barely introduced to a flame.

As a journal-writer I can't stop you. My powers are limited to shaming you from the dark recesses of your interfaces.

entries.name: Sweet Veg Ball
entries.description:
Popular among gnomes, this sticky ball of fruits and vegetables is a combination of savoury and sweet that almost feels like it shouldn’t work. Yet it does.

There is a crispness to the outer shell, savoury and salty, which gives way to a delicious fruity sweetness beneath.

Gnomish ambassadors would create large numbers of these sweet treats, piled high on silver platters, to delight visiting dignitaries at lavish receptions. Diplomats would often joke about being spoiled by such treats. Which is ironic really, as these spoil very quickly, so enjoy them now while you can.

entries.name: Vegetable Soup
entries.description: A good soup won’t just fill your stomach, it’ll lift your spirits. Warm and comforting, the taste of home. Popular across all of Gielinor by anyone with a pan and some vegetables.

entries.description: Satisfying, if a little chewy.

entries.name: Wild Pie
entries.description: A delicious pastry crust seals the flavours inside. Warm and filling, each bite designed to fill you with comfort. The flavour is earthy, and rich, letting you shrug off almost anything.

entries.name: Adamant Crossbow
entries.description:
You’ll be pleased to learn, dear adventurer, that the first person to make this crossbow in Ashenfall is, indeed, you… or your friend if there are a few of you around.

The techniques that create them are no different to the previous crossbows, but the wood is sturdier, stronger and capable of sufficiently more damage when wielded with skill.

The Moon Garou are traditionalists, preferring the art of archery in hunting and combat, so why not take this opportunity to show them how much they’re missing out.

entries.name: Adamant Greatsword
entries.description:
Few foes can stand against a great big slab of metal, filed down to the keenest edge. The weight of a great sword applied tremendous pressure across the edge, meaning that victims of a swing tend to find themselves falling to pieces in the face of it… quite literally.

The adamant greatsword is stronger than most blades, with only a handful of other metals offering sturdier construction. It was forged first by the legendary hero, Connakt, a Moon Garou warrior of great regard. Massive was his frame, and so he required a similarly sized blade in battle. He wielded his greatsword in a single hand, terrifying all who stood before him.

Connakt, it is said, travelled beyond the Umbral Sands, and indeed beyond Ashenfall, though the legends on how he did so vary greatly.  They say that he travelled far away, settled down somewhere and had a family.

His greatsword “Sgian ìm” was buried with him.

entries.name: Adamant Helmet
entries.description:
It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages.

Malgo, druid of Guthix, was one of the first to see the worth in adamant. It was an age before dwarves were cursed by Zamorak to be unable to use magic without severe consequence, and Malgo was one of the greatest spellcasters of his people. He joined the ranks of the Guthixian druids, even though - like many dwarves - he was only a follower of Guthix, rather than a worshipper.

He had been called to Ashenfall with Guthix’s expedition, and he joined a small band of explorers heading deeper into the realm. In a time before Kuldra, you might believe the continent safer, but in a place so infused with magic, terrible evils lay in wait.

entries.name: Adamant Logging Axe
entries.description:
As the anima infused them more deeply, the trees of Ashenfall sought ways to create stronger defences against their hated foes – the lumberjacks. Yew trees, hardened after surviving the cruel rays of the sun, developed bark that would shatter lesser axes.

They felt invulnerable. Unbeatable. They could take the time to plan their war against the logging axes, so that they might rise up and strangle the world with their roots. Yet, the lumberjacks had a friend in the earth, and adamantite rose up to aid its allies.

The metal was harder than any before it, and the yew trees didn’t stand a chance, falling to the new weapons in droves.
