entries.name: Adamant Mace
entries.description:
The first adamant mace was not, as you might expect, used for battle. Rather it was a rolling pin used by the ancient matriarch known only as The Crone – a name she chose for herself, thinking it quite funny.

Her baking skills were so dire, that whatever she produced had the consistency of iron and was more durable than steel. So, she required a tool strong enough to fight back against her sturdy pastries. She commissioned a rolling pin of adamant metal, and she used it with great zeal to beat her baked goods into submission.

Though teeth would still shatter against her scones, there was an artistry there that none could deny. So it was that more people would create adamant rolling pins, until an angry chef beat her rude husband to death with it, and the first true adamant mace was born.

After that, Moon Garou would still favour an adamant rolling pin, but many a warrior would bring a mace into battle, just in case they were forced to face up against the crone’s pastries. Which happened more often than is reasonably explainable.

entries.name: Adamant Platelegs
entries.description:
It was the dwarves who first discovered adamant: a metal so strong and powerful that it could turn aside almost any other blade. It was hard to work with and difficult to refine, so it saw little use in the early ages.

Karibdos was the obstacle between the rest of Ashenfall and a slow, defeated, trudge home. Malgo refused to allow the latter. He studied adamant carefully, experimenting with techniques and styles none bothered with before, even infusing it with a little magic. In doing so, he discovered the strength of the material.

When the expedition faced Karibdos again, it was in suits of solid adamant and glistening green blades ready to strike. They fell into the beast’s great maw, but rather than a delicious dwarven meal, Karibdos found its teeth shattering against their armour and its ancient hide torn apart from flashing blades of green metal.

With Karibdos dead and gone, Malgo and his team continued deeper into the region, vanishing into legend. For those who make the desert their home, none have witnessed anything like Karibdos again… though, perhaps, they simply haven’t dug deep enough.

entries.name: Adamant Scimitar
entries.description:
Wherever there is a sea, there are pirates, and the desert sands are a sea of sorts. A contingent of young Moon Garou once created a combination of rats, sails and a dash of magic, to create a sort of sand-ship, which they intended to use in acts of glorious buccaneering across the umbral desert.

They equipped themselves with scimitars of adamant, as it most closely resembled the cutlasses they’d heard about from human stories that had been stolen during the garou wars centuries past.

With eye-patches, golden teeth and an overzealous use of a particular consonant these youths set forth to become legends. Or they would, if their ship hadn’t immediately capsized and their mothers called them all back for tea.

entries.name: Adamant Shield
entries.description:
You may ask yourself what better defence there is than a large sheet of metal between you and your enemy, and the answer will surprise you. Thicker metal.

OK, so that’s not a surprise, I’m sorry. I was just trying to build a little dramatic tension.

The adamant shield is one of the greatest defensive creations available in the Umbral Sands and favoured by any Moon Garou that needs to brave the kalphite hives or the KotHaar territories. Lesser arrows ping harmlessly off them, and weaker blades have been known to shatter against the adamant’s hardness.

Shields are good, everyone should have one.

entries.name: Adamant Sword
entries.description:
It is said that the pen is mightier than the sword, but there are multiple examples where this is proven false. A pen cannot stop another blade. It cannot slay a monster. It can write strongly worded letters, but when have they ever worked?

The Moon Garou know the power of a good sword. They took the metal of the desert, with it’s green hue and unyielding nature and they turned it against the monsters of the sands. Beasts, great and powerful, fell to these weapons, entire legions of deadly creatures cut down in the dunes.

Moon Garou poets carry a sword with them, because words can only cut so deep. For a lasting impression you need a very sharp edge.

entries.name: Adamant Warhammer
entries.description:
A little know tradition among Moon Garou blacksmiths, is to gather up all the bits of scrap metal from their workshops and create from them little figurines. They then sit beneath the shade somewhere, with various paints and turn these tiny creations into little pieces of art.

That was, until, Thraag learned of the game. Thraag was a blacksmith only so much in that he liked seeing metal melt. Something about the glow, the heat and the sheer sturdiness of the cooling metal, filled him with a sense of pride he never put into his personal hygiene.

Reeking like some unholy nightmare, Thraag was never invited to the gatherings of other blacksmiths, and over time the slight of being shunned festered within him, slowly mutating into something nasty.

He crafted a great hammer of pure adamant, sturdier and heavier then any hammer ever crafted before and he brought said hammer to the blacksmith gathering. There are few sights quite so tragic as grown blacksmiths weeping over smashed figurines.

It certainly did nothing to improve Thraag’s social standing.

entries.name: Amulet of Glory
entries.description:
Power, trapped in dragonstone crystal and worn around the neck, that is the essence of this amulet. The facets of the dragonstone refract and refine the enchantments cast upon the item, somehow creating a magical lattice of surprising strength.

Many have tried to create variations of this theme, yet dragonstone proves too fragile a substance for practical use. Once someone attempted to make a dragonstone dagger, to see if they could turn it into a blade of glory, yet they could not find a sufficiently large stone that wasn’t valuable enough to bankrupt a small nation.

One wizard attempted strange alchemical practices to try and forge a staff of pure dragonstone. Alas, not only did he fail to create such a stone, but the magical explosion that resulted from his hubris removed his lab, and all his research, from this plane of reality.

It’s probably a good idea that no one attempt to duplicate his work.

entries.name: Ancestral Leggings
entries.description:
Long ago, there were people in Ashenfall. Not humans, not elves, nor anyone you might remember, but sentient beings with a life, a culture and a civilisation all of their own. No trace of them remains today. 

Within a few years, the Kobalios were all but extinct. The remaining members of their number began to become twisted creatures; pale reflections of their once noble ancestors. Their limbs elongated and their mouths stretched wide, so that they might feast more and more upon the Wellspring’s power.

Soon, only a handful of the Kobalios remained, and they were easy pickings for the dragonkin when Rasthin and her allies arrived. The battle was swift and brutal, for the dragonkin know nothing of mercy. The slothful, greedy Kobalios had long forgotten the spells of their ancestors and therefore lacked any defence against the dragonkin’s weapons.

The last of the Kobalios were obliterated by Rasthin’s strange arcane cannons, and the legacy of their entire species died with them.

Now, all that remains are a handful of robes cut in the style of the Kobalios. A poor legacy for a once proud people.

entries.name: Black Dragonhide Body
entries.description:
The scales of a black dragon are sturdy things, capable of deflecting all but the strongest attacks. It’s not so much that they’re harder than other scales, but that the creature that bore them is so determined to survive that that tenacity passes on to one who wears it.

There were a few garou hunters that were skilled enough to challenge a black dragon, but only one was ever strong enough to skin an entire one and wear its scales as armour. Her name was Scathach, and she was the very model of garou savagery.

She wielded a great spear and, where other garou would sneak, she would leap, proudly, into battle against the dragons, to prove that the garou were just as deadly as the dragons, if not more so.

When her spear pierced the heart of a mighty dragon, she would let out a howl that would terrify even the bravest of souls.

entries.description:

Scathach wore armour forged from the scales of her victims, and necklaces of their teeth dangled around her neck. She walked bravely among the dragons, because she knew that none would dare challenge her as she wore the skin of their kin.

Her confidence won the attention of Kuldra. Impressed with the garou’s skill, strength and sheer audacity, Kuldra granted her a drop of her blood, elevating Scathach above both her kin and the dragons she challenged.

It was this blood that would cause Scathach’s betrayal, because the remnants of the moon goddess, Lougrim, whispered within Kuldra’s blood and urged Scathach to turn on her mistress.

Sadly, her betrayal was short-lived, and stands as a warning to all other garou not to attempt the same foolish plan.

entries.name: Bow of Elidinis
entries.description:
She is known by many names, both here and in the deserts entire oceans apart from one another, yet to all of them she is a source of life and creation. She is the river in the desert sands, from which all civilisation blooms, and she is the rain that washes away the cruel and merciless when the monsoon season comes.

To the Moon Garou she is the River Mother, the Moon Maiden and their salvation. For it was she, who helped the wandering garou to step away from their primal predatory nature, and tame the sands, cultivating crops and building cities.

She left the deserts centuries ago, to places unknown. Some say she wanders the stars in search of a place where her grief can be lessened. While others claim she prepares for war against a more insidious foe. A creature of fire, ash and hatred, the demon of the sun.

This bow was left to one of her favourite Moon Garou, a warrior called Kyter, whom she had raised as her own after he was orphaned by a cruel sandstorm. The bow was passed down his family line, parent to child, until the last of the bloodline was murdered by Fuzan.

Now, the bow is yours. Use it wisely, for she will surely be annoyed if you don’t.

entries.name: Desert Hood
entries.description:
The desert is a cruel and unforgiving place, and that was before Fuzan corrupted the sun against it. Dry air, filled with sand particles, leech all moisture from the body, leaving you dehydrated, exhausted and with no respite in view. Oases can be mirages, tricks played by the dunes to lure you deeper into your own destruction. These robes help to limit some of the desert’s power, through ancient tricks learned by those who have dwelled within the dunes for generations.

The hood is the most basic necessity of the desert. It shields the top of one’s head from the sun’s cruel ministrations, acting as a barrier between sunstroke and you. The hood also helps protect against particulates of sand that have been stirred up by meagre breezes.

The overhanging fabric shields the eyes from the light, just a little. A tiny point of shade in a glaring light that’s almost crushing in its brightness.

Finally, they’re surprisingly fashionable, everyone should try one.

entries.name: Desert Net
entries.description: Desert waters throws up some interesting challenges for a net. There are fish that like to nestle into the sand, both below the surface and where a net would not usually reach. To counter this problem, a desert net is weighted on one side but not the other. The weighted side trawls the sandy floor, while the unweighted side catches the fish that attempt to get away. It does lead to some unwanted catches - be prepared to find a wealth of bones in the Umbral Sands - but that's testament to how effective it is.

Robes are freeing, allowing the body to breathe and allowing moisture to evaporate, cooling you down. They’re also easy to brush down, expelling sand that has crept its way into all the most uncomfortable parts.

This desert outfit was apparently passed down to the Moon Garou by the River Mother, who brought the lessons she had learned from her own deserts with her. She taught them how to craft them, how to fold the patterns for best effect and she taught the Moon Garou how to dance in them.

On rare festivals, the Moon Garou will attach ribbons, bells and obsidian glass shards to their robes. When they dance it creates a glorious swirling medley of colour, sound and glittering sparkles.

entries.name: Dragon Full Helm
entries.description:
Only the dragonkin know the process to create true dragon armour. Others can perhaps manipulate the base metal, orikalkum, but they lack something in the process that turns the metal into true dragon metal, a far stronger source. In aeons past, on their original world, dragon armour was worn by the Ortius Chen, the mighty warriors of what was once a great dragonkin army.

In the revision before, this army swept across worlds subjugating the other races, few in number as they were. The other races were weaker, smaller, and less self-aware, a trait that made them perfect to work in dragonkin mines. There life was harsh, cruel and often short, and the dragonkin masters had little sense of pity.

All, save one.

Nastralla was a seer whose visions pierced the flow of time and allowed them to witness the entire lifespan of the dragonkin’s cruelty. They saw worlds before dragonkin invasion and the worlds after and they found it abhorrent. They were not alone.

entries.name: Dragon Kiteshield
entries.description: A five-headed dragon and a hidden island took spot #1 and #2 respectively, but the presence of dragon metal was the third most surprising thing that Zilyana found on Ashenfall. Dragon metal meant a sequence of things to the icyene. It meant that the dragonkin had not only lived here, but lived here long enough to create their own dragons and combine their dragonfire with orikalkum. She noted it as something that she wanted to investigate further - once the malevolent dragon-queen was stopped, of course.

entries.name: Dragonfire Shield
entries.description:
Fuzan was the youngest of Kuldra’s offspring, yet one of her most violent. As a child he was overcome with a curiosity infused with childlike cruelty. When Kuldra gifted him with the flames, stolen from the Dragonkin’s Harmonic Resonator, it did nothing to temper that childlike need to discover and destroy.

The fires within him were a delight to wield and he grew more and more focused on their flickering flames, one day glancing through them to worlds of cinders that lay beyond. In the embers he heard a whisper, and as he listened it turned into a promise and a proclamation. A voice of true divinity, far surpassing the power of his mother’s dimmed spark.

She was a queen of worlds far beyond this one, each of them shining beacons in the dark twilight of the heavens and Fuzan was enraptured. Through her instruction he learned to mark others with his seal, sharing some of his power with them, and in turn, some of hers.

Now, with his destruction, you wield the flames yourself. A shield protecting you from her manipulation. Yet, should you stare too closely at the flames that burn within this shield, you might find yourself blinded by divine radiance.

entries.name: Dragonslayer's Cape
entries.description:
A seer once dreamed about brave warriors who walked across Ashenfall in another time. An age both past and present, where the rules of the world were different. These great heroes challenged and slew an echo of Velgar, saving a land that never was. 
While the seer’s memory of that dream fades with each passing moment, she was able to embroider the event into a cape, so that all might know of these legends from another time.

entries.name: Enchanted Rune Bolt
entries.description: You can argue the semantics, but rune is already enchanted. It has inherent magical properties, which means that 'enchanting' it is a complicated process. It's like cursing a spell, or summoning a rune: you're just smooshing magic together and hoping nothing bad happens. And, as the Wise Old Man says, 'hoping nothing bad happens is basically inviting the bad into your bedchambers'. We'd have worded it differently, but you get the idea.

entries.name: Gilded Paladin Legs
entries.description:
All that glitters is gold, is factually inaccurate but a fun song lyric. However, golden armour is most certainly glittering. Forged from gold bars, melted down and refined into plate armour, there are few who can deny the sheer audaciousness of an outfit like this.

Needless to say, the fate of Sir Leigh is entirely predictable. Even though his armour lacked the gemstones of his sovereign, it was still armour forged from solid gold. This meant that not only did it lack the defensive capabilities of sturdier metal, but it also meant that every opponent went straight for him.

He was torn to shreds, and his armour sold off in pieces.

His sacrifice, however, did save the king’s life. After witnessing the horrid destruction of his most loyal commander, the king decided that future battles would be waged in steel armour… very very thick steel armour… and, preferably, from very far away.

entries.name: Infinity Robe Body
entries.description:
Garou druids borrow from nature when crafting staves or weaving robes. In Ghornfell they took antlers from deer, and leather from their hunted prey. In the Umbral Sands they were forced to adopt a… sparklier approach.

Parts of the kalphites, most notably their wings, were a scintillating spectrum of beautiful colours. As they caught the sunlight, they would bloom into a radiant rainbow of delight and Karia found herself overcome with a strange sort of envy previously unknown to her people.

She wanted to sparkle. She wanted to shine. She wanted to live a life encased in the most magnificent and wondrous colours, and she would do anything to make it happen.

To call the events that followed a war would be an over-exaggeration, but not wholly inaccurate. The garou descended on the hives with blade, claw and bow, ready to tear the beasts apart so that they might claim the colourful materials for themselves. The kalphite, of course, did not fall easily and many garou lives were lost in the clothing-mad conflict.

The garou descended on the hives with blade, claw and bow, ready to tear the beasts apart so that they might claim the colourful materials for themselves. The kalphite, of course, did not fall easily and many garou lives were lost in the clothing-mad conflict.

entries.name: Infinity Robe Hat
entries.description:
Garou druids borrow from nature when crafting staves or weaving robes. In Ghornfell, they took antlers from deer, and leather from their hunted prey. In the Umbral Sands they were forced to adopt a… sparklier approach.

Kaira, druid of the Softfoot tribe, was one of the first of the Moon Garou to hunt through the sands in search of materials they could use to craft robes of their own. They expected magnificent beasts with scales and horns the likes of which they had never seen. They found the kalphites instead.

Their first interaction did not go well.

As the storm approached, the buzzing sound grew to a crescendo as the great kalphite swarm blotted out the stars and moon, descending upon the village.

There were none left alive once all had passed.

entries.name: Kalphite Carapace Chest
entries.description:
Perhaps it’s a little strange to wear the skin of your enemy, but who am I to judge? The Kalphite are certainly an imposing bunch and donning armour comprising of the most resilient parts of them certainly hits that survival game vibe, even if it is a little grim.

The shell of a Kalphite is strong and durable, a thick layer between them and the rest of the world. It keeps them safe, yes, but closed off from sensation and feeling, an emotional gulf between them and everyone else.

Fortunately, they’re insects and couldn’t care any less.

You, at least, are in possession of vocal chords and the ability to interact with others. You can also take off your armour,  should you ever need to—something not recommended in the middle of battle, no matter how much you’d like to improve your emotional bond with something.

It is worth noting, however, that there is an unexpected side effect to this armour. Dragons find you extra crunchy.

entries.description:
Perhaps it’s a little strange to wear the skin of your enemy, but who am I to judge? The Kalphite are certainly an imposing bunch and donning armour comprising of the most resilient parts of them certainly hits that survival game vibe, even if it is a little grim.

Once you hollow out the squishy parts of the Kalphite and rearrange the plates to better fit the human form, the carapace helmet is more comfortable than it might first seem.

Seen through the eyes of the Kalphite the world is a fractured place. Multifaceted eyes see the world in strange and wonderful ways, their vision split among multiple different views, yet never obsessing over a singular image. You lose the finest details to focus on the bigger picture, a trait perhaps more of us need in our lives.

Kalphites are well adapted to the sands, they spread their weight out across all six legs, allowing them to move across the sands with relative ease. They can move fast too, something Moon Garou hunters discover all too late.

entries.name: Keris
entries.description:
The Moon Garou believe this weapon was given to them by a goddess of the river, who took the desperate garou and raised them up to become masters of the desert sands. The weapon was created as a  tool against one of the deadliest denizens of the dunes – the kalphites.

The blade tip can find its way through the chinks in the Kalphite exoskeleton, piercing through the chitinous armour and damaging the much squishier flesh beneath. It was turned many a battle against the Kalphites from a garou bloodbath, to a garou victory banquet – though they  tend to find the Kalphite meat a little less appetising then they’d like.

Moon Garou champions are gifted the Keris dagger after achieving a great victory. It is a symbol of their bravery and marks them as skilled warriors to all the other tribes. In olden times, a bearer of the Keris would be treated with great respect. They would be given food, lodging and anything else they needed to further their victories.

Nowadays, however, the Keris is seen more as a tool of survival against the insectoid foe.

entries.name: Lunar Garou Robe Legs
entries.description:
Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wears these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician.

A Moon Garou shaman must walk the deserts before they can be truly considered magi in their own right. They wander, explore and contemplate the loneliness of the sands as they do so.

Some hear voices, believing them to be ancestors, deities, spirits or just their own internal monologue trying to dull the silence.  Others find a profound calm in the silence, many choosing to live a quiet life in return.

Others, find monsters. There are many shamans who report that they did battle with the terrible demons creeping out from Dowdun Reach. Others battled kalphites, KotHaar or even dragons. One claims to have battled a creature that rose out of smoke, whimpering and wailing as it went, and it left the shaman’s mind shattered in return.

Yet, no matter how far the shamans wander, eventually they all found their way home, enlightened and enriched, and ready to serve their people.

entries.name: Lunar Garou Robes
entries.description:
Garou magic is not born of runes, but of their connection to the moon, the stars and the spirits within them. Moon Garou shamans dance in the moonlight, with the glittering moon sprites swirling around them in mystical threads that help to reshape reality. Magic is sacred, spiritual and serene. Shamans wears these robes so that the tribe may know to call on them for spiritual aid, both magical and personal, as the shamans act as counsel as much as magician.

These robes are only given to a shaman after completing three mystic trials. The first is a trial of contemplation, where each applicant is given a complicated riddle to solve and three nights in which to do so. During that time they are allowed no forms of communication, and must rely purely on their ability to contemplate the words and arrive at a solution. The answers to the riddle are rarely set in stone: it is the interpretation that matters.

The second is a trial of compassion, and they are never warned of this one in advance. Indeed the trial may have happened before the applicant even entered into training. They could be tested at any point in their lives. It’s a simple trial: the applicant at some point finds someone in need and how they go about helping, or not helping them, is noted for the trial. This weeds out the cruel people pretending to be shamans, and encourages an attitude of compassion in potential applicants.

The final trial is the hardest of all, the trial of creativity. Here the applicants are given time to study magic, its forms, its methods and its malleability. To complete this trial, the applicant must create a new spell, enchantment or other form of magic, that has never been seen before. This trial has led to some of the most beautiful discoveries… and some of the most terrifying.

entries.name: Master's Staff
entries.description:
Before the master wand, there was a staff of such power that the mages of the wizard’s tower decided it was too dangerous to keep. They placed the staff in teleportation circle, scrambled the coordinates and hurled it through the Abyss to settle far away from Misthalin.

In truth, it should have ended in the depths of the sea, sinking down and down into the darkness, but something caught it instead.

A powerful elven mage had found their way to Ashenfall, and they had already indulged in powers darker than what their kin traditionally allowed. They felt the staff hurtling through the Abyss and used their unnatural sorcery to pull it to them, so that they might benefit from its power.

This elf and his retinue found their way to the Umbral Sands, where they challenged one of the Moon Garou’s mages to a magical duel, over some perceived slight or other. The battle was magnificent, power that shook the dunes and cast a great sandstorm into the skies. The garou was defeated, but not before her spells shattered the master’s staff.

In his arrogance he cast the remains aside and continued his journey into Ashenfall.  Moon Garou would find the remnants of the staff and found a way to recreate it. Weaker than the original, true, but still possessing a power that would make lesser mages tremble.

entries.name: Obsidian Cape
entries.description:
Once this cape was part of the shell of a KotHaar you’d befriended - Zi. It sounds cruel to wear the skin of one’s friend, but the KotHaar do not have flesh like you and I sometimes do, instead they wrap themselves in layers of magma and obsidian, until they have a strong enough form to move around in.

What a KotHaar really is, is a tiny fragment of the creature you see. They are the core, a mote of consciousness that can be crushed down and down to a surprisingly small size. Their carapace, what we might call this body, is almost irrelevant to them, in the grand scheme of things. They feel no pain, no loss when it is taken from them, so don’t be too sad about your weird little friend giving you theirs.

Wear the skin of your friend with pride, adventurer! They would love nothing more than to know that at least part of them is joining you on your adventures.

entries.name: Obsidian Chest
entries.description:
The KotHaar do not die as we do. There is no afterlife for them, just silence. They are reduced to fragments of obsidian, crushed down and down with the weight of their souls. Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait.

There is a common misconception that the KotHaar are a hive mind. Certainly many of them work as if they are one, but they are bound by a shared purpose, not a shared consciousness. This is a distinction that other races struggle with regularly, but it is easily understood when, as inevitably happens once in a while, one of the KotHaar turns away from their intended purpose and dares to wonder what else could be.

There are a few stories, hidden in the deserts, of KotHaar explorers found doing various things. They might spend days staring at a cactus, or they might dig through a mountainside to see what’s inside.

Perhaps this chest armour, that you now wear, might once have dreamed of being something other than its purpose. Now, perhaps, that dream has come true.

entries.name: Pharaoh's Sceptre
entries.description:
The Moon Garou tried the whole Pharaoh concept exactly once. Unused to non-violent systems of government, they gathered together as a people and pulled stones from a bag to decide who was the luckiest of all of them, and therefore who deserved to rule.

It was, as you can imagine, not a smart system of governance.

The winner was a garou called Hakanaten, and he did not want the job. He had always been an outsider, far more interested with the goings on of the nearby Kalphite hives then he was with the goings on of the city. Still, he had been chosen by an assumption of destiny and was set upon a throne with crown and sceptre in hand.

He hated it. He made decisions as best he could, but could never please everyone. If he tried to help one person, it angered another. If he cast judgement on a lawbreaker, he was deemed cruel by some and weak by others. No matter what he tried, he only found himself more and more isolated from his kin.

In the end a revolt saw him deposed and the throne destroyed. He was cast into the hive he so adored, where he was expected not to live for long. Yet, he had studied the hive and he could mimic their behaviours better than some of his own people’s. He helped them dig tunnels. He joined them on hunts. He lived a life far happier among the hive then he ever did at home.

The sceptre, that had been cast down with him, carries with it a measure of his fondness for the insects. It is said that anyone who wields it, can call on the hive for aid, in memory of an unlucky monarch.

entries.name: Red Dragonhide Body
entries.description:
A garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour.

Dragons are not pets. They’re violent creatures, prone to random acts of aggression, driven by a rage that burns in their very soul. Still, Mayev was patient and she lured the dragon hatchling away from the corpse of its parent and out into the desert sands. Moonlight transformed the desert from gold to glittering silver, yet the ruby-red scales of the dragon seemed brighter than before.

Over the days, weeks and months to come, she kept the dragon secret. She brought it scraps of food, and kept it company on lonely days, and it came to see her not as a parent, not as a master, but as a friend. She saw him as the same. She named him Vakar – the flame-wrought song – and they would hunt together.

Over time, they knew each other’s strengths and could balance out their weaknesses. They hunted stronger prey, earning the respect of her tribe with the offcuts. Life was set to be everything they had both dreamed – until they met the KotHaar, and it all turned to ash.

entries.description:

As a cub, Mayev was never one to stay in one place. She ran round and round the caravans without a care in the world, always bringing the frustration and ire of her elder. “Be still!” were the words she heard first thing in the morning. “Be quiet!” the command she heard each night before bed. Yet, stillness and silence were as alien a concept to her as the magic of the druids - something far out of her reach.

One day, she left her camp in search of wild adventure, much to the chagrin of the camp guards. She risked the harsh sunlight of the dunes, clinging to shadows, exploring caves and passages revealed by the passing sandstorm of the day. Each morning her world was different, new paths appeared while familiar ones were hidden, and on this day she found a cavern deep underground.

There she found a red dragon, breathing her last breath, and the hatchling beside her breathing his first.

One day, she left her camp in search of wild adventure, much to the chagrin of the camp guards. She risked the harsh sunlight of the dunes, clinging to shadows, exploring caves and passages revealed by the passing sandstorm of the day. Each morning her world was different, new paths appeared while familiar ones were hidden, and on this day she found a cavern deep underground.

There she found a red dragon, breathing her last breath, and the hatchling beside her breathing his first.

entries.name: Rune Barbed Arrow
entries.description: Possibly the cruelest use of runite is making barbed arrows. The metal applies a force against anything that tries to touch it, which makes removing a barbed arrow painful. You are just as likely to send it further into the wound than remove it. Some areas of Ashenfall banned their usage a long time ago, but that won't be a consideration if you're fighting Kuldra.

entries.name: Rune Greataxe
entries.description:
It may surprise, but there was once a Garou King in Kuldra's Tower. Kuldra, perhaps fearful of a mutiny (or having to kill everyone who mutinied, diminishing her forces), allowed the various troops to keep their customs. That included the Rite of the Moon, where garou would challenge each other for the privilege of becoming the King. Her initial belief was that, if the garou were content on challenging each other rather than her, then it would be the best for all involved.

That ended with King Rí Túath. Rí Túath had delusions of something beyond grandeur. He claimed to have been visited by Lougrim, who had crawled out of Kuldra's gullet while she was sleeping. According to Rí Túath, Lougrim was a prisoner in the belly of Kuldra, and it was the job of the Garou to recover her. He led a contingent of garou against a sleeping Kuldra, and carved into her skin with a rune greataxe. 

In a sense, King Rí Túath achieved his aim. He made it inside Kuldra, and did, in fact, find Lougrim. It didn't happen in the way that he might have wanted, and he certainly wasn't alive for any of those steps.

Kuldra was quick to deny the garou the Rite of the Moon after King Rí Túath.

entries.name: Rune Logging Axe
entries.description: To a tree, a human with a rune logging axe is their final boss. You are the ultimate test; the nemesis that they have been training for. They have been stretching their branches and aggressively photosynthesising for this moment. They have been fantastising about taking you down, so that they can be talked about in groves for centuries. 'The Lumberjack Ripper', they think. 'That's what they will call me.'

entries.name: Rune Platebody
entries.description:
It is perhaps fitting that the first pieces of rune equipment were worn by the creator of runes themselves, Guthix. Of course, rune metal is not made of runes, and indeed has no actual connection to runes at all, but Guthix, for all his many qualities, was not the greatest of wordsmiths.

Luminite, somehow, limited the metal’s reaction to other metals, but only within the smelting phase. It allowed the construction of bars, which in turn allowed the construction of plates which could be fitted together to form armour.

It took several weeks, for Guthix’s blacksmithing skills had long fallen to atrophy, but the god was able to fashion himself a full suit of rune metal. Just in time for the Dweller to attack.

entries.description:

The Dweller was a beast that had nestled into the Wellspring and the energies had transformed it into something more than it was. What had previously been nothing but an unpleasantly large arthropod, was now a great lumbering beast full of hunger and fury. The anima had twisted it into something resembling the colossi and it roared out of the Wellspring straight for the god of balance.

Yet, for all his desires for a peaceful existence, Guthix had the warrior’s heart and he was more than a match for the Dweller. Though the battle shattered mountains and diverted rivers, the Dweller soon found itself sliced in twain by the god’s terrible sword.

He cast the body into the deepest depths of the ocean, in fear that it might one day return.

entries.name: Skills Necklace
entries.description:
Not all magic is focused on the obliteration of one’s enemies; though many would argue that’s where the fun lies. No, magic can also improve the rest of one’s life in similarly impressive ways.

This necklace, favoured by artisans, miners, lumberjacks and similar, is an example of such magic. The enchantment is simple, it enhances ones luck. When swinging at a rock, you have a higher chance of finding that weak seam. If cutting down a tree, the forces acting on your cuts make it easier to fell it. You are a little luckier in your endeavours and therefore get better results.

In the Wizard’s  Tower this has caused no end of arguments. Luck, isn’t a thing. It’s not a law of creation, nor a principle on which the measured universe runs. Cause has Effect. Doing one action creates an outcome, a different action another. Luck, whilst popular with the layperson, isn’t something that can be measured or refined, it’s simply coincidence, nothing more.

Yet, this necklance proves that it must be a thing. Even though it can’t be. Therefore this little trinket has been the source of some of the longest, loudest and most violent debates for decades.

entries.name: Yew Shortbow
entries.description:
Moon Garou scouts scour the desert armed with these bows. The sands obscure much until you’re right on top of it and so these bows are often more useful than the longer ranged weapons, against the dangers of the desert.

In the camps, the eldest garou will often teach the young cubs how to handle a shortbow. They will have the youngsters unleash a volley of arrows at clay pots, straw dolls, or cacti, and help train them to fire with greater accuracy.

Many of the young cubs will keep the shortbow with them as they grow into adulthood, using it as a decorative piece in their home  -- a sign of a youth well spent, and a reminder that nothing lasts forever.

entries.name: Abraxus Ring
entries.description:
Little is known about the great necromancer, Abraxus, a fact he finds deeply frustrating. In his youth he sought secrets forbidden to others and he wandered the Whispering Swamps of Brynmoor in search of secrets that others dared not know. The swamp was ancient and haunted, so the legends went, and there was a magic to it that was different to any other part of Ashenfall. He explored vaults, caves and battled goblins in the mists, but never found the power that his youth demanded. Until one day, he found the smoke that promised him the power he so desperately craved. 

From there his history is clouded, obscured just as the mist obscured the swamps. He founded a small order of necromancers in Fellhollow and took advantage of the chaos when the Withering began. He sought to bind the souls of the dead into his service, gaining power just as Imaru gained hers from the consumption of the fallen. 

But Abraxus was no dragon, and so frustratingly mortal. A single hoplite spear is all it took to end his life, he would have been embarrassed if he felt it had mattered. As a spirit he lost a lot of things we take for granted, sensation, corporeality, and many of the emotions that everyone else enjoys. Yet, in exchange, he was given the most precious gift of all – time. Time to contemplate. Time to scheme. Time to think about what really matters, in the grand scheme of it all, and he has found his answer. 

His ring, imbued with his dark power, offers no value to him any more. So he bequeaths it to you. In time, perhaps, it may help you become a mage strong enough to earn his respect. Well, a small fraction of it, at least.

entries.name: Inspiring Amulet of Magic
entries.description:
It is perhaps not surprising that wizard’s made use of magical jewellery as early as possible. Indeed the first few pieces worn on Ashenfall were little more than decoration, and gaudy wizards would attempt to outdo one another with shinier and shinier pieces.

As part of their ever increasing “prank war” wizards began to create jewellery that was enchanted with effects designed to frustrate, or otherwise hinder, the wearer, believing that enchantments in jewellery were little more than silly trinkets. One mage created what she assumed was an auditory illusion, within an amulet, the intention being that when the wearer would try and cast a spell, the jewellery would play an annoying earworm tune, distracting the poor caster.

This did not happen. Something about the threads of magic, the structure of the crystal and the concealing spell that was intended to hide the prank, created something unique. Instead of making it harder to cast spell, the wearers found it easier. Understanding came faster, spells and incantations clearer than before.

What was intended to distract instead focused the wearer, allowing them to concentrate in ways they had never been able to before.

entries.name: Ravanna's Ring
entries.description:
Hate can be a powerful tool. It forges and it destroys with equal might. Grudges can last generations, well beyond the lifespans of those first slighted, and vengeance… vengeance can be eternal.

Ravanna knew this well. She stoked her hatred and turned it into a weapon. She wrapped it around her soul like a cage and unleashed the power of it into the very sky over the Highlands. A storm, driven by grief, rage and unfettered loathing, turned the clouds into agents of her vengeance and as they writhe, rage and hate, they build static charge that they unleash upon the garou that live below.

This ring was on her finger when Ulv died, and it became infused with that same hatred. At first it only turned its rage against the garou, but the problem with hate is that it festers and mutates into something worse. Everything is to blame for Ulv’s death. Every plant, every rock, every movement of the stars, they all led up to that moment and so the ring hates them too, and now it seeks, in its own small way, to take revenge upon the world.

entries.name: Ring of Life
entries.description:
Harold has a job for you and won’t let something as trivial as your expired mortality get in the way. This piece of enchanted jewellery is primed to go off when you’re about to land on Death’s list, whisking you away to safety before the scythe needs to be swung.

There are many sorcerers that have studied these rings for years, going slowly mad as they try to uncover the secrets of immortality. If they could just learn the methods by which this ring operates, then they could extend their lives indefinitely.

Only one wizard ever actually learned this secret, but he forgot the method by which this ring works, for it teleports you at the moment of your death. As the ring does not stop the aging process, this unfortunate mage now spends his eternity in perpetual teleportation – hurled through the abyss, never to take form again.

entries.name: Ring of Pursuit
entries.description:
Hunters have always needed an edge, and this ring is just that. It enhances a hunter’s senses and quietens their movements. Their prey becomes less wary of them, and more vulnerable to attack.

The garou were particularly fond of these rings, and during the few years of peace between the humans of Bramblemead and the garou of Ghornfell, villagers could barter these trinkets for far more than they were worth to other villagers.

entries.name: Ring of Recoil
entries.description:
Vengeance isn’t a dish best served cold, but one served quickly. Whilst taking years to enact the cruellest retaliation might work in the civilised world, in the wilds of Ashenfall a quick strike is far more valuable.

This ring was first created by one of the Amalgamated, worn as both deterrence and for some small satisfaction when they were targeted by vigilante mobs. It didn’t prevent the bruises, or fix the broken bones, but their assailants attacks would end much more quickly when they discovered they weren’t as untouchable as they thought.

entries.name: Salve Amulet
entries.description:
The name is a bit of a misnomer, since this amulet has very little to do with the river Salve. Instead its name refers to the crystal that traditionally sits at the heart. This crystal was first brought to the region by Saradominist priests, some time in the third age. They had harvested it from a cave near the river Salve and found ways to cultivate on Ashenfall’s soil, by utilising the natural magic infusing everything.

Sanctified by faith and magic, this amulet was deadly to the undead, and the dragonkin Lacrussa was fascinated with the properties. She stole the recipe for its creation and hid it within her vault, long before the withering curse spread over Fellhollow. Instead she had delved too deeply in her own experiments and discovered something buried within the earth that would twist and reanimate the dead.

This amulet allowed her to hold the forces back and keep them from overrunning her lab. That was, until, she met her end at Kuldra’s fangs.

entries.name: Ash Rod
entries.description:
Ah, the ash rod. It's been here from the First Age, and will be here for many Ages to come. Ever-reliable, and gets the job done. Line up all the tools in the world and the ash rod will likely be named the most productive and certainly the most loved. 

All hail rod ash!

entries.name: Berry Drizzle Pan-Seared Fish
entries.description:
"Pan-seared what?", you may ask. Well, pan-seared herring and anchovies, my good fellow. That might sound like a lot of fish in one meal, but some dwellberry acts as a sweet binding agent, making the whole eating-process rather delightful. It's a meal that's been around for generations, and you will often hear battle-worn adventurers wishing that they were back home for 'some of mammy's pan-seared'. 

We suspect that the berry drizzle pan-seared that you've made is NOT from mammy, however. We may be wrong: it's very possible that there's a quest that we've forgotten.

entries.name: Braised Armoured Catfish
entries.description:
Cooking a braised catfish is no mean feat. The process involves removing the armoured shell while managing to avoid the nerve-endings that, once severed, can release a poison that is fatal to humans. Then a chef needs to achieve precisely the right temperature to neutralise the latent poison without - again - activating it. 

Of course, if you want fewer friends, braised catfish is easy as pie to cook.

entries.name: Braised Undead Eel
entries.description:
Sweet Saradomin on High, why on earth are you braising an undead eel? Are you a mind rune short of a rune pouch?

Perhaps it's a dare, and you're going to get a hefty payout after making it? I can't think of any other reason, sane or otherwise, why you would fish for the horrible, wriggly thing, pick it up afterwards, then braise it, which - we may add - is a process to DRAW OUT FLAVOURS. 

What next? Bury it in the ground for days and eat it afterwards? I would not put it past you.
pages:
Sweet Saradomin on High, why on earth are you braising an undead eel? Are you a mind rune short of a rune pouch?

Perhaps it's a dare, and you're going to get a hefty payout after making it? I can't think of any other reason, sane or otherwise, why you would fish for the horrible, wriggly thing, pick it up afterwards, then braise it, which - we may add - is a process to DRAW OUT FLAVOURS. 

What next? Bury it in the ground for days and eat it afterwards? I would not put it past you.

entries.name: Bronze Leaf
entries.description: If you want to prettify some jewellery or clothing, there's nothing quite like leaf filigree. It makes you realise that nature really knows what it is doing. Everywhere you look, we've embellished our craftmanship with stuff from nature: animal feet on the legs of furniture, animal-skin rugs, carved foliage on bigger units. There really is no better muse than Mother Nature.

entries.name: Coarse Net
entries.description:
Pity the poor shrimp or lobster, approaching the final moments of its life, only to find themselves in a coarse net. The snobbish among them might look down their antennae and think 'couldn't it have been a wool net, perhaps, or linen?'. 

We're inclined to agree with them. They have minutes before they get cooked in a pot, yet they don't receive the simple courtesy of a comfy net. When you're on your deathbed, we'll wrap you up in a coarse net and see how you like it.

entries.name: Dowdun Reach Cape
entries.description:
The Dowdun Reach Cape is an emblem of your complete and utter mastery of Dowdun Reach. Congratulations.

You've seen things people wouldn't believe. You've attacked lesser blue dragons while on fire on the battlements. You've watched the Dreaming Stone glitter in the darkness near Dowdun Reach gate. All of these moments will get washed out, in time, like a wet cape in rain.

entries.name: Dried Giant Krill
entries.description: Did you know that, for a short period in the First Age, time was once measured in Krill Hours? If watches existed back then, you would have been able to set it by the migratory patterns of krill. The dominant shoal would take precisely one hour to pass from one side of Bramblemead Valley, round Temple Woods, to the other side of Bramblemead.  Children would often try to match their speeds, attempting to see who could notch up the greatest KH (krill hours).

entries.name: Eggs Royale
entries.description:
Do you know what they call an eggs royale in Asgarnia? 'Salmon and egg'. Barbarians.

There aren't many flavours that go together as well as salmon and egg. Pork and cheese. Bread and butter. Fishing potions and a hangover.

entries.name: Feather Bait
entries.description: Some fish are drawn to feathers, something about the colours and the way the water dances around them, it’s almost hypnotic to them.

entries.name: Feathered Lure
entries.description: Sometimes a feather alone isn’t enough, there must be flavour as well. Delicious, sticky, berry juice is pressed into this lure, so that the taste of it might spread through the water and attract the attention of fish with fruitier palettes.

entries.name: Fine Net
entries.description:
Oooh, look at you, making a fine net. Lah-di-dah. 

I bet you're the kind to make a net and never use it. You just drape it on your side-table at dinner parties, so people can compliment it and ask where you fish. "Oh you know, here and there", you say, idly gesturing to a mounted bass on your wall (bought from a shop). But we see you, fisher-dandy. We see you very well.

entries.name: Fish Fry
entries.description:
A 'fish fry' is something of a misnomer as only the eel is a fish, and even that's questionable now that it's undead. The lobster is most definitely a crustacean, and a cabbage is a holy orb of sustenance, delivered by the majestic Brassica Prime. Therefore, not a fish.

We give a fish fry a pass, mainly because it's a Fellhollow delicacy, once favoured by Ravanna. It was invented after a sailor saw a lobster and eel fighting and threw a well-aimed cabbage. He fried the result and lo, fish fry was born.

entries.description: You're a fishing colossus, conquering rivers and seas with nowt but your net and rod.

entries.name: Focused Agility Potion
entries.description: While under the effects of a strong enough agility potion, everything becomes a shortcut. You'll see branches over paths and wonder if you might swing ahead. Rivers are there to be jumped over; mountains to be scrabbled up. Just make sure you've got enough dosage to fully complete the shortcut. Running out halfway up a rockface can be a pain.

entries.name: Fried Salmon
entries.description:
Fried salmon may not be the most substantial or healing of fish, but it's celebrated for its moist texture and delicious taste.

Famously, it was the subject of a smear campaign from the Saradominist church to get it banned as a foodstuff, as they objected to the populace describing it as 'moist'. They deemed the adjective 'unsaintly'.

entries.name: Giant Krill Bait
entries.description: The vile ashes imbedded within these strange fishing lures, whisper to the most sinful part of the fish, drawing them to their demise. At least that’s what the Zamorakian mages claimed. In truth, they were simply tastier and more desirable to the fish, who have little concept of morality.

entries.name: Gold Leaf
entries.description: Fashion is often described as circular, turning from modish to outmoded and back again. Or it's portrayed like waves, as fads come and go, never to be seen again.

entries.name: Golden Bloodblight Cape
entries.description: Fast AND able to survive the poisoned swamps? You're a walking humblebrag. You couldn't hop into Bramblemead and get me some Undead Twigs for the Animal Magnetism quest, could you?
pages: Fast AND able to survive the poisoned swamps? You're a walking humblebrag. You couldn't hop into Bramblemead and get me some Undead Twigs for the Animal Magnetism quest, could you?

entries.name: Golden Bramblemead Cape
entries.description: If you're going to master an area, why not Bramblemead? Lovely sights, and slightly less dragon-filled than the rest of Ashenfall. You might have to leapfrog the odd goblin, but we've all done that.

entries.name: Golden Dowdun Reach Cape
entries.description: Considering that Black Knights are some of the least nimble warriors in all of Ashenfall (it's the clunky black armour), you might be the most agile person to set foot in the Reach. Congratulations!
pages: Considering that Black Knights are some of the least nimble warriors in all of Ashenfall (it's the clunky black armour), you might be the most agile person to set foot in the Reach. Congratulations!

entries.name: Golden Fellhollow Cape
entries.description: Withering? What Withering? When you're moving as fast as you, the Withering hasn't got a hope of catching up.
pages: Withering? What Withering? When you're moving as fast as you, the Withering hasn't got a hope of catching up.

entries.name: Golden Fractured Cape
entries.description: When you're faster than a garou in their homeland, you know that you've won some kind of evolutionary jackpot. Congratulations!
pages: When you're faster than a garou in their homeland, you know that you've won some kind of evolutionary jackpot. Congratulations!

entries.name: Golden Umbral Sands Cape
entries.description: Running in sand is one of the hardest things in the world, so take a bow. You've not only mastered Umbral Sands, but you've run about in it, which is something that most of us would try to avoid.
pages: Running in sand is one of the hardest things in the world, so take a bow. You've not only mastered Umbral Sands, but you've run about in it, which is something that most of us would try to avoid.

entries.name: Golden Whispering Cape
entries.description: A Golden Whispering Cape is a very special achievement, especially considering that you can't see where you're going half the time. I struggle to move fast anyway, but doing it in fog? Nah, you can keep your cape.
pages: A Golden Whispering Cape is a very special achievement, especially considering that you can't see where you're going half the time. I struggle to move fast anyway, but doing it in fog? Nah, you can keep your cape.

entries.name: Grilled Undead Bass
entries.description:
Only moderately less disgusting than braising an undead eel is grilling an undead bass. At least you can close your eyes and imagine what the bass once was: a tasty fish that took a wrong turn at Ardougne and ended up in the Withering. 

At some point in the future, some forward-thinking chef will determine that grilled undead bass is a delicacy. Right now, however, we look at you with the stinkiest of eyes and think 'for shame'.

entries.name: Herb Baked Trout
entries.description: Cathan was known for his love of herb baked trout. He would often claim it was 'the best thing you could do with a tater'. That was until Vannaka picked up a potato, threw it halfway across Temple Woods, and knocked the Party Hat off of Dionysius's head. Cathan subsequently admitted that herb baked trout was 'the second-best thing you could do with a tater'.

entries.name: Infernal Fragment
entries.description: A little like a conch, you can put this infernal shard to your ear. But instead of hearing the sea, you might hear the mumblings of an ancient mind. It's no less soothing, though. If you ever have trouble sleeping, we recommend the calming white-noise of a fractured malevolent soul.

entries.name: Lesser Focused Fishing Potion
entries.description:
If you're one of those anglers who exclaim that fishing is 'about taking a load off' and 'more about relaxation than the end-product', then you might want to try a lesser focused fishing potion. It removes the need for excuses and offers a chance of actually catching fish. Your experience grows and you will soon be gathering catches on the regular.

As an added bonus, with a higher fishing level, you can look down on all the other anglers who claim they fish 'to take a load off'.

entries.name: Lobster Bait
entries.description: Some fish can only be attracted with a very expensive meal. Kind of like trying to date someone far out of your league. What better way to woo those with more refined palettes than a delicious lobster dinner?

entries.name: Maple Rod
entries.description:
This is it. You've made it now. The pinnacle of Dowdun Reach fishing: ownership of a maple rod. Don't let it go to your head. The hook will get stuck in your nostril. 

The humble angler doesn't draw attention to the maple rod. They don't wax it or buy it a nice kebbit-fur sheath. They don't name it something like 'Deborah', or kiss it before they go to bed.

No, the humble angler strides into the middle of other anglers and says "levels?". They listen to the fishing levels of others and nods with appreciation. 

Be the humble angler.

entries.name: Mystic Net
entries.description:
Brassica on a Bullock, that net is garish. You're not going to lose that, are you? I bet that your eyes lock onto it every time you open your inventory. First thing you see. Boom - MYSTIC NET.

It has the same effect on marine life, of course. They're merrily swimming about, doing whatever lobsters and shrimp do, and then boom - MYSTIC NET. Not much they can do, is there? They're transfixed, drawn in by the brightest of blue colours, like moths to a mirrorball. 

Which explains why the mystic net is rather formidable as a net. Not the most fashionable, mind.

entries.name: Oak Rod
entries.description:
Oak rod is much like its anagram: it's an A-OK rod. Not brilliant, not terrible.

It's a rod that you will you look back on fondly when you wield the mighty maple rod. "Ah, I remember when I used to use an oak rod", you will say, as you bite the head off a live catfish and stand astride a pile of infernal eels. 

For now, appreciate your time with it. You will miss it once you have left it behind.

entries.description: You could eat these by the handful if you didn’t mind the crunch. Traditionally cured in brine and turned into a deliciously salty snack. Goes very well on pizzas.

entries.name: Raw Armoured Catfish
entries.description: Looking at this, you’re going to struggle to prepare it properly. Make sure you have a very, very sharp knife.
pages: Looking at this, you’re going to struggle to prepare it properly. Make sure you have a very, very sharp knife.

entries.name: Raw Giant Krill
entries.description:
To its krill kin, this creature is a beast of epic proportions. The sort of monster of legend that would tower over mountains and shatter towers with a single swipe of its enormous claws.

Here, though, it’s a bit like a big shrimp. Much less intimidating.

entries.description: A bit too floppy to be useful for lumberjacks.

entries.name: Raw Infernal Eel
entries.description: Possessed of a strangely smoky flavour, with a surprisingly spicy kick. Best cooked very carefully, preferably in the presence of a priest.

entries.name: Raw Lobster
entries.description: Although some people insist that to get the best flavour a lobster must be alive while it is boiled, you, fortunately for the lobster, have already put it out of its misery. Now you can look forward to boiling it guilt-free for a much gentler flavour.

entries.name: Raw Salmon
entries.description: The Wushanko islands are masters of turning this into a delicious and satisfying meal. Alas, you never did take the time to study their culinary ways and must apply heat to this meal, lest your eject your internalised failures upon Ashenfall’s soil.
pages: The Wushanko islands are masters of turning this into a delicious and satisfying meal. Alas, you never did take the time to study their culinary ways and must apply heat to this meal, lest your eject your internalised failures upon Ashenfall’s soil.

entries.name: Raw Sardine
entries.description: Sardines travel in large shoals; their lives spend as part of a grand community. There’s something a little tragic seeing one here on its own. Still, with a little heat, perhaps a sprinkle of salt and other seasonings, and you’ve got yourself a nice snack.

entries.name: Raw Shrimp
entries.description: There are many ways to cook shrimp. Countless recipes that promise wonderful taste sensations. Right now, though, I would suggest you don’t really want to eat them. They’re all wriggly.
pages: There are many ways to cook shrimp. Countless recipes that promise wonderful taste sensations. Right now, though, I would suggest you don’t really want to eat them. They’re all wriggly.

entries.name: Raw Trout
entries.description: Bonier than some of the other popular fishes, the trout is nevertheless one of the most regularly consumed freshwater fishes. Its flavour is heavily modified by its diet…which, on Ashenfall, is more than a little worrying if I’m honest.
pages: Bonier than some of the other popular fishes, the trout is nevertheless one of the most regularly consumed freshwater fishes. Its flavour is heavily modified by its diet…which, on Ashenfall, is more than a little worrying if I’m honest.

entries.name: Raw Undead Bass
entries.description:
In life, these are gamy fish, sleek of form and delicious with a bit of lemon. In unlife… well… they’re a little less appetising and lemons seem surprisingly sparse on Ashenfall.

Still, needs must.

entries.name: Raw Undead Eel
entries.description:
Sometimes you have to ask yourself why you cook everything you find. Is this really going to make a succulent meal? Even dead it twitches occasionally, animated by some remnant of necromantic energy. Its flesh is partially decayed and the smell… oh the smell…

I recommend cooking it very, very thoroughly.

entries.name: Roasted Lobster
entries.description:
On the sea voyage to Ashenfall, Zanik went through a period of shouting 'lobster!' at the end of perfectly normal conversations with her shipmates. She claimed it was a joke that young dorgeshuun would play on each other, but it led to her being roundly ignored by Vannaka and Dionysius for several days. 

It's also a roasted food - one that makes you feel more refreshed and less thirsty after eating it. If you are to attempt to cook one, it is recommended that you... LOBSTER!

entries.description:
Redberries are red

Sardines are grey

This is the meal 

I eat while I slay.

entries.name: Sauteed Shrimp
entries.description:
In a burst of freakish coincidence, the shrimp is both the easiest sea creature to catch, and the easiest to cook. As a result, some folk from seafaring towns have been known to call shrimp 'eggs of the sea'. Both are considered over-easy.

If you burned rather than sauteed a shrimp, congratulations! In some towns, a burnt shrimp is considered a rarity, such is the negligence required to make one.

entries.name: Seared Anchovies
entries.description:
Not be confused with Seered Anchovies: a delicacy from Umbral Sands where the anchovies are lightly toasted on clairvoyants.

The naturally salty taste of an anchovy has been ascribed to salt flats on the ocean floor, where anchovies feed on the underwater flora. In an attempt to deepen the anchovy flavour, fishermen have been known to sprinkle pepper, marrentil and pineapple on those same salt flats.

entries.description: Fishing bait made from a shrimp. Not terribly exciting, in the grand scheme of things, but still very useful to catching more fish.

entries.name: Shrimp Omelette
entries.description:
It was inevitable that shrimp, known as the 'eggs of the sea' for being over-easy to catch, would get combined with actual eggs to form a meal. Shrimp Omelette is the go-to feast for a shipman, often whipped up by the ship's cook and delivered en masse to the crew. If you're assigned to a long-haul crew, it's best to get a taste for the 'Shrompy' (as it's often shortened). 

Shrompy is also common among Wizards' Guild students who only have space in their dorms for a frying pan and some fire runes.

entries.name: Spooky Bait
entries.description: The ghostly remnants of ectoplasm can be strangely appealing to certain fish. Perhaps it is the siren call of the rivers of the underworld, calling all life to it’s ultimate destination. Perhaps it’s some sort of ancestral grief urging the fish to reconnect with those they have lost. Perhaps it’s simply that they find the thing pretty. Who can really say?

entries.name: Stir-Fry
entries.description:
Imagine if we named all our meals after the processes that make it. Ooh, I'm going to make a pot of boil-strain-pour. I might follow it up with a batch of roll-cut-bakes. It's all a bit odd, if you ask me. 

The Ashenfall stir-fry is something of a curio when compared to the mainland's. To make a mainland version, you would have to swap the krill for seaweed and the infernal eel for lava eel. Whisper it, though: I think the Ashenfall version is better. And it goes particularly well with some grow-chop-fries.

entries.name: Stuffed Catfish
entries.description:
Perhaps it's a good thing that fish have no idea what their future holds. We can only imagine their reactions. "Sorry, chap, you're going to have your armour removed, your innards replaced with cabbage, and krill pushed into your orifices". 

Would it soften the blow if they knew how tasty they became? A stuffed catfish is elevated by the brassic flavours, achieving culinary peaks that are unrivalled on Ashenfall. We like to think that the knowledge would soften the blow.

entries.name: Super Focused Agility Potion
entries.description: Whatever you do, don't go to an Agility Potion party. They were popular back in the Fourth Age and they were UNBEARABLE. Everyone was doing backflips, running up walls and generally never sitting still. There were mid-air collisions and constant bashed heads. Being the tee-total, designated wagon-driver was a nightmare.

entries.name: Undead Delight
entries.description:
'Undead Delight' sounds like an audio track from a long-forgotten Halloween event, but NO - it's an unexpectedly tasty meal. The very dead flavours of an undead bass are meshed with the very alive flavours of a tomato, and the combination is capital-D Delicious.

We will admit that it's off-putting that the un-alive also find the Undead Delight tasty. Put it in front of a skeleton, zombie, demon or other wretched being and they will gobble it up like there's no tomorrow.

You will think you're reaching for a bowl of cookies, only to find that you've over-exerted and done a front-flip over them.

entries.name: Weak Focused Fishing Potion
entries.description:
'Weak' and 'focused' may seem like an oxymoron, but you have to look at the terms from a different perspective. When we say 'focused' we mean you - the angler - and your concentration. It is a measure of how much you narrow your eyes, quell your breath, and attribute all of your senses to the timeless art of poking hooks into fish. This potion increases those faculties. You become so focused that nothing else in the world matters. 

And by 'weak' we mean that the potion is a little bit rubbish at doing all of the above.

entries.name: Willow Rod
entries.description:
The weeping willow is a sallow tree, known for its love of water. Find a brook or ford and a willow will be there, lost in its reflection. 

That familiarity with water makes willow a strong wood for fishing rods. There's the merest wisp of magic running through it, an affinity for water. The fish recognise that affinity and relax. They circle until they're caught, which is pretty handy for an angler.

entries.name: Wool Net
entries.description:
Wool is absolutely rubbish in water. Throw a sheep in a lake if you don't believe us. The water soaks into the wool and turns the poor animal into a sad, soggy anchor.

That rubbishness is - conversely - rather useful when it comes to nets. The wool clods up, leaving barely any holes for a shrimp to make a getaway. It's also heavy as sin. The marine life is thoroughly pinned. 

Now, getting the water out of the net: that's another matter entirely. You might do well to leave it out to dry in the Umbral Sands.

entries.name: Zamorakian Mage Pack
entries.description: The knapsack of a mage within Dowdun Reach. It contains all the materials that the mage would have needed for a day's work. Now they are yours.

entries.name: Antifire Potion
entries.description:
While the antifire potion is a miraculous thing - one of the most useful items on Ashenfall - it does have a flaw. It can be hard to know when its effect wears off. Knowing that you are protected, or not protected, while standing in front of a dragon is something of a problem.

One solution is to bring someone with you. Get them to count while you fight a dragon. Then they can give you a happy thumbs-up while protected and a sad thumbs-down when you're not. 

Of course, they probably need antifire if they're going to assume that role. Which means a third-party to give a thumbs-up or thumbs-down for that second person. Yeah, we see the flaw in the plan.

entries.description: Just because you're protected by antipoison, it doesn't mean that you should start glugging poison or poking yourself with poison-tipped arrows. Your body still needs to get rid of that poison, and it's not pleasant on the exit.

entries.name: Focused Artisan Potion
entries.description: Looking and smelling suspiciously like coffee, this potion lets crafters sit down and create their favourite things. Tapestries, wood carvings, anything that requires time and focus, can be enhanced with the focus this potion provides.

entries.name: Focused Artisan Potion
entries.description:
While it might seem like a good idea to drink several artisan potions at once, the results aren't - unfortunately - multiplicative. The quality of what you make doesn't improve.

In fact, the effect is a bit like dancing when you're drunk: your confidence improves to the point that you THINK you're god's gift to crafting. But then the potion wears off and you see the results: you've made half a tunic with a pom-pom taped to the sleeve. 

Please drink your artisan potions in moderation, people.

entries.name: Focused Attack Potion
entries.description:
Vannaka doesn't believe in attack potions. Oh, he's aware that they might exist, and he has even given them to adventurers on occasion, but he doesn't want them to exist so doesn't believe in them. 

Vannaka, to almost no-one's surprise, is a combat purist. Battle is between two warriors with two blades. The dance is unfettered by things like potions, buffs and perks. If he had it his way, it would be unfettered by armour or clothes. Potions are just one more way that 'combat has gone to the dogs' and 'killing someone isn't as good as it used to be'.

entries.name: Focused Construction Potion
entries.description:
This potion is sweet, yet strong. The ingredients have stewed within the mixture for some time and allowed it to increase in potency. While it’s perfectly fine to drink it directly from the bottle, you find yourself wishing you had a nice mug to use instead.

Still, this potion makes you acutely (haha, see what I did there?) aware of angles. You can measure a plank of wood with just a few well placed glares. The inner architect in you revels at the new possibilities before you, and you find yourself planning much further ahead.

entries.name: Focused Construction Potion
entries.description: Alchemy is a magnificent thing. With innocuous ingredients like ground sandstone and irit, you can make a concoction that is focused on something as singular as construction. One rock and one herb can make you better at making an architrave or lintel.

entries.name: Focused Cooking Potion
entries.description: It’s easy to forget that cooking is more than just throwing ingredients into the pot and applying fire. There are balances of flavours. Subtle blendings of ingredients to create that perfect mix. This potion assists with that by enhancing the smell and tastebuds of the chef, so they can learn just how much of an ingredient needs to be added for optimal results.

entries.name: Focused Cooking Potion
entries.description:
Ironically, a cooking potion tastes horrible. Truly, truly awful. Cooking Guild students have been known to stick two fingers down the throat to eject the potion. It's not worth it before an exam. 

Great chefs like The Culinaromancer stand by the potion, however. The belief is that it strips away the tastebuds so that new tastebuds can grow. Like coppicing a tree, the newer tastebuds are more refined.

entries.name: Focused Runecrafting Potion
entries.description:
It's wonderful to see how far the world has come. Before the First Age, no-one had runes. The only way to wield magic was to become a god, and those opportunities weren't particularly common. 

But now? Not only can you mine essence and make runes, you can use potions to min-max the making of runes. People are swapping strategies for runecrafting runs. We've gone from no runes at all to experience-per-hour. 

It makes you wonder what's next. What is impossible now, but people of the future will consider commonplace? I'm going for toilets, but INSIDE the house.

entries.name: Focused Woodcutting Potion
entries.description: Woodcutting is less about speed and strength, and more about precision. The focus this potion provides, lets you hone your senses, attacking the same place repeatedly along the tree trunk. The result is more efficiently felled trees and far fewer splinters.

entries.name: Lesser Antipoison Potion
entries.description: While the weaker variant of antipoison is sufficient for everyday usage, there are some situations that require a more potent resistance. The toxic mists in Ghornfell, over the swamps, are more powerful than a weaker resistance will protect against. These lesser potions strengthen the immune system and keep the toxic miasma from the drinker’s blood. Imperfect, still, but a much greater chance of survival.

entries.name: Lesser Attack Potion
entries.description:
No one is entirely sure who invented this potion, but those without the knowledge were invariably the losers in warfare. In ancient times armies would be given doses of this potion before they were sent off to battle. It made them deadlier, faster and vastly increased their chances of victory.

The Children of Shadows used to try brew large quantities of this potion every time they went off on a mission, so that they would have the edge were they ever caught. Many a guard could attest to the power of this potion, but fortunately it didn’t make up for a general lack of melee skill.

entries.name: Lesser Magic Potion
entries.description:
Although humans cannot use magic without runes, they can become quite proficient conduits for power. A wizard and a farmer, when possessing the same runes, do not produce the same results, the former far outshines the former. 

This made some farmers pretty upset. For years they had ranted to their cows and sheep about how wizards were just snooty uppity types with shiny rocks. Yet, faced with this revelation, there was no denying that a farmer and a wizard simply weren’t equals in disguise. 

One farmer wanted to level the playing field and brought in a local witch who was had a grudge against the snooty men in blue robes. 

Between the two of them, they found a way to improve a person’s connection to the magic within them via a magical potion. Those who drank it cast spells more efficiently and with greater skill than they ever could before. 

The farmer wanted to use this new advantage to put the wizards in their place, raze down the tower and claim magic a tool of the people. Unfortunately, the witch saw a different future, one that sparkled with glittering gold coins. 

She died happily, wealthier than she had ever dreamed, surrounded by adoring young suiters who wanted a piece of her inheritance. The farmer died after being trampled to death by cows that were tired of his grumbling.

entries.name: Lumberjack Potion
entries.description: This potions helps you sleep all night and work all day. It gives you the feeling of well oiled elbow and shoulder joints, and it numbs the pain in your muscles that’s created from swinging an axe for long stretches at a time.

entries.name: Quarrymaster Potion
entries.description:
As with many physical activities, you can over-exert yourself when mining. Lactic acid builds up in the muscles, sweat clouds the vision, and an accidental pickaxe swing can lodge in the head. A mining potion addresses all of these shortcomings. Lactic acid and sweat forms slowly. The likelihood of accidents is reduced.

What it can't do is improve the quality or amount of ore. Pour it in your mouth or pour it on the deposit: it won't matter. No mining potion is going to help you there.
