entries.description:
Poison has always been a problem for hunters. The forests are full of venomous creatures, just waiting for a chance to strike. The difference between an edible mushroom and one filled with deadly toxins, is hard to spot on a moonless night. Thus the antipoison potion was once of the first to be created. A glorious catch-all that fought against all the venoms and toxins of the realm.

They’re also surprisingly good for a hangover.

entries.name: Abyssal Spine
entries.description: The spinal column of an abyssal demon. A monstrous creature from between the gaps in reality. It pulses with hatred, and you’re convinced it wriggles occasionally.

entries.description: Please, for the love of the River Goddess, don't lick, sniff or apply acrid adhesive to your skin. You might think it would be worse for the Moon Garou who are covered in fur, but at least they can shed the fur when gets sticky. Its harder to shed a finger or lip.

entries.name: Adamant Bar
entries.description: Adamantite is one of the most durable and impressive metals, that would have revolutionised the human populace of Ashenfall if they’d survived long enough to find it. The Moon Garou have learned to make good use of it, but they are comparatively few in number and have little desire for the industrialisation such metals could bring.

entries.name: Adamant Crossbow Limbs
entries.description:

They’re sturdier, stronger and allow for the creation of more impressive crossbows than the other, lesser, metals.

entries.name: Adamantite Ore
entries.description: Smelt this, alongside coal, to create adamant bars. One of the most impressively durable metals available on Ashenfall, adamantite ore is highly prized by the desert-dwelling Moon Garou, who use it in a variety of endeavours.

entries.name: Adhesive
entries.description: Tacky like your great aunt’s wardrobe, this sticky substance has a wide range of uses when it comes to crafting.

entries.name: Anima-Infused Bark
entries.description: The magic of Ashenfall permeates the very trees of the region, imbuing their bark with mystical properties. This bark can be refined into wild anima, a magical crafting component that is popular with spellcasters of all kinds.
pages: The magic of Ashenfall permeates the very trees of the region, imbuing their bark with mystical properties. This bark can be refined into wild anima, a magical crafting component that is popular with spellcasters of all kinds.

entries.name: Animal Bone
entries.description: Bones are not just the favoured materials of necromancers, they can be incredibly useful to a skilled survivalist as well. Designed to withstand great force, while still being as light as possible, bones make excellent components in an array of crafting recipes.
pages: Bones are not just the favoured materials of necromancers, they can be incredibly useful to a skilled survivalist as well. Designed to withstand great force, while still being as light as possible, bones make excellent components in an array of crafting recipes.

entries.name: Animal Hide
entries.description: Animal hides have a variety of uses and have made hunters very popular throughout history. In Bramblemead there was an annual competition to see who could find the most interesting hide. While anima twisted animals were plentiful, many hunters turned to cheating, leading to a rise in the dye trade.

entries.description: What ash logs lack in durability, they make up for in availability. Found all over Brynmoor, ash trees became a vital resource to the humans that resided there. entries.name: Black Dragon Leather
entries.description: Rangers are stealthy little blighters. They like nothing more than to crouch behind a mushroom and ping arrows at a target, preferably without being seen. That preference makes black dragon leather hugely attractive to a ranger. Not only does it bend nicely at the joints for the mushroom-crouching, it's highly durable and - best of all - it's black, which makes the whole subterfuge thing more likely to succeed. I've aways suspected that rangers like the black as it makes them look a bit edgy, but that's unproven.

entries.name: Black Metal Bar
entries.description:
Congratulations on killing enough Black Knights to form a bar from their resulting scraps. Don't think about the children you have orphaned, the dreams that you have impaled on the sharp end of a greatsword. Don't think about the concentrated misery you hold in your hands. 

It is rather shiny, though, is it not? Black Metal, particularly if you have the draconic sort (more chromatic, less matte), is mesmerising.

entries.name: Black Metal Scraps
entries.description:
Fun fact: black metal is actually steel that has gone through a form of vulcanisation. Demonic or draconic sulphur are used in the process, to slightly different effect. Demonic vulcanisation gives the metal a matte finish, while draconic is more chromatic. 

What you have here is some scraps of black metal. Could be demonic, could be draconic. They're likely off-cuts from the smithing or vulcanisation process, or it's entirely possible that they were bashed off a Black Knight's armour when you boffed them. Regardless, waste-not, want-not. Now you have the material required for some new gear.

entries.name: Blightwood
entries.description:
There is something about the swamps of Ashenfall that encourage strange trees to grow. The result is blightwood, durable, powerful and somehow capable of channeling more potent magic than other trees.

The wild knights joked that blightwood houses the souls of the victims of the swamp, and that they are imbued with their regrets and hatred.

It’s probably not true. Probably.

entries.name: Bloodwood Sap
entries.description:
Bloodwood trees are a genuinely horrible creation. Their very existence a wound in the decency of the world, because this tree grows only in places steeped in violence and death.

The biggest bloodwood trees tower over battlefields. Sinewy spiderlike branches cast shade over the homes of serial killers, and you should never trust anyone that can grow one in their garden.

Leech-like roots soak up the suffering, sorrow and cruelty that has seeped into the soil, and then converts that misery into a sticky red sap of raw emotion. This sap can be used to amplify feelings, to convey anger, fear or hatred, across a much greater range.

The dragonkin Lacrussa was very fond of this medium, and used it’s power to shackle dragons to her will.

entries.name: Blue Dragon Leather
entries.description:
A discerning archer would do well to craft blue dragonhide leather. The colour is fetching, the defence against magic is second-to-none, and the material has an elasticity that makes it perfect for the nimble stuff that archers tend to do.

If it has a downside, it's a little tight. There's no hiding in blue dragonhide chaps, for example: all the lumps and bumps are out there.

entries.name: Blue Dragon Scale
entries.description:
There is a curious trend on Gielinor, whereby the most fragile fighters - archers and magic users - are the easiest to spot. From blue dragonhide to mystic robes, the fashion is to wear garish colours as if the rules of the animal kingdom apply. But no, archers and magic users aren't poisonous, venomous or hoping to be mistaken for a bee.

We wonder why that lack of subtlety might be. In the case of blue dragons and their scales, perhaps it's a cruel joke played by the dragonkin. They have seen that humans keep killing their creations, wearing their hides as trophies. They've got their revenge by way of a generous use of the rainbow.

entries.name: Blue Dragon Scale Dust
entries.description:
Blue dragon dust is one of those things where you wonder who invented it, and what curious sequence of events led to it happening. Some unknown person had the wherewithal to strip a dragon of dragon scales, crush those scales in a pestle and mortar, then apply the resulting dust to a potion. Not only that, they downed said potion and stood in the path of a dragon. Does that not seem inexorably mad to you? 

But thank you, inexorably mad person, because now we have this potent ingredient which can protect a person from dragonfire. You have been forgotten in time, but your blue dusty legacy lives on.

entries.name: Blue Dragonhide
entries.description:
Blacksmiths hate this one simple trick. They spend their lives mastering interlocking chains and plates, only for dragons to be born with them. A third of the blacksmith's punters are now gone, hunting for dragons rather than dropping some coin at their forges. It's enough to make a blacksmith sob into their anvil. 

Blue dragons hate that one simple trick too, of course. Their venn diagram overlaps with the blacksmith's: they'd rather people got their armours from somewhere other than dragons.

entries.name: Blurite Crossbow Limbs
entries.description:
Not all cats are terrified of crossbows, though most of the Bramblemead population quickly learned to fear them. Some cats could see their merit but were painfully aware of their human pet’s limited imagination.

Mittens was the lifelong owner of Gothren Actillian. A blacksmith’s cat, he had learned how to keep the forge fires perfectly hot by playfully jumping on the bellows periodically – something his pet seemed to enjoy. He knew the right length of time a sword should be cooled for and would make sure his human stuck to that timing by offering useful alarms made of glorious clattering things.

But blurite? That was a new one. Mittens could see there was little value to the metal, beyond some weird human aesthetic that he did not understand, yet there was some potential to the construction. With carefully timed meows, and some creative knocking over of reagents, Mittens was able to engineer a crossbow of superior design, worthy of his cherished pet.

entries.name: Blurite Ore
entries.description:
Sometimes colours just want to manifest themselves. There is the sweetness of orange. The cowardice of yellow, and the peaceful serenity of a summery green. Blue, tired with only being linked to sorrow and sadness, sought a physical existence. One that could be shaped into new and wonderous things, and so blurite was born.

A metal that is so very, very, blue.

It’s in the name. After all, it’s blue, right?

This journal entry was sponsored by the tree haters of Lumbridge, if you’re interested in joining their focus group, please speak to Tim near Bob’s Axes.

entries.name: Cooling Arcane Infusion
entries.description: The stereotype is that wizards are the lazy corner of the combat triangle. They don't have to swing an axe like a melee warrior, or dodge behind mushrooms like a ranger. They stand stock-still, tossing fireballs: a glass cannon who crosses their non-spellcasting fingers, hoping that they don't get impaled on an arrow. But let me tell you: the wizard has to wear the heaviest, most uncomfortable robes, even in the heat of places like the Umbral Sands, and that is hard work. For those wizards, there is nothing like the cool, soothing taste of a cooling arcane infusion.

entries.description: Vannaka approves this message. When you absolutely, positively have to kill every skeleton, demon or dragon in the room: accept no substitute. Except, perhaps, the cooling relentless infusion. Honestly, Vannaka can't pick between them.

entries.description: The best archers in the world are often said to have ice in their veins. It's an odd idiom - you would imagine that would be both uncomfortable and give an archer the shivers, precisely what they wouldn't want - but it's meant to indicate a steeliness, a cold efficiency. Well, imagine applying a tap (or faucet, if that's your orientation) to an archer and draining them for a drink. That would be the cooling relentless infusion.

entries.name: Corpse Cotton
entries.description:
The corpse flower is a strange creature. Strange, almost flesh-like sacks, filled with a noxious gas that explodes upon contact with the air. The resulting mass of fibres looks disturbingly like thin strips of a cadaver’s skin, earning it the name “corpse cotton” by the more macabre Emberwood villagers.

In truth it’s little more than thick plant fibres that can be woven together into a smooth, durable and, frankly, fashionable fabric.

entries.name: Cursed Essence
entries.description:
Cursed essence is a magical agent often used in tanning. It is also something of a curiosity, one that a simple tanner can't readily explain. It goes further than simply binding itself to material; it latches onto it, almost parasitically. 

Demonologists have a theory that, although cursed essence drops from avernic demons of Dowdun Reach, it is actually cthonic in nature. It would explain the tendril-like tenacity.

entries.name: Cursed Leather
entries.description:
You may wonder where the 'cursed' moniker comes from. There is no need to worry: you're not cursed by wearing it, and you're not going to be visited by the three dragons of past, present and future in the night for making it. It has a wildly different etymology. 

The 'cursed' is a tannery thing, you see. Cursed leather is notoriously hard to work and shape. Only the foremost tanners can manipulate it. But even they have a hard time, often exclaiming "cursed leather!" at the top of their lungs.

The 'cursed' is a tannery thing, you see. Cursed leather is notoriously hard to work and shape. Only the foremost tanners can manipulate it. But even they have a hard time, often exclaiming "cursed leather!" at the top of their lungs.

entries.name: Demonic Oil
entries.description:
Combine corrupt bonemeal and vile ashes and the result is demonic oil. We should be specific about what kind of oil this is: please do no pour it into a frying pan or use it on a squeaky hinge. This is potent oil, as the 'demonic' prefix will attest. It is used for crafting, and solely for crafting.

Now you've got us wondering what would happen if you did actually add it to a frying pan or a squeaky hinge. Obviously, please don't do it. But if you do happen to do it, through an accident or momentary lack of wisdom, could you let us know what happens?

entries.name: Desert Cloth
entries.description:
You might think that any cloth found in the desert could be called desert cloth, but you’d just be arguing semantics and that won’t win you many friends at parties. No, the desert cloth we refer to here is the sort of thing woven from desert weed and cacti fibres. It is forged of the desert, not simply found within it.

That said, explaining this at parties probably still won’t make you many friends.

entries.name: Dihydrogen Monoxide
entries.description: If a smiling garou sells you some 'human salts', or 'dinner dust' then be wary. There is a good chance that the garou trader doesn't like you and is selling you one of Umbral Sands' common compounds: dihydrogen monoxide. The scientists among you will perk up your ears: dihydrogen monoxide is a compound that forms a base for so many toxic substances and diseases. It's not 'dinner dust', as the cheeky garou might have suggested. Put it in a vial, keep it away from the hands of grasping children, and use it with care.

entries.name: Dire Wolf Hide
entries.description: A tougher, more resilient hide, obtained after slaying a deadly dire wolf. It is said that if you wear the hide of a dire wolf, during the light of a full moon, then you’ll rapidly reduce the size of your circle of friends.

entries.name: Dire Wolf Leather
entries.description:
The tanned hide of a powerful dire wolf. It's sturdy, thick, ready for enchantment and more resilient than normal leather. 

A legend speaks of a warrior that wore the tanned hide of a dire wolf. He wore it proudly as he walked the streets and used it to strike fear into the hearts of bandits and criminals alike. After all, a warrior that could best such a beast, was no one to be trifled with. 

The story goes that one day he met another warrior, proud, skillful and handsome, and the two of them became the best of friends. They would fight together, spar together and rescued helpless villagers as an unstoppable pair. Until the night of the full moon, where the truth was revealed. Where once his new friend had stood, there was now a dread wolf of midnight-black fur and eyes of burning coal. They fought again, but gone was the jovial sparring of friends. Now they fought as man and beast, tooth and claw versus blade and shield, until all that was left of the two of them was this story.

entries.name: Draconic Leather
entries.description:
Tanned hide infused with a dragon’s vigor, draconic leather was a gamechanging discovery to the people of Fellhollow. It was as flexible as normal leather, but more resilient than even hardened leather, and it could be fashioned into a variety of shapes useful in a variety of armoured styles.

For a short while, the fashionistas of Emberwood village would use this leather to create garments that evoked the majesty of their draconic protectors, without bearing the scales that might cause undue offence.

entries.name: Dragon Blood
entries.description: The blood of a dragon is a strange thing. It is infused with magic in a way that most other creatures can’t match, a side effect of the alchemical processes that created their kind. Dragonkin scientists needed blood that could adapt to a wide range of chimeric additions to the body. As such dragon blood, unlike human blood, doesn’t possess any particular type and each could act as donor to the other.

entries.name: Dragonstone
entries.description:
These purple stones are a wonder to behold. The way the light catches them and sparkles - it can delight even the smallest of children for many hours.

It was for this reason that it’s been sought after by artisans everywhere. Or possibly because of its inherent magical properties?

Nah, must be the distracting kids things. I’ve spoken to parents, a little quiet time seems like it’s worth its weight in gold.

entries.name: Dragonwolf Hide
entries.description:
Do not pity the dragonwolf. Oh, you don’t? That’s fine then. Yes, horrible little blighters aren’t they? Their teeth are too jagged and they’re far too aggressive for my tastes. Still, apparently deadly critters don’t just want to roll over and die so you can harvest their skin, who’d have thought?

The dragonwolf is an experiment that didn’t quite go right. It wasn’t wrong, exactly, it was certainly a step in the direction their creator wanted, but like most Dragonkin experiments, they was never “good enough”. Too warm-blooded. Too fluffy. Too weak.

Fortunately, the crafters in Emberwood were not quite so picky. They found that hide to be incredibly durable and hardy, whilst remaining surprisingly flexible. They would craft wonderous outfits from the tanned leather, trying to emulate their winged overseers.

entries.description: It's almost impossible to hold dried tea leaves up to the nose, have a huff, and not go "aaaaaah" in a deep, relieved sort of manner. It's the smell of lazy Sunday afternoons, butt in a rocking chair, wistfully thinking back to your golden years.

entries.description: A simple amulet bearing Bandos’ symbol. Every once in a while you could swear you hear strange whispers from it, like a song you can’t quite remember. It’s cold to the touch and makes the hairs, on the back of your neck, shiver constantly.

entries.name: Ectoplasm
entries.description:
There are many theories on what ectoplasm is, each as disturbing as the last. Some say that it’s emotion, condensed over years of existence. Others think that it’s some sort of infection of the soul, as only the undead seem to produce it.

In truth, ectoplasm is none of these. It’s the outer shell of a soul, the skin more or less, and acts as a sort of lubrication between the flesh and the spirit. Tiny bits of reality combine with the immaterial otherness of the underworld and congeal into a sort of spiritual mixture that ghosts and other undead find incredible useful.

Necromancers prize the stuff, finding a myriad of uses for it. Most people find it weird and decidedly “icky”.

entries.name: Egg
entries.description:
If you prescribe to the theory of evolution, then this object wins the debate. After all, what came before the egg wasn’t technically a chicken, but something similar yet different. So, the egg would have come first, to then hatch the first chicken.

Of course, the real question here is whether chickens evolved, or whether they were created by the gods? No god claims to have created the first chicken, nor, indeed, the first egg, but they never deny it when asked.

So, which came first? The god or the egg?

entries.description: More elegant and refined than cotton cloth, this fabric was very popular mong Emberwood citizenry. They would craft beautiful dresses, fine shirts and elegant robes, many of which included patterns of undulating blue and black in honour of the serpentine dances they would watch in the sky, as Imaru and Xikotal swam the air currents together.

entries.name: Fine Thread
entries.description: Because “corpse thread” is far too sinister a title, this thread is referred to as fine thread. It’s stronger, thinner and more malleable than cotton threads. The villagers of Emberwood enjoyed this thread in their clothing, creating garments that would suffer greater strain than their previous gear. Farmers were particularly fond of it.

entries.name: Fire Oil
entries.description:
Used to craft Fire arrows.

Some people just like to watch the world burn… and you can too, with these new handy fire oils! That’s right, just lob one of these beauties at your enemies and watch them ignite. Enjoy their screams as their skin boils away and breathe in the delightful aroma of a fresh barbecue!

Fire oil, like snake oil, was once the creation of a travelling merchant to Ashenfall. She had journeyed to Brynmoor alongside some of the Saradominist settlers, and with her she brought pungent unguents, elucidating elixirs, marvellous medicines, and weapons of localised destruction.

When her wares summoned the call for refunds, she would dazzle the onlookers with a sudden fiery display and then disappear into the alleyways until she had been forgotten. She would then return in one of a staggering array of disguises, until the tragic day when her wagon hit a pothole during a quick getaway and her many, many, bottles of fire oils decided to sing the song of their people.

Fortunately, even though she and everything she owned, tragically found itself reduced to smouldering atoms, her recipe lived on and found more conventional uses.

entries.name: Flax
entries.description: Flax was a popular plant during the time of Guthix. Found all over the continent, it could be easily harvested and refined into various materials. Villagers would enjoy the seeds as tasty snacks, but they mostly prized the flax for the threads that could be woven from the stems of the plant.

entries.description: These leathery packs are carried around by garou warriors. They store rations, herbs and the spoils of battle inside. Crafted by elderly garou in the villages, or parents sending their child off to battle.

entries.name: Garou Weave
entries.description:
Sadly, this is not a new hairstyle unlock, rather it’s a special cloth created by the Moon Garou. They say it’s woven from moon sprite silk, which can only be obtained in the light of a full moon and, even then, only by shamans. 

The truth is that it’s less complicated than that. It’s crafted by a gaggle of garou grannies, each of them weaving together special fibres that have been passed down their family line for generations. Each bolt of cloth may seem the same, but they are each a unique blending of garou family craftwork.

entries.description: When you take me out of a window, you leave a grieving wife. When you stick me in a door, you will save somebody’s life. What am I?

entries.name: Glass Vessel
entries.description:
The glass vessel. The emblem of potential. It could find itself filled with anything. Water, demonic oil, maple syrup. It could smash before it ever sees use. It could languish in someone's inventory, forgotten for months. In many ways, we are all glass vessels. 

Check back in your journal for other delightful moments of poignancy and philosophy. You may find your life unutterably changed by the wisdom there.

entries.description: Few things have led to quite so much wanton destruction as gold. Wars have been fought over it. Brother has slain brother just for a handful of the glimmering nuggets. Yet, without the trappings of commerce, it is but a metal like any other. Pretty though, good in jewellry.

entries.name: Greater Kalphite Wing
entries.description: Next time you find a greater kalphite wing, open it out to its full length and hold it up to the light. It's a wondrous sight, like a mixture of oil slick and flickering flame, which would be unwise to combine anywhere else. Its beauty, of course, has made it a desirable trading material, and is used by the Moon Garou in dream-catchers, mobiles for younger garou, and - of course - infinity cloth.

entries.name: Green Dragon Hide
entries.description:
Dragons are never fond of surrendering their natural armour, a natural feature they’ve used to great advantage.

In the earliest days of the Dragonkin experiments, the scales of a dragon were something to be proud of. They would turn away blade and arrow with equal skill, and even magic struggled to pierce their natural defences.

Still, this wasn’t good enough for their makers. Lacrussa, herself, saw the hide of dragons as a promising start, but little more, and she would strive to forge newer and more resilient scales on her creations. The green dragons were, in her opinion, some of the weakest of the dragons, and she only kept them around because her sibling enjoyed the glittering green reflections of the sunlight on their scales.

entries.description: By grinding clay down into powder, you can create a much smoother medium for crafting. The grinding process gets rid of various impurities and allows for more resilient results.

entries.name: Ground Dragon Tooth
entries.description: Alchemists and specialists in herbal remedies would be lying if they said they hadn't considered the medicinal properties of Kuldra. They imagine what it would be like if they could get hold of one of her teeth, crush it, and then use it in place of the traditional ground dragon tooth. Just how much of a kick would that give their concoctions? They're self-aware enough to know that it's just a fantasy, but they like to daydream about it anyway. Sure, it would be lovely to rid the world of a tyrant dragon, but think of the potions!

entries.description: It takes a lot of effort to crush granite into powder. Blood, sweat and tears go into the process of refining this solid stone into something more manageable. In doing so you prove yourself a master over the earth itself, though the earth rarely acknowledges your claim.

entries.name: Ground Gypsum
entries.description: Gypsum is a versatile old construction material, used for drywall, plaster and other essentials of the modern home. If you have mined gypsum and turned it to powder, there is a strong chance that you, too, have found a construction use for it. Just make more than you need, as the grinding process tends to create a lot of wastage. As builders will tell you: "you gypsum, you lose some".

Just make more than you need, as the grinding process tends to create a lot of wastage. As builders will tell you: "you gypsum, you lose some".

entries.name: Ground Limestone
entries.description:
Clearly, all limestone is ground limestone, as it comes from the ground. In many places it IS the ground. But this is specifically limestone that has been ground down into a dust. 

Ground limestone's primary use is in glassblowing. Should you have the crafting capability and a healthy, strong puff, you can use the ground limestone to make molten glass and then glass-produce.

entries.description: Sometimes you just want to prove how much better you are than a lump of rock, by grinding it down into a fine powder. Yeah, take that sandstone, you’re not all that tough as dust, are you?

entries.name: Ground Stone
entries.description: Much harder to stub your foot on in powdered form. Stone ground down and down until all that remains is a fine powder useful in ways that big lumps of stone are not. Like cake frosting for your enemies.

entries.name: Gypsum
entries.description: There are more glamorous rocks to mine than gypsum. If you want to get an amorous wink from a dwarf then you should probably aim for diamond or adamantite. But gypsum is an honest, hard-working rock that is exceptionally practical. Gypsum just needs a better PR agent.

entries.name: Gypsum Wax
entries.description: A combination of gypsum powder and dihydrogen monoxide, gypsum wax contains the worst of both materials. It's as claggy and hard to remove as gypsum powder, and as deadly as dihydrogen monoxide.

entries.name: Hard Leather
entries.description: Thicker and more resilient than normal leather. Still smells though.
pages: Thicker and more resilient than normal leather. Still smells though.

entries.name: Harmonised Compound
entries.description: Smelting discordant residue into harmonised compound is astonishingly reckless. In essence, you're 'cooking anima', which is akin to gargling fuel and then sipping on fire. You are dealing with some of the highest percentages of anima - the lifeblood of the world. We'd tell you to be careful, but this is the person who has wandered into the home of a five-headed dragon with the express intention of killing it.

entries.description: A bitter tasting herb that makes for a poor tea, yet is often used as a morning pick-me-up by people with no tastebuds. It’s useful in crafting certain potions.

entries.name: Hollow Bark
entries.description:
It is perhaps strange that bark could be referred to as hollow. It’s generally extracted in strips, or patches, but nothing that could act as a container. Indeed there would need to be an entire tree without a centre to make it hollow, and that’s exactly the case here.

When the withering began it was souls that suffered first, torn away and dragged into the underworld to be consumed by the cursed dragon. Yet, as time drew on, Imaru’s hunger did not diminish, only grow, and so the world itself began to suffer.

Things taste worse in Fellhollow. Dreams are vapid and empty, if you have them at all. A campire feels colder, even if it warms you just as well as before. Because the substance, the soul of that thing if you will, is being consumed.

Hollow bark comes from a tree that has been hollowed out from within. Its insides less than they should be, weaker and wrong. As awful as this is, it makes the bark develop in strange ways desirable by skilled mages with a poor sense of fashion.

entries.name: Imaru's Head
entries.description:
A rotting and twisted dragon head, momentary twitches still flicker through it, the last remnants of necromancy at play.

The tragedy of Imaru is that she was once a sweet and gentle creature. Cruel dragonkin experiments had robbed her of the only thing she had ever wanted, to be a mother. So when the humans came to her land, she saw in them the children she never had. Xikotal, her mate, encouraged this nurturing behaviour, knowing the joy it would bring his beloved.

She could have been happy, and the people of Fellhollow could have been happy with her.

But Kuldra could not allow it. The queen’s hatred and rage became an infection that took hold of Imaru’s grief and, like some foul parasite, twisted it into something worse.

It is better that Imaru is no more. There is none who would argue otherwise. Yet, whilst we should not mourn the monster, perhaps we should take a moment to mourn the mother she could have been.

entries.name: Imbued Granite Block
entries.description: A chunk of granite imbued with powerful magic. On its own, this hunk of stone isn’t useful, but when combined with other components it becomes part of a much stronger weapon.

entries.name: Imbued Leather Wrappings
entries.description: These wrappings are made from the leather of a powerful and dangerous beast. The ambient anima of Ashenfall infuses it with a sturdiness that most leather wrapping can’t equal.
pages: These wrappings are made from the leather of a powerful and dangerous beast. The ambient anima of Ashenfall infuses it with a sturdiness that most leather wrapping can’t equal.

entries.name: Infinity Cloth
entries.description:
Some fabrics are too beautiful for mundane hands. It feels almost a crime that you, a mere mortal, should be allowed to hold such a material. To craft it into clothing is an act so sacred, that priests should be set up solely to handle this fabric.

At least that’s what some tailors believe.

Infinity cloth is so garish, so incoherently vibrant, that it induces a strange sort of psychosis into those who use it. They do not see the vulgar brightness of the colours, nor the incomprehensible combinations that would be a fashion crime in any other world. Instead, they see only shimmering colours and a sparkling iridescence that reaches somewhere inside of them and murders their sense of taste.

Infinity cloth is a beautiful blasphemy, handle with care.

entries.name: Irit
entries.description:
It is unsurprising that irit grows in Fellhollow, considering it has such a close association with the dead. Whereas normal irit grows around graveyards and near the temples of death deities, the irit in Fellhollow grows everywhere.

Yet, unlike its leafier version, the irit here is twisted and sharp. It is formed of thorny roots that writhe out of the ground and must be cut down to access the herb beneath. After all, the dead in Fellhollow refuse to stay buried without a fight, why wouldn’t the irit react the same?

entries.description: A heavy ingot of iron.

entries.name: Iron Ore
entries.description: Iron is sturdy, durable and malleable. Blacksmiths prize it highly as a material for crafting superior arms and armour from. It is rumoured that certain fae creatures are repelled by the ore, perhaps due to it’s rigidity and refusal to change to the whims of magical beings.

entries.name: Jade
entries.description:
The more green the colour of jade, the higher the concentration of iron in its makeup. Popular among many cultures for both its beauty and it’s use as a crafting material.

In the eastern lands of Wushanko, jade is highly prized. Some islands have elaborate rituals about its usage. There are rumours of rare jades with magical properties, each a different colour of the rainbow.

entries.name: Kalphite Shell Fragments
entries.description: You might get some looks, but make sure you pocket the little scraps of kalphite that you find. These little exoskeleton offcuts may not be much on their own, but grab some acrid adhesive and you can glue them together to make kalphite shells. Where you go after that is up to you. We recommend magic carpet battles, tossing shells at each other as you race.

entries.name: Kot Pack
entries.description: To say that a Kot Pack is the belongings of a single KotHaar is something of a misrepresentation. You're actually holding the belongings of dozens of KotHaar, stretching back millennia. A KotHaar will carry the obsidian of their ancestors, which was reconstituted from their ancestors before them. The Kot Pack is a lineage, an ancestral record of the creature you killed. It puts things a little into perspective, and I'm sure you will treat it with the respect it deserves.

entries.name: Kwuarm
entries.description:
This herb has travelled far to deliver its malicious benefits to the people of Ashenfall. Its name, in Dwarvish, means “warm death” since it causes a terrible burning fever if the sap is consumed.

Crushed down, so that it’s sap and oils can be easily accessed, this herb is a requirement in some of the deadliest and most dangerous poisonous mixtures.

entries.description: Tanned animal hide has a distinctive smell and was surprisingly popular among some of the quieter villagers of Bramblemead. This versatile material can be used to craft a wide range of items, including armour and weapons.

entries.name: Limestone
entries.description:
Turn your limestone this way and that and you might come across a fossil. Lesser blue dragons have been in the region for some time, and there were experimentations that led to them. Being experimentations, they weren't cognitively blessed, so it's entirely possible to find the talon of a dragon that got trapped in a rockfall.

You could also find the odd chicken wing from the Second Age. The Children of Shadows loved a shake and bake.

entries.description: You'd struggle to find a better catalyst than luminite ore. If it was a person it would be the life of the party, the guest who dances on the table, gets everyone enjoying themselves, and then promptly passes out upstairs. It burns brightly but briefly, enabling other ores - like runite - to realise their potential.

entries.name: Luminite Deposit
entries.description: I'm something of a geologist, and I have three reference books that describe different origins for luminite. A fanciful book states that they come from the sky, from shooting stars. Another reference with a theological bent claims that Elidinis brought the rocks to Ashenfall (how she drilled them into the ground is not covered in the book). Another tome, which I am more inclined to believe, says that luminite was once coal that got twisted with anima. If you're a student geologist and fancy a good topic for a thesis, I'd recommend investigating which one is correct.

entries.name: Magic Logs
entries.description: They say that you can tell how old a tree is by cutting it down and counting the rings. That's true of most trees, but not the magic tree. A magic tree is coy about its age and prefers to hide its rings. All that's left is to guess a magic tree's age, and - as per the adage - a gentleman should never try to guess a magic tree's age. At least guess a few decades younger: they're sensitive to that sort of thing.

entries.name: Maple Sap
entries.description:
It's like the maple tree wants to be cut down. Not only does it produce hardy, versatile wood for tools and weaponry, it bleeds sap that is only a single step away from being maple syrup. If you want proof of the gods' existence in RuneScape, you need only look at maple trees. 

The maple tree gets its revenge in subtle ways. Its sap is inordinately sticky and too much syrup will give you a paunch. They're small victories, but the maple tree takes them.

entries.name: Mithril Bar
entries.description:
In the Third Age on Ashenfall, mithril was incredibly desirable. It was only available in small quantities then, as its scarcity - perhaps inevitably - made it the fashion of the time. High-priests would incorporate it into their rosaries. Community leaders would wear it as brooches. It was rare enough that people would comment when they saw it. "Ooh, Rosie's doing well for herself". That sort of thing. 

The idea of a mithril bar would have been mind-boggling to anyone in the Third Age. No matter their alignment, they'd have stabbed you in the belly and run away cackling with it. But here you are with an entire ingot. Take a moment and consider yourself a Third Age king.

entries.description:
What do you call a crossbow without limbs? A REALLY cross bow. 

Oh shush, you. That joke plays well at fletching conventions.

entries.name: Mithril Ore
entries.description:
Mithril means much to the dwarves. It was first discovered by a dwarf called Tolkun in the First Age, and its seams have been uncovered in much of Gielinor. The dwarves call it 'The Dwarven Welcome' thanks to its shine. Find the ore when mining and it lights up to greet you: a dwarven welcome. 

A 'Dwarven Welcome' is also what dwarves call a headbutt while wearing a mithril helmet.

entries.name: Molten Glass
entries.description: Beautiful, yet hard to handle, the creation of molten glass was a turning point for Gielinorian civilization. It allowed the creation of vials, windows, and those pretty little animals that grandmothers love to collect and put on shelves.

entries.name: Monkfish Skewers
entries.description: Monkfish skewers are the friend of any travelling Moon Garou. Compact and easy to carry, a couple of dozen can be taken on any scouting or hunting party. They also double-up as weapons, should a garou find themselves ambushed during a hearty meal. It's not uncommon to see a half-dead kalphite staggering about in the desert with rows of monkfish skewers puncturing their carapace. They look a little like a buffet dish.

entries.name: Monstrous Fang
entries.description: The deadly canines of a large creature. Much more fun when they’re not still in the snapping maw of the creature chasing you.

entries.name: Mystic Cloth
entries.description:
It is almost imperceptible, but mystic cloth hums. It's the magical resonance: the elemental threads pushing against each other as their charge shifts. That oscillation also means that there is a lightly massaging effect on the wearer. It's entirely possible to feel calm from the vibrations as you stride into battle.

You might also be mistaken for thinking that mystic cloth is blue. On a microscopic level, it's actually a multitude of colours, combining to form the illusion of blue. As a magician once told me, it's the same effect as a blue sky: it is the result of all the colours in the world combining to make wondrous azure.

entries.name: Mystic Fibres
entries.description:
The origin of mystic fibres, thread and cloth are wreathed in mystery. There's little to no mention in any written histories, which - on its own - seems unlikely. It is not a subtle material. There should be log after log of merchants trading it, or actively avoiding trading it. 

It leads me to believe that the mystic material is an elaborate troll. It's a plant - and I don't mean that in the floral definition. I think someone has introduced it as a joke, and I have a list of potential culprits. Brassica Prime: you are number one on that list.

entries.name: Naphtha
entries.description:
Distilled from Swamp Tar and Charcoal.

Once known as “thick water”, naptha is liquid fire in waiting. It takes little to bring this substance to ignition, even too bright a sunny day can bring the raging flame from within.

As such, this material is widely sought by anyone with a strong desire to set things aflame. Pyromaniacs, alchemists and dragon cultists alike yearn for this liquid.

entries.description: Stronger than ash, the oak tree strands proud against its lesser cousin. Oak logs are more durable, sturdier and more desirable for more advanced construction. Though the trees are harder to find in Brynmoor, it is said that Ghornfell offers more of them, if one is willing to face the dangers of exploring it.

entries.name: Opal
entries.description: A very shiny stone. Prized by magpies around the world, who are drawn to it’s magnificent luster.

entries.name: Ornate Maul Handle
entries.description: The handle for a powerful weapon. Wrapped in sturdy leather and imbued with ritual magic. A dwarf capable of crafting such a piece is acknowledged to have completed one of the trials required to be a master smith.

entries.name: Padded Cloth
entries.description: A bolt of cloth that has been reinforced. Makes for sturdier armour than normal cloth.
pages: A bolt of cloth that has been reinforced. Makes for sturdier armour than normal cloth.

entries.name: Pristine Beltfish
entries.description: If there were a Fishing Contest quest in Ashenfall, you can be sure that this little belter (ha!) would win outright. The lean, whiplike grace; the elegant lines of its form; the shimmer on its scales. We don't want to go overboard, but this fish you have caught is quite the looker.

entries.name: Pristine Monkfish
entries.description: Congratulations! Of all the monkfish in the world, you have come across possibly the most dapper. You may wish to spend some time forging a monocle, to really tie the look together. That is, of course, one of those things that is funny to write in a journal like this, but will lead to disappointment and frustration if you actually try it in game.

entries.name: Pumpkin
entries.description:
They seem strange without faces, don’t they?

Heralds of the spookiest of seasons, the humble pumpkin exists in two worlds, the world of the living and the world of the dead. When carved it acts as a ward against dangerous spirits and when mixed with spices and added to warm drinks, it acts as a lure for ex-girlfriends, distracting them as it gives you time to escape.

entries.name: Quests Crystal Orb
entries.description: A crystal sphere containing a shimmering fog. It’s part of a magical ritual needed to craft a powerful staff, one that is infused with celestial power. The Icyene, of Hallow, once gifted these orbs to the followers of Saradomin, so that they might better serve the god of Order.

entries.name: Quests Horn Challenge
entries.description:
Cathan’s challenge horn design is a collection of materials hastily thrown together. A dragon’s tooth, carved with dragonkin sigils as well as metal wires used to connect them together –  like a spiderweb lattice, glistening with traces of magical power.

When placed in the dragonkin altar, the horn acts as a focus point for the magical power stored within the tower, sending an invisible beacon off into the air, in a perfect draconic pitch.

Velgar has been summoned many times before. By heroes, kings, warriors and gods, and yet still the tower stands.

Be ready, when you send out the call.

entries.name: Raw Bestial Meat
entries.description: Thick and tough to chew, this meat makes for a filling meal, but an exercise to bite through.
pages: Thick and tough to chew, this meat makes for a filling meal, but an exercise to bite through.

entries.name: Raw Bird Meat
entries.description: The white meat of a bird is surprisingly versatile. While delicious on its own, it can be combined with various dishes, seasoned or marinated to create surprisingly varied flavours. The meat is often softer to consume, making it an easier meal for the on-the-go hunter.

entries.name: Raw Farm Meat
entries.description: This dense meat is a sturdy meal when prepared properly. It comes from larger animals who are far less willing to give it up than their smaller kin, making it a well deserved delicacy.
pages: This dense meat is a sturdy meal when prepared properly. It comes from larger animals who are far less willing to give it up than their smaller kin, making it a well deserved delicacy.

entries.name: Raw Game Meat
entries.description: Tender meat, straight from the hunt. Traditionally you would hang the meat to dry out a little before consumption, marinating it in wines, spices and preservatives. However, you can lob it in a fire if you want a more immediate meal. We don’t judge.
pages: Tender meat, straight from the hunt. Traditionally you would hang the meat to dry out a little before consumption, marinating it in wines, spices and preservatives. However, you can lob it in a fire if you want a more immediate meal. We don’t judge.

entries.name: Raw Rat Meat
entries.description: Smaller creatures have much less meat on their bones, making them a less fulfilling meal. Hunters would subsist on these while stalking larger prey over several days. The Wild Knight Ilom was particularly fond of drying out these little morsels, treating them as a meaty little snack for boring patrols.

entries.name: Red Dragonhide Leather
entries.description: There is no better advert for red dragon leather than Fuzan. The tyrant of Umbral Sands has seen his fair share of upstarts. Moon Garou of all shapes and sizes have confronted him over the years, and none have managed to break his red leather hide. The only blades to have cut him were the claws of his mother, and the glaive of one mutinous KotHaar. Fuzan has met very little resistance over his long life, which might go some way to explaining why he is the way he is.

entries.name: Red Topaz
entries.description: This glittering gemstone really catches the light, sparkling like a tiny little star that’s dying. Count Valingard, one of Brynmoor’s nobility in the third age, was very fond of these stones and was said to have an entire chandelier made from them. Sadly, dragon fire appears to be particularly good at melting them, so the chandelier is no longer with us.

entries.name: Refined Obsidian
entries.description: It's hard for a human to understand just how much obsidian means to a KotHaar. Imagine that your homes, tools and weapons were the flesh of your ancestors. Imagine that the money in your wallet was stretched skin from a distant relative. Now, switch out your disgust for a kind of holy reverence: the KotHaar feel this towards all the obsidian about them. That flesh isn't just a physical remnant of their ancestors, it carries their memories too. Knowledge permeates the rock.

entries.name: Ruby
entries.description: To the followers of Zamorak, the ruby was the perfect stone to bedazzle their finery, their weapons, or their very confused pets. The redness of the stone was seen as recognition of their god, and the sparklines of the gemstone was… well, sparkly and pretty, and everyone likes sparkles, even evil wizards.

entries.name: Rune Essence
entries.description:
A magical stone with the ability to absorb the ambient anima around it. On Ashenfall, the rocks hover in the air as if resting on some invisible structure, held aloft by invisible currents of magical energy.

With the right equipment and skill, rune essence can be infused with certain magical resonances, taking on the elemental power of the air, or the flame.

This discovery is one of Guthix’s greatest triumphs and perhaps his longest lasting miracle.

entries.name: Shimmerscale Powder
entries.description: Stare into the shimmer scale powder and it's like looking up into the night sky. Constellations form in the dust. Often, you'll see Moon Garou merchants idly stirring their stocks of shimmer scale powder, fascinated. It's not difficult to see how infinity cloth gets its many shimmering colours.

entries.description: It seems almost unfair that plants could become electrified – a secret guarded closely by eels until now. These bulbs still contain a residual trace of that lightning charge, making them much desired in herblore.

entries.name: Silver Ore
entries.description: Silver is an excellent conductor of magic. It’s why it shows up in so many legends and myths about supernatural foes. As a precious metal, it is highly prized in the crafting of jewellry and strongly disliked by lycanthropes everywhere.

entries.name: Skeleton Pack
entries.description: A foul-smelling sack, with threads frayed by the cruelty of time. Contains whatever strange possession were being hoarded after death.

entries.name: Small Animal Fang
entries.description: Much more fun now that they’ve been removed from the mouth of a particularly angry critter. These teeth are surprisingly sharp, capable of piercing some armour. Scholars argue that the anima twist of Ashenfall makes the teeth more durable, whereas hunters would claim that the animals here are just more naturally belligerent than others. They prefer to use more colourful language to describe them, however.

entries.description: Children are often disappointed that this plant does not resemble an actual dragon. There are no snapping motions in these colourful leaves, and a depressing lack of firebreathing lizards in the stems.

entries.name: Soul Fragment
entries.description: A piece of a soul, half devoured by Imaru. Death seeks these to try and restore what he can of the lost, so that they might move on to the Afterlife.

entries.name: Steamed Beltfish
entries.description: The custom with a steamed beltfish is to eat it all in one, like a sword-eater swallowing their blade whole. The Moon Garou chomp it down like they were raised by pythons. The human gullet isn't quite built for this method of eating, so be careful if you're invited over for a Moon Garou celebration. Aim for the smaller ones at the banquet table. Chew subtly.

entries.description: Sticks and stones may break your bones, which makes them greatly desired in warfare. Stone can be found everywhere. In the grass, behind bushes, hiding in an uncomfortable part of your shoe just waiting for the right time to strike.

entries.name: Strong Sweet Tea
entries.description: The strong sweet tea is like being punched and kissed at the same time, which makes it something of an acquired taste. The Wise Old Man swears by it, and mumbles something about "liking my tea like I like my women", which we won't dig into for fear of getting the Wise Old Man cancelled.

entries.name: Strong Tea
entries.description: Only the most hardcore crones and witches will dare drink strong tea. We're talking about the ones with a twitch in their eye, who burble to themselves when no-one else is looking. They like it so strong that it resists the spoon, when a biscuit will bounce off the surface tension. It is said that the strong tea's aroma goes perfectly with a pair of twins roasting nicely in the stove.

entries.name: Sun Baked Sole
entries.description: Most Moon Garou would consider an adventurer's version of dune-smoking to be a pale imitation of the true process. 'Real' dune-smoking involves burying a raw desert sole deep within a dune, preferably a couple of metres down. Inside the dune, it alternately cooks and cools with the Scorch and cold nights. The sand helps to delay the rotting process, but - I am slightly debatably told by Moon Garou chefs - that a little bit of rotting never hurt anyone.

entries.name: Super Antipoison Potion
entries.description:
Once the desert was full of snakes, until they were banished below the sands by an angry goddess. Only rarely do they manage to break through the surface of the dunes to bite someone, and their venom has been concentrated so heavily by their solitude, that it’s lethal to anyone that suffers it.

Fortunately, the shamans were able to create this antipoison, stronger and more powerful than previous tiers. It has saved many lives.

entries.name: Super Focused Artisan Potion
entries.description:
Fermented with wild anima, this potion is a concentrated and more powerful version of its predecessor. The effects last longer and yet the power of the potion loses none of its efficiency.

Be warned, after drinking this potion, you may find yourself dreaming of assembling furniture, painting little clay decorations, and a billion other little crafty things that you would never have dreamed of before.

Just beware not to dream of the forbidden macramé, for in its strange knots do dark secrets dwell.

entries.description:
Have you ever wondered what it would be like to know nothing but bloodlust? To know nothing but the call  for battle and the need to slaughter?

Well, with this potion, you can! Condensed and fermented alongside wild anima, this potion will flood your system with so much adrenaline and aggression, that you’ll be looking to cause destruction on a catastrophic scale.

Ah, to be a zen-like architect, focused on nothing but crenulations and scaffolding. Such thoughts were nought but dreams before this potion, yet now you have a chance to soar to new heights of… err… masonry?

It’s hard to write about a potion that enhances your desire to build things. To wax lyrical about a liquid that grants greater XP when you craft new decorations and bigger stairs. Yet, here we are.

entries.name: Super Focused Fishing Potion
entries.description: If you want evidence of the strength of a super focused fishing potion, then look no further than Granny Potterington, who got mixed up and accidentally poured some into her pond. She came back the next day to find that one single fish had caught and eaten all the other fish in the pond. It had a confused look on its face and blood across its mouth and fins. Potent stuff.

entries.name: Super Focused Mining Potion
entries.description: There was a time when certain Moon Garou miners would down vial after vial of super focused mining potions. The hope was that they could find a mine, away from the Scorch, and work away at gypsum deposits without having to stop for hours. After the super focused potion wore off, they would step out of their trance state and survey the material for moonstones. It's likely a good explanation for why moonstones are so rare - perhaps even mythical - to the modern garou.

entries.description: Once this tar was some living creature, perhaps and ancient dragon or other colossal beast. Time and pressure refined it down into this sticky substance that can be used for a variety of crafting purposes.

entries.description: Woven from swamp weed, this thread is both stronger than it appears and magically stable. Enchantments woven into garments, crafted with this thread, are more potent than those woven with normal fibres.

entries.name: Tea Leaves
entries.description: Tea leaves have three uses, at least at the time of writing. The top survey answer is of course 'for making tea' - congratulations if you got that one. Then there's augury, using the tea leaves to divine the future. Finally - and this one's the pointless answer - if they are stuffed into someone's nostrils while they sleep, it will often induce the voiding of one's urine. It's true, go look it up. Information to hold back from your children, if you have any.

entries.name: Undead Bone
entries.description:
You may think an undead bone is no different from a normal bone, and in most cases that’s true. The animating forces of necromancy normally just puppet the bones, allowing them to be possessed by a spirit or controlled by some external force.

The undead of Fellhollow are different. They animated by the last remnants of their humanity, tiny bits of soul clinging on in tattered forms. They move because they need to and they shudder because they fear what happens when they stop.

As such, the bones of the Fellhollow dead have strange properties that a skilled craftsman can refine and find uses for.

Morbid, yes, but inventive.

entries.name: Undead Meat
entries.description:
Despite the appearance of their former owners, and the deeply unpleasant smell emanating from it, undead meat is not rotten. It, like the nature of its former owners, is preserved in a state between life and death, as if it’s on the cusp of souring, but never quite getting there.

This unique nature gives it some very interesting properties, but sadly taste isn’t one of them.

entries.name: Vault Core
entries.description:
A heart of alchemically modified rune essence. Layers of complex enchantments, and anima veins run through this core. It allows it to absorb ambient anima from its surroundings, which in term power the various functions of the vault guardian servitors.

This marvel of dragonkin science had revolutionary potential. The ability to create power sources that thrived off of the ambient anima of the region. Ashenfall, with it’s surfeit of magical power, was the perfect place for such a technology and the dragonkin would apply it to all of their arcane machinery.

entries.name: Velgar's Head
entries.description:
General Velgar was one of Queen Kuldra’s most feared disciples. Infused with the power of the earth itself, his poison corrupted entire regions and slaughtered countless foes.

The fall of Blue Flame Keep, Bramblemead village, and the Saradominist presence on Ashenfall, was orchestrated by Velgar’s hand. His army incinerated villagers, priests and soldiers alike. His forces tore down castles and houses with equal relish.

For thousands of years, Velgar has been a thorn in everyone’s side, until one hero took him down.

Bring this to the Wise OId Man, rumours are that he can make something useful from it.
pages:
General Velgar was one of Queen Kuldra’s most feared disciples. Infused with the power of the earth itself, his poison corrupted entire regions and slaughtered countless foes.

The fall of Blue Flame Keep, Bramblemead village, and the Saradominist presence on Ashenfall, was orchestrated by Velgar’s hand. His army incinerated villagers, priests and soldiers alike. His forces tore down castles and houses with equal relish.

For thousands of years, Velgar has been a thorn in everyone’s side, until one hero took him down.

Bring this to the Wise OId Man, rumours are that he can make something useful from it.

entries.name: Vile Ashes
entries.description:
Demons do not leave bones behind on death. That would require a skeleton, a prospect that would make a demon queasy. Instead, demons are magical entities, composed of essence and energies. On death, they disperse, leaving behind an ashy composite.

Don't be mistaken in thinking that it's similar to the ash left after a fire. Dab your tongue in vile ash and you'll soon understand where the 'vile' comes from.

entries.name: Vis Cloth
entries.description: Vis cloth is not the most comfortable material to wear. It's waxy, leaving a thin magical residue on the skin when worn. Wizards have compared it to skinning and wearing a giant slug, which isn't the best of adverts. They have complained about peeling it from their skin after a day of magical combat. If you're a hirsute magical user, you should be warned that it can rip a layer of hair from you whenever you use it. The wizards of Ashenfall's past may have had long beards, but you can be sure that there wasn't a scrap of hair on the rest of their bodies.

entries.name: Watermelon
entries.description:
Sometimes it’s not enough to drink water, you desire the urge to chomp on it instead. These melons are delicious and refreshing in ways that few other fruits seem able to match.

Smashing one with a hammer is not recommended, but still manages to be weirdly satisfying.

entries.name: Weapon Barbs
entries.description:
Used to craft Barbed Arrows or to coat your equipped melee weapon with barbs, causing Bleed buildup for a short duration.

Sometimes you just really want to hurt something. It happens. We each have that little voice that tells us to make something bleed, just a little.

Well, blacksmiths thought to themselves “what if we listen to that voice?” and created these little doohickies. Barbs for your weapons, so that they may tear, rend and otherwise force your opponents to bleed with every strike.

entries.name: Weapon Poison
entries.description:
Used in crafting Poison Arrows or to coat your equipped Melee Weapon with Poison for a short time.

There are times in life where you really want someone to regret ever meeting you. It could be a long-held grudge, it could be on the battlefield, or it could be in a never-ending meeting that could so easily have been an email but has now persisted past your lunchbreak and you had so been looking forward to that sushi… ahem… sorry, where was I? Oh, yes, pain!

Poison is sometimes considered to be a coward’s weapon. Personally, I prefer to think of it as the smart weapon choice, after all, honour is only worth anything if you’re the winner of the battle. A corpse with honour still rots in the dirt. With a blade coated in poison, you can almost guarantee the death of your enemies, all it takes is a single nick and their fate is sealed.

An investment well worth making, if you ask me.

entries.name: Wild Anima
entries.description: Magic is made up of motes of anima, refined and collected into specific forms. Rune essence can be made to hold these motes, creating dedicated magical components for spells and enchantments. Wild anima is useful for magical construction, but cannot be converted into true spellcraft, as the motes and unaligned and prone to strange reactions.

entries.name: Willow Logs
entries.description: Willow wood is a wonderful material. Flexible and yet strong and durable, it makes for an excellent resource in a variety of projects. Rare to find, it exists predominantly in small groves connected to a pool of water. Legend has it that the pools of water are formed from the tears of weeping willows, whose spirits lament the loss of a long-lost god.

entries.name: Wither Water
entries.description:
Drawn from pools of wither-rot water, lakes and streams poisoned by the waters of the river Noumenon – the river of the dead.

These waters have become corrupted by Imaru’s hunger and each drop longs to devour one’s soul.

entries.name: Withered Heart
entries.description:
The heart is a pump, nothing more, designed to push precious blood around the circulatory system, so that our weak and feeble frames can function. Yet, metaphysically, it is the most important organ, for it houses our emotional centre, the very essence of what makes us human.

A withered heart isn’t just a heart that has languished. Nor is it just a heart that is drained of blood. No, a withered heart has had all the humanity leeched from it, emptied of emotion, or connection, of self.

This process is imperfect, of course, and tiny fragments of soul-matter remains, that can be refined and extracted from the heart. Withdrawing the last remnants of what made the owner “them”.

entries.name: Bronze Logging Axe
entries.description:
Where bone and stone fail, metal provides. The bronze axe is strong enough to withstand greater force than its predecessors and can break through the bark of some of the strongest trees. On Ashenfall, nature has been hardened by the ambient magic, the bark of trees makes them resistant to most attacks. Yet, the bronze axe breaks through that barrier, not by magic, nor by cunning, but by sheer durability and resolve.

The lumberjacks of Brynmoor favoured bronze axes over iron. While iron was stronger and felled a tree quicker, the relatively cheapness and availability of copper and tin ore, made it a much more cost effective choice.

The villagers disapproved when the leadership pushed for iron in everything. They felt that bronze was more than enough for the village needs. But the lord wanted progress, and didn’t care about the price

entries.description: Wood breaks, shatters and splinters, which can be very frustrating when out in the garden. Metal is more durable and longer lasting, and bronze is a very malleable metal. With one of these spades you can assault the skin of the planet, reshaping Gielinor to suit your own grand designs.

entries.name: Bronze Watering Can
entries.description: While the druids relied on wooden watering cans, the more pragmatic farmers turned to metal. Bronze was sturdier, lasted longer and proved to ultimately be the better tool. Crops across Ashenfall found themselves constantly existing a state of blissful hydration, never knowing the agony of thirst.

entries.name: Compost Bucket
entries.description:
The first bucket on Gielinor was created by Mrs Hyacinth, to help her around the farm. They had buckets back on the human homeworld of Teragard, of course, but she hadn’t brought anything with her from the village Guthix had recruited her from.

The problem was that Mrs Hyacinth had a cow, named the traditional Bessie, that produced an unreasonable amount of manure, and Mrs Hyacinth needed something to help with the clear up.

She used local twigs, at first, weaving together more of a basket than a bucket, and the results were not as watertight as she had hoped. In the end, she meticulously combined strips of wood, tied together with cord, and they were able to withstand even the worst of Bessie’s endeavours.

Now, you too can fill one of these marvelous contraptions with horrifically pungent compost. Spread the smelly stuff across your farming plots and marvel at the health and happiness of your leafy little friends.

entries.description: Flammable objects pressed together into a smaller, even more flammable object. The fuel pellet burns hotter and stronger than basic fuels, making it much more desirable for more complex smithing techniques.

entries.name: Iron Logging Axe
entries.description:
While it might be cheaper to use bronze, there are some times when sheer power is necessary. For those times, a lumberjack need look no further than the glittering might of an iron axe’s blade. The mightiest of Ghornfell trees falls before its onslaught, and none in that region may stand against its might.

Iron was so powerful, that it created a problem in Brynmoor. The population craved the metal so desperately that they mined the region almost dry. This let to infighting, small civil skirmishes and the white knights of the Blue Flame Keep, needed to be brought in to keep the peace.

It is said that where iron goes, blood soon follows.

entries.name: Iron Secateurs
entries.description:
The best way to get leaves to stay healthy, is to instil within them a healthy sense of fear. By pruning away the leaves that have allowed themselves to fall to weakness, frailty and disease, you show the other leaves what happens if they don’t behave.

I find that whispering their failures to the plant, as I slice away parts of their extremities, emboldens the plant with a desire to thrive.

entries.name: Magical Focus
entries.description:
The wizard Mallory was never as good as he had hoped to be. He was proficient in spellcasting and his rote memory was excellent, but the power of his spells always fell a little short. He advanced through the ranks mostly through technicality, but he never quite earned the respect of his peers. 

That was until the day he created the focus. Mallory had always been good at making things. He enjoyed the simpler magic of crafting, and he found you could weave small threads of magic into the construction of something, breathing just a little bit more life and wonder into it than before. True craftsmanship, he believed, carried a little bit of the creator’s soul in it. 

The focus proved this theory and elevated it further. By creating a focus and subconsciously imbuing it with a bit of his essence, it would create a smoother, more fluid, channel of magic through the body, which created spells of greater potency. 

Tragically, after sharing his knowledge with the other wizards, he was murdered by his mentor. Who then took his knowledge and claimed it as his own. Karma is a stern judge, however, and the offending wizard later found himself being swallowed whole and digested by a dragon. 

Just punishment, I’m sure Mallory would agree.

entries.name: Mithril Logging Axe
entries.description:
It hurts Doric a little that you've used his prized mithril to make something that chops wood, but don't worry - he can be something of a snob. Dionysius often reminds him that he uses wood in his minecarts, pickaxe handles and toothpicks. 

Take some time to enjoy your increased capacity for woodcutting. There is a simple joy in watching your own increased efficiency.

entries.name: Mithril Pickaxe
entries.description:
A sign of mining distinction, the mithril pickaxe will get you noticed if you hang out with the right mining crowds. Doric in particularly will give you an appreciative wink. He might even toss you a rock cake or two. 

The mithril pickaxe is cold to the touch, incredibly reflective, and - most importantly - strong as an ox. You will no doubt have already realised that it makes short work of any deposit you find.

entries.name: Steel Spade
entries.description:
Fallen from too many tall buildings, only to be punished for your misstep by the cruel and malicious ground? Well, now is your chance to get your revenge. The smug soil doesn’t think you can touch it, but you can prove it wrong by stabbing it through it’s smug topsoil smirk with a nice steel spade.

Oh, sure, it’s great for gardening, but really this is a tool for sweet, sweet revenge.

entries.name: Stone Logging Axe
entries.description:
Trees are arrogant creatures, standing tall in the forests and refusing to bow to the wind. For decades they spread their roots claiming dominion over the nearby soil. The claws of beasts are a mere distraction. Raging storms barely rustle their leaves. They refuse to move for anyone, arrogant to the core.

Yet, it is not the wind, nor the heavens that shatter their resolve. Indeed, it is the lowliest of stones, refined to an edge. No matter how old the tree, how sturdy its fame, a single stone, the size of your fist, can bring the mightiest ash low.  

The stone axe is an alliance of such a rock, working together with branches cast aside in the tree’s hubris. Proof that even the lowliest of us can make a difference.

entries.name: Stone Pickaxe
entries.description: It is always a sad moment when brother must turn against brother. When we must strike at the heart of our own people. Such is the curse of the stone pickaxe, whose role in life is to strike at its brethren, cutting large rocks into pieces, so that they might better be put to use. The smaller stone, carved so sharply that it has nothing left but the edge, turns the action of a single swing into an force that can shatter the largest boulder. There’s a metaphor there, I’m sure.

entries.name: Whetstone
entries.description:
The blade is not just a weapon in the wilds of Ashenfall, it’s a tool. Sometimes it’s the difference between seeing tomorrow and having a very bad today. 

Dwarves have always understood the importance of properly maintaining one’s equipment. They turned the care for their weapons into a ritual of almost religious significance. Blades would be cleaned, serviced and sharpened so that they might cut through deadlier dangers and challenge greater threats. 

The whetstone is a simple device, but one that served as a backbone of this ritual. A smith would learn to gently sharpen the blade to the thinnest edge possible, treating it almost like a competition. They would boast and brag with each other about the sharpness of their blades. 

A popular dwarven myth speaks of the Prime Whetstone, capable of sharpening a blade to the point that no armour or metal could withstand it. Sadly, or perhaps thankfully, no evidence exists to provide any truth to the myth.

entries.description: Sometimes the very earth itself must be punished for its cruelty! These wooden tools, simple and elegant, can break through the planet’s crust, letting you show Gielinor exactly who’s boss.

entries.name: Ash Longbow
entries.description:
Many a villager longed to be a master archer. The youngsters would spend hours shooting cabbages, potatoes and whatever fruit or vegetable they could get their hands on, all to prove they had what it took to be a master of the bow. 

The ash longbow was their first weapon in this journey. Many wouldn't be able to muster the strength needed to pull the string taught. More still would struggle to fire the arrow straight, missing their targets by embarrassingly large distances. But those who could wield the bow, who could strike the cabbages from as far as possible, they would become the most popular of the Bramblemead youngsters.

entries.name: Ash Shortbow
entries.description:
An ash shortbow is the first weapon most young archers train with. It’s easy to make and, therefore, not so problematic if it breaks during training. Human villagers would often craft their first bows together under the tutelage of a visiting Wild Knight. They would use branches that had naturally fallen from the trees and carefully whittle them into the bow’s limbs. Bowstrings would be created by gathering flax from the nearby fields and spinning them into thin but hardy threads. 

Most would break on first use. Some would break before the first arrow was fired. Still, village youngsters would laugh at their misfortunes and start the whole process again. Each time improving. Each new bow sturdier than the last.

entries.name: Black Greataxe
entries.description: Black metal was most commonly used for armours, crossbows and swords. On occasion, it was used for a greataxe. The reason is not a pleasant one. They were almost exhaustively the tool of an executioner, when the crime merited a public execution. The black metal was a message: you have betrayed the Children of Shadows, and your death will come from the metal of our own.

entries.name: Black Sword
entries.description:
Where the mithril crossbow is the standard issue of the ranged Black Knight, the black sword is standard for footsoldiers. 

'Black', you may be aware, is not a material. It is instead a descriptor for steel that has gone through a process similar to vulcanisation. There was a time when the vulcanisation was performed by the dragon Xikotal, as a gift to the isolationist knights.

With his death, the process moved towards the demonic. The resulting quality is lower, which has made the original, dragonfire 'black' metal sought after in Dowdun Reach.

entries.name: Blightwood Battlestaff
entries.description:
The stranger the wood, the more powerful the magic. It’s unsure why this is, but it’s been true since magic was first discovered. When used as a tool for destructive magic, Garou druids learned the power of blightwood. 

Ashien, a legendary druid among the garou, was among the first to wield such a weapon. As the story goes, they were wandering the swamps when the goddess Lougrim came to her in a vision and gave her a quest. Ashien was to journey deep into the swamps and do battle with a demon that dwelled within. 

They found the demon; it emerged out of the fog with a chilling screech and destroyed their staff with a single swing of its blade-like claw. In panic, Ashien blindly reached for the nearest weapon, the root of a swamp tree that had fallen in the mud. Through it, they channeled their will to survive, and it burst free of the branch as a flash of lightning. 

The creature burned beneath Ashien’s gaze, vanishing back into the mists as if it never were. 

Since then, garou druids would favour blightwood when crafting a staff.

entries.name: Blightwood Longbow
entries.description:
The wild creatures of Ashenfall have always been elusive. Bramblemead villagers would tell wild stories about the deer that got away or the sheep that shrugged off an arrow. Still, those who could wield a bow rarely left their family hungry. 

One Wild Knight, Frode, was so skilled with the bow that he never returned from a hunt empty-handed. His siblings among the Wild Knights would send him out hunting before every great gathering so that they might feast heartily upon his return. For years, this was their happiest tradition. 

Until the day he did not return. 

It is said that his body was found in five separate places, spread out across the forests of Brynmoor like some gruesome compass. His quiver was empty, yet none of his arrows – marked as they were, with his symbol, an owl – would ever be found.
