entries.name: Blightwood Shortbow
entries.description:
Every hunter reaches a crossroads in life when a choice becomes clear. They have honed their skills with a bow, surpassing the challenges posed by the Brynmoor prey. They could settle into a comfortable life in the village—hunting the same old deer, earning a regular wage, and basking in a relaxing level of respect from their peers. Or, they could dare to dream bigger, to push their skills to new heights. 

The Wild Knights journeyed into more dangerous territories, facing off against deadly monsters warped by the anima twist. Joining them would mean abandoning the comfortable life of friends and family but earning a chance to face challenges that they would never face at home. 

Most choose comfort, as one might expect. But those who choose to improve would be taught how to craft a more powerful weapon, casting aside the oak bows that carry their names. They would carve a new name and identity into the limbs of their latest weapon and join the knights. Their names would be whispered, and gossip about them would transform into fireside stories—ghost tales about those still alive—the first embers of legends.

entries.name: Blurite Crossbow
entries.description:
For centuries alchemists have yearned to create gold. To transmute base metals into something pure and shiny. While gold is the goal, there are other, stranger metals, along the way, and what could be more bizarre than a bar of purest blue.

Blurite is defined by its colour. It’s in the very name. Yet it offers no real magical, or alchemical value beyond other metals. Artistic, perhaps, it was favoured by poets, bards and artisans of more eccentric tastes, but it still offered little in the way of superior weaponry.

That was until Gothren Actillian took a crack at it. He was an blacksmith, obsessed with the less desired metals and materials. He would hunt for hours in the darkest caverns for slivers of blue, ignoring glittering silver and gold. To him the metal was special, radiant and beautiful. The hues generated a joy in him that he could not describe, and he longed to craft it into something befitting its splendour. He was delighted when he found the ore glittering away in a hidden dragonkin vault in Ghornfell's central region. 

He was never any good with a sword, and his magical prowess wouldn’t frighten a kebbit. Yet crossbows, those he could wield. He was a skilled marksman, and could knock an apple from a chinchompa’s head before it exploded.

The crossbow, blue as the ocean, caused much mockery from his companions, yet their mockery soon died as he speared a bolt through the heart of a dragon. Something all of their weapons had failed to do.

He was just disappointed that the dragon’s scales were green and went searching for that ever elusive blue.

entries.name: Bone Club
entries.description:
Animal bones are surprisingly durable, especially those found on Ashenfall. The magic of the continent seeps into their marrow, slowly strengthening them and making them tougher. This goes some way to explaining the ferocity of ordinarily docile creatures, but it also helps when crafting tools. 

Cows and similar beasts were celebrated in the age of Guthix. The people of Brynmoor preferred to take an animal’s life only on the hunt or after long years of service. When an animal passed, it was thanked for its sacrifice, and the materials helped strengthen the village. 

A club forged of bone was a simple tool but one that made defending the village much easier. Roving beasts were easily pushed back, and the village was protected by the animal’s last gifts.

entries.name: Bone Dagger
entries.description:
Before he learned to use the bow, Ulv survived with simple daggers of bone. He lived outside the village, cast out for his silence and strange ways. Ulv did not follow the polite nonsense of human society, nor did he seem to care for their troubles. The boy was happy just to survive and whittle small carvings of animals from fallen branches. 

He hunted silently, using the daggers to slay small prey such as rabbits and chickens. He ate what he needed and sold the excess at the markets for enough coin to purchase simple clothes and tools. 

When he was thirteen, he was beaten by bandits and left for dead. But a Wild Knight found him and brought him to safety. Recovering in the knight’s home, Ulv would be taught how to use a bow, a skill he soon mastered. 

When a wolf attacked Bramblemead, this outcast slew it. Villagers thanked him for his bravery and asked him what he wanted as a reward. He refuted their offers and asked only for the wolf’s skull in return. He fashioned it into a mask that he chose as a new face, one he wore away from the village that had spurned him.

entries.name: Bronze Crossbow
entries.description:
The members of the Wild Knights who trained with melee weapons, generally found themselves the victors in friendly sparring matches against their companions. The reasoning was simple – shields. A shield could turn aside blade, arrow and spell, with equal skill and it left their enemy vulnerable to counterattack. This sense of superiority began to change from friendly competition, into a sense of smugness capable of souring many friendships.

Roliker Hallister was particularly obnoxious. His skill with sword and shield was admittedly impressive. At the age of twenty he could best even some of the commanders of the Wild Knights in single combat. Healthy pride twisted into smug egoism, which then rotted down into unpleasant superiority. He was rude. He was dismissive. He was pretty much an obnoxious nightmare to be around.

Which is why he was very surprised by the bolt in his shoulder, and why no one else seemed too inclined to help him out. Vanida Mox was a skilled archer and inventor. She was quick to learn, quick to study and she had the enviable ability to see when something was wrong and work to find a solution. Popular with the other knights, because she would work with them, share accolades, and stand for what the order truly meant – a barrier between the world and the wild.

As Roliker’s ego grew and grew, she realised that the archers in the order were at a significant disadvantage in close combat. At range, they were obviously superior, but as all the sparring matches were held in the courtyard, there was precious little distance available. So she began working on a device that would deliver the power of an arrow but allowing one hand free to hold a shield.

It was very effective.

She named it a “cross-bow”, because she was very very angry when she unloaded it into the cloud of smugness known as Roliker. Later that name would be attributes to the mechanical structure of the device, but now you know better.

entries.name: Bronze Greatsword
entries.description:
The Wild Knight Kessel was unusual in her choice of weaponry. Where most of the order chose to wield bows, daggers, or swift blades, Kessel favoured a bronze greatsword. On the battlefield, she hefted it across her shoulders, never letting the hilt leave her grip.  

As one of the Amalgamated, Kessel’s skin glowed like burning coals, her battle scars resembling faint reddish embers. She harnessed this heat, channelling it through her sword. Her magic set the blade ablaze, a sight that struck terror into the hearts of her enemies. With great arcs of red flame, she cleaved through enemy forces, incinerating them as she severed their limbs from their bodies. 

On one fateful day, she would use this technique against a force of garou hunters. The battle was long, hard, and brutal, and both sides faced great casualties. But it was when she sliced her blade across the young garou prince that war was inevitable.

entries.name: Bronze Sword
entries.description:
Legend has it that when the first sword was forged, Guthix wept. Given that Guthix commissioned warriors and soldiers and, at times, encouraged war, this is perhaps not a truthful statement. Yet, the sword is a weapon with a singular purpose: to end the life of another. Of course, this is true of all weapons, but none so iconic as the blade. 

Children would play in the street, striking one another with wooden blades rather than clubs or daggers. They would pretend to be knights rather than brigands or priests. To wield a blade was a sign of bravery. To draw a sword was the hero’s stance. 

War shatters all childhood dreams. 

Nothing removes the nonsense of chivalry more than seeing the life leaving the eyes of a terrified foe. A sword puts the wielder in that moment, forcing them to face what it is they destroy. To understand that there are no such things as heroes, only warrior against warrior and knowing that one of them will fall.

entries.name: Crystal Bow
entries.description:
Crystal bows are not crafted but sung into existence. Harmonies are layered over one another to teach the weapon a story so that it might understand why it needs to be strong. Traditionally, the plight of the elves, their loneliness without their goddess, and the many dangers they must face are sung. 

The shimmering substance they’re made from is traditionally a shard of the elven goddess Seren, left behind when her crystal form shattered at the end of the Third Age God Wars. 

This bow isn’t the same material, and the song is different, too. There’s no divine essence in the crystal, no lament of the elves. Instead, it is sung memories of a lifetime together, distilled down into facets reflecting in the crystalline flaws. In the moonlight, those facets sparkle like tiny stars held within glass—moments of hardship, conflict, happiness, and grief. 

It is music as a weapon, with memory as the handle and sorrow as the string.

entries.name: Draconic Staff
entries.description:
Rasthin was a powerful sorceress, even among the dragonkin. She had mastered all manner of spells, and was even schooled in the techniques from the previous Revision.

Still, magic as an art was largely looked down upon by dragonkin society. It was considered vulgar, and the obsession of children, and alchemy and science was the real way forward. In part it’s because of the connection between magic and the hated Elder Gods, and the dragonkin feared rousing, further, their anger.

But Rasthin knew the value of magic, as did the other members of her group. She created a staff, forged from glittering crystal and anima-infused iron, which allowed her to channel her magic into powerful spells.

Yet, even with a weapon as powerful as this, she discarded her magic when she uncovered the power of Ashenfall – preferring, instead, to enjoy her newfound connection with elemental flame.

Still, the remnants of the staff bristle with potential, and while they may never reach the might of their ancestor, they remain powerful magic tools just waiting to be crafted.

entries.name: Dragonbone Dagger
entries.description:
Viika was never fond of creating dragons, they thought the process was cruel and unbecoming. When an egg was laid, Viika saw in that moment both the egg and the dragon it would become. They saw past and presence at the same time, and they grieved the creature before it had even hatched.

They pleaded with their sibling, and with the other Dragonkin, to change their treatment of the beasts. But Viika’s curse, like so many Seers, was to be ignored by their kindred.

A rare egg hatched once, containing a dragon with white scales like pearls. The dragon was infused with magic and possessing a power capable of travelling to other worlds, where she might have lived a happier life. But Viika wept, for they knew she would manage no such ending.

Viika kept the hatchling company. Treated them like their dearest friend, and held them softly when Lacrussa’s need for knowledge, took the dragon’s last breath.

The Seer kept only a single keepsake – a blade carved from the tooth of their white-scaled friend. A dagger capable of terrible damage, but as fragile as the friendship that it reminded them of.

entries.name: Goblin "Swingslash"
entries.description:
Contrary to popular belief, a goblin is as smart as any other species. It was Bandos that instilled within them the notion that intelligence was a sin, and demonstrating your education was something to be discouraged. As a result, goblins often go out of their way to make themselves seem less intelligent than they really are.

Hence “swingslash”, the name given to this axe because of how it swings through the air, slashing anything it hits. It’s so reductive and silly, it can only be an overcorrection, a desperate attempt by the creator to seem dumber than they are.

You can ignore, therefore the curve of the blade and the sharpness of the edge, created by carefully thought-out techniques that make the weapon deadlier than those before them. The name, chosen by the blacksmith, so none might accuse them of the crime of being smart.

entries.name: Greataxe Thane
entries.description:
Might makes right. This is the truth of the Garou philosophy. Strength and cunning dominates all. The Garou thanes demonstrate this might in the weapons they wield. Though heavier and more tiring, this axe swings with deadly force, capable of cleaving through almost any armour.

The design is passed down to the garou from templates granted to the first garou blacksmiths by divine revelation. Lougrim taught them about the curve of the blade, and the heft of the hilt. Designed for the hunt, it could fell most quarry in a single blow.

Under Kuldra’s leadership, the chosen quarry was human. The dragon queen had a deep hatred for the humans, she found them weak, petty and flawed. The Thanes carried out her orders, using the axe to wield their authority, in her name.

entries.name: Imaru's Talon
entries.description:
The essence of an undead dragon, distilled down into a blade. What could go wrong?

This weapon is cold to the touch in ways far beyond chilling. Holding it feels as if you’re out in the cold, with no shelter to protect you. Exposure in the palm of your hand.

Worse than the cold, is the hunger. This scimitar wants to cut, to stab, to slice and to maim. It wants to see your enemies bleed so that it can feast on their suffering. Imaru may be dead, but her hunger is eternal and you feel it infecting you with each swing of the blade.

Still, the power of this blade makes it almost worth it. What’s a little hunger when faced with the destruction of your foes? Lament later, surely, and revel now in the carnage. Perhaps there’s a little dragon in you too?

entries.name: Iron Crossbow
entries.description:
Iron turned the war against the garou more than some people would like to admit. They would claim superior training, tactics, and skills of their soldiers, but the truth is far simpler. Iron was strong and iron weapons were brutal.

Ranged weapons proved effective against the garou leadership, bound as they were by strict codes of honour. A thane was a deadly opponent up close, but if you could pierce their internal organs before they were within a swing’s reach, then they were no more dangerous than any other beast. It is perhaps no surprise then, that there was a race to create weapons to challenge them.

The people of Brynmoor had learned of a Wild Knight invention, a weapon that would allow one to deliver powerful ranged attacks, whilst still allowing the bearer to wield a shield. They took this design, studied and refined it and then upgraded it to include the power of iron weapons.

Garou numbers dropped rapidly as a result, turning the war heavily against them. In their desperation, the garou turned to their goddess and she, in turn, sought allies with deadlier weapons still.

entries.name: Iron Dagger
entries.description:
Iron daggers are dangerous weapons in the hands of someone skilled. Light, quick, and sharp as can be, they cleave flesh from bone before the victim knows they’ve been assaulted. This is why they became a favourite weapon of the Children of Shadows. 

Though the cult rarely harmed anyone -- it was mostly a social club -- there were those among their number who took their calling seriously. 

They smith daggers themselves, and as the blade cooled, they added a single drop of their own blood in honour of their master. Some carved demonic pacts into the blades, though none are known to actually create such a contract.

entries.name: Iron Greataxe
entries.description:
Few sights are as intimidating as a great axe hefted toward you. It can only be carried in a pose that exudes raw strength, and a bearer of such a weapon can rarely look meek. 

Bandos was also a fan of the aesthetic. While he favoured the sheer brutality of the kyzaj, he chose to wield a great axe against Velgar. He stormed Brakka’s Folly, great axe in hand, and challenged the dragon to single combat. A god versus a dragon, the outcome felt obvious, yet it did not play out how Bandos expected. 

It should have been easy. Yet Velgar’s stone-touched flesh turned away blows, and his poisonous breath leeched even Bandos’ strength. Bandos cut a great scar down Velgar’s side, yet the wound was not fatal, and the counterattack sent Bandos reeling. 

He never surrendered, but there was no victory for the big high war god. He sounded a tactical retreat, seeking superior tactics – far, far away.

entries.name: Iron Mace
entries.description:
Few instruments are as good at shattering bones as the iron mace. It was a favourite weapon of White Knight paladins, who dreamed of shattering the bones of the risen dead. Necromancy was rare on Ashenfall, though not unheard of. Two necromancers had been reported to the order, one a girl with a knack for bones and another who whispered with the dead. Neither summoned skeletal hordes for the knights to shatter. 

But garou and goblin bones broke just as well. In the war against the garou, Sir Lear, a white knight paladin, used the mace to great effect. He crushed warriors, battered druids, and shattered the shields of powerful thanes. He was a symbol of the might of Saradomin’s faithful when faced with overwhelming odds. 

He joined the Wild Knight commander, Vemmeck, in their siege against a northern garou stronghold. With countless goblins at their side, their victory was almost assured. Yet a single druid’s magic held the forces at bay until Sir Lear learned how ineffective his mace was against the scales of a dragon.

entries.name: Longbow Hunter Stagbow
entries.description:
Gahl was a garou druid who lost everyone he knew. In the wars inflicted on his people by the other races of Ashenfall, he grew jaded with the cruelty he saw all around him. This reached its peak when he found a garou village in ruins and goblins dancing and laughing as they threatened a newly born pup, in her crib.

The village is gone now, dragged beneath the soil. Gahl’s vengeance unleashed upon the goblins, erasing them from existence. He took the child as his own and raised her in a way alien to his people – he raised her with love.

She had no talent for magic, and could not learn his druid spells, so he taught her how to hunt with a bow, and she was a natural. Dahnu, as he named her, made a bow out of the first deer she and her father had hunted and that bow became a symbol to all she encountered.

In time she would claim a king’s seat. Defeating the prior monarch with reason and wit. Charming him out of his power and offering her people another way.  

Her people thrived, making her father proud.

Until Velgar brought her reign to an end.

entries.name: Maple Battlestaff
entries.description:
The Children of Shadows were never a grateful sort, but they would acknowledge that the groves of maple in Dowdun Reach were a boon. Almost everything wooden in the keep - from the library bookcases to the bannisters - was made from maple. 

Alric relished walking among the maple trees. For so much of his life, he had been encased in stone and surrounded by essence: working long hours in the keep. But the maples were for thinking. 

In his twilight years, Alric carried a maple staff with him: the Subjugation Staff. It was a crutch for an old man, yes, but it was also a way to bring the grove with him. When he couldn't muster the energy to visit his favoured trees, he carried a remnant with him.

entries.name: Maple Shortbow
entries.description:
Putrilius, the cthonian demon, will tell you that any living thing can be possessed. If needs must, a cthonian can be a cockroach or spider, for a time. 

In one desperate moment, after the Dreaming Stone was shattered, Putrilius was forced to possess a maple tree. It wasn't an experience she enjoyed. Most curiously, she found themselves aligning to the maple's inner cadence. Everything slowed. Putrilius barely registered a thought in two years.

What woke Putrilius was a logging axe. Their maple body was toppled and then fletched into an armature. For a moment, as Putrilius's life faded from the wood, she was a shortbow. 

It was the closest she had come to dying. With a cognitive spark, she moved from the bow to a passing hound before all her lifeforce ebbed away.

entries.name: Mithril Crossbow
entries.description:
A mithril crossbow is the standard issue for any modern Black Knight. If you showed capability, then you might be promoted to Black Knight Sniper, and that came with the Black Sniper Crossbow. But for the average Black Knight, the crossbow was a long-kept friend. 

The crossbow's main purpose was to stop demons in their tracks. The Zamorakian magi claimed to keep their demon hordes under control, but demons tested that claim.

The crossbow had other uses. Remove the bolt, rest the crossbow on the floor stock-upwards, and you had a stool. Sit on the floor and it was a headrest. 

You could also waste time shooting ravens. Shooting the red, glowing ravens was an immediate dismissal, however. Alric demanded they were protected, for reasons that he never expanded on.

entries.name: Mithril Greataxe
entries.description:
In the early years of Dowdun Reach, the concept of a mithril greataxe would have been unthinkable. A big, showy weapon that used large quantities of mithril would have been seen as a betrayal. The Children of Shadows, holding a monopoly on mithril, wanted to present it as a rare metal. At best, the richest on Ashenfall might have a brooch or tiara that sparkled with mithril. 

Nowadays, Doric can have two greataxes whipped up for you before dinner. Much has changed.

entries.name: Mithril Greatsword
entries.description:
"You see a mithril greatsword, I see a mithril dagger," Vannaka would say. He would then pick two up from Doric's forge, one in each hand, and try not to register effort. It was a routine, a little play, between Vannaka and Doric. 

This time, however, the joke was on Vannaka. Doric had made his mam's rock cakes, and folded some mithril round them - one for each hilt. 

Vannaka wobbled. "Cripes," he said.

entries.name: Mithril Mace
entries.description:
The standard term is mace, but Vannaka prefers bludgeon. "It's one of those sound words, like stomp and grunt, right? When I hit someone with it, it bludges. Bludge, bludge, bludge."

"You're thinking of onomatopoeia," Dionysius said, helpfully. 

"Nah, but good try. I'm thinking of breakfast," said Vannaka.

entries.name: Mithril Scimitar
entries.description:
The scimitar form is not commonplace on Ashenfall. Unlike the mainland (where you can't walk five metres in the Kharidian Desert without getting slashed by one), the scimitar is a rarity. Only an offshoot of the Garou, found in some of the harshest deserts of Ashenfall, are known to wield it. 

That is likely to change, of course, as more adventurers make landfall. It makes you wonder what the island will look like in five, ten years' time as the cultures intertwine.

entries.name: Mithril Warhammer
entries.description:
The mithril warhammer was once the weapon most associated with Lord Rasmodel of Dowdun Reach. He was rarely seen without it. In the mornings, when he was most in pain, it would be a prop, something to lean on while the night's watch recounted the events of the early hours. In the afternoons, it was a beautiful warning, a threat of what might happen if you disobeyed him.

Lord Rasmodel wasn't one for naming his weapons. He found the custom a little juvenile. But when his thoughts were elsewhere, you might see him pat the head of the warhammer. There was kinship there, even if he wouldn't admit it.

entries.name: Necromancer's Staff
entries.description:
Necromancy isn’t inherently evil, despite what some of the scriptures might say. Whilst some cruelly force the dead into service, others make bargains and pacts with spirits, offering them a chance to influence the mortal world again, rather than simply watch events unfold.

In Fellhollow a small group of mages encountered a smoking fissure in the earth. From it they heard strange whispering voices in the darkness, promising them power and knowledge. Greedily they listened, making pacts with the whispering in exchange for the ability to bind the dead to their service.

In life they performed their arts in secret, raising corpses none would miss, or binding ghosts no one even knew were haunting them. Yet in death, that’s where their true power lay.

With their souls withered away and consumed by the dread Imaru, the necromancers were no longer limited by the last vestiges of morality, and with the new powers at their command, turned a struggling defence against the undead, into a horror-filled nightmare where each fallen ally would rise as a foe.

entries.name: Oak Longbow
entries.description:
The longbow is every hunter’s friend. Capable of taking down prey over a greater range than the shortbow, it has been the end of many a deer trying to flee through the woods. 

Bramblemead would host a thrilling archery tournament. The villagers would proudly bring their own longbows, meticulously crafted by hand, and compete to take down cleverly hidden targets scattered across the village. It was a spectacle of skill and precision, with the only rule being that the target must be shootable from the open street. 

With the introduction of magic, the competition took on a whole new level of silliness. Participants conjured magical air currents that sent arrows astray – often into unsuspecting washing lines or pies cooling on windowsills – or they would playfully blast arrows out of the air with fire spells. 

However, this stopped after the Amalgamated archer, Derien, joined the game. Gifted with the element of air, his arrows curved gracefully with each shot, missing traps, tricks and deceptions. His victory earned the Amalgamated more jealousy, which led to the competition ending out of envious spite.

entries.name: Shadow Crossbow
entries.description:
Climb the turrets of Dowdun Reach in its prime, and you would have found the Black Knight Snipers. These were the elite marksmen of the Black Knights, tasked with looking outward when the rest of the order would look inward. They would scan the skyline for threat - for the beating wings of a dragon. There was no greater trophy for the Black Snipers.

One one occasion, a bolt was loosed at Imaru. She had arrived at the keep for diplomatic purposes, and was rewarded with a bolt to the neck. You could see the conflict within her, as her urges were swallowed. For a second, a disdainful eye moved to the Black Sniper. But she reset and continued to talk to Lord Rasmodel and Alric like nothing happened.

Restraint was certainly beaten into the Black Snipers that night.

entries.name: Shortbow Wild Scout
entries.description:
There was magic once, in this bow, though it has mostly faded now. Runes were ground down and mixed with plant oils, to create a special resin that allowed the Wild Knights to work their magic through the bow, as if they were carrying runes. That magic has faded away, and the recipe for the mixture lost to the ages, but these bows are still formidable in their own right.

Wild Knights told tales of creatures that lived within the wilds of Ashenfall, that could not be felled by normal bows. Deer with hides that glistened with starlight, sheep who’s silver fleeces repelled all arrows. They claimed that these magically infused bows were the only ones capable of harming the creatures, though none ever returned with trophies to share.

entries.name: Skullsplitter
entries.description:
Garou children would often play pretend at great, epic, battles. They would create their own stories, true, but they enjoyed reenacting the battles of legend, and no character was more popular than King Raluh, the mighty.

Pups would wander into the forests in search of the sturdiest stick they could find and then announce to the other children that they were the king, and this stick that most legendary of weapons – Skullsplitter.

As the legends go, King Raluh had been granted a weapon by the moon goddess, Lougrim. A weapon capable of destroying any foe. Armour was as paper to Skullsplitter and the fables had him crush the bones of villain and monster alike.

It is, therefore, no surprise that as the garou pups mature, they create weapons to match the legends, and garou warriors wield mighty maces carrying that mythical name. Though the true Skullsplitter may be just a story, these powerful imitations are no less deadly.

entries.name: Splitbark Staff
entries.description:
Magic always inspires people. Something about rewriting the underpinning rules of your reality, with little more than force of will and a handful of stones, makes people reach for lofty goals. In Fellhollow it was the wizard Falistrius that wanted to make a name for themselves.

They wanted to be a magical scholar. A researching who might uncover the secrets of the universe itself. They sought spells of greater and greater power, dabbling in mysteries both profane and forbidden, and came up empty handed.

After constantly searching for power, it was an unexpected duel that would grant her the fame she sought, at a price she would have preferred to avoid. A travelling elven sorcerer arrived in the village of Emberwood one night and the local drunk foolishly picked a fight with him. Unfortunately for Falistrius that drunk was her wife.

The elf challenged the drunk to a duel, for satisfaction over a drink spilled, and by local custom Falistrius was forced to answer. They met in the forests of Fellhollow, and unleashed their magic.

The elf’s spells were like nothing she had ever seen before. Cold and dark, sanguine and terrible, they tore into her magical defences like they were nothing and writhed inside her soul like a foul nightmare. Against the strain, her staff shattered, leaving her vulnerable and in desperation she grasped a fallen hollow tree branch and urged her magic through it.

It wasn’t enough to save her. But it was enough to earn the respect and satisfaction of the sorcerer, who left the region with his pale-skinned cohorts. Ever since then, young Fellhollow mages would craft staves from the hollow bark from the forest, in memory of Falistrius.

entries.name: Staff of Light
entries.description:
In the third age, before someone could wield a staff of light, it would first need to be blessed by three people. 

A priest would bless it first, instilling the weapon with Saradomin’s wisdom. A monk would bless it second, imbuing the staff with the humility of Saradomin. Finally, an icyene general would give their blessing, dedicating the weapon to Saradomin’s righteousness. 

Those battlemages chosen to wield such a sacred weapon would dive into battle against Zamorak’s forces and believe themselves invulnerable. 

They were often proved wrong. 

Yet, those who carried the staff into battle seemed to survive longer than their compatriots. The defensive magic of the staff kept them alive longer than others. A demon once stole a staff and tried to use that power for himself. Still, when he tried to channel demonic power through the staff, it is said that the explosion could be seen from across the battlefield.
pages:
In the third age, before someone could wield a staff of light, it would first need to be blessed by three people. 

A priest would bless it first, instilling the weapon with Saradomin’s wisdom. A monk would bless it second, imbuing the staff with the humility of Saradomin. Finally, an icyene general would give their blessing, dedicating the weapon to Saradomin’s righteousness. 

Those battlemages chosen to wield such a sacred weapon would dive into battle against Zamorak’s forces and believe themselves invulnerable. 

They were often proved wrong. 

Yet, those who carried the staff into battle seemed to survive longer than their compatriots. The defensive magic of the staff kept them alive longer than others. A demon once stole a staff and tried to use that power for himself. Still, when he tried to channel demonic power through the staff, it is said that the explosion could be seen from across the battlefield.

entries.name: Steel Crossbow
entries.description:
There were no garou in Fellhollow for the people to deal with, so in the early days of the settlement people created steel crossbows primarily for hunting game. The dragons that guarded the people were gentle creatures, but possessed of an enormity so great that they required a great deal of food to keep going. Hunting, therefore, became a very popular activity, with many competitions and events crafted to provide meals for the draconic caretakers. 

When the withering began to spread and the dead began to rise, steel bolts proved just as effective at piercing a zombie’s skull, as it would catching the quarry from a hunt. 

Though the dead would come in droves, the crossbow would let them be taken out at great distance, keeping the last remaining settlements safter for just a few days longer. Every moment counted in those final days.

entries.name: Steel Greataxe
entries.description:
Power corrupts, and what’s more powerful than an enormous axe comprised of a metal stronger than any seen before? Such was the logic of Olga Skulltaker (not her real name), the self-styled bandit queen of Fellhollow.

As a child, Olga had always enjoyed listening to her grandfather’s stories from the mainland. Tales of mighty warriors defeating terrifying foes. Purehearted heroes challenging evil knights to great battles across pointlessly high bridges and the like. Her parents always laughed and called her “their little hero” but the truth was she was far more interested in the villain.

When she was old enough to wield a weapon, she trained with the biggest axes she could carry, and her sparring partners feared facing off against her because she always took things too far. Once even costing another student their fingers.

As an adult, she found a place for herself among the Children of Shadows. She had hoped they would be dangerous, wicked people, like herself, but instead they spend their time reciting terrible poetry and talking about evil, without ever doing it.

So she took her axe, changed her name, and found the highest bridge she could, and attacked anyone that tried to cross it.

entries.name: Steel Greatsword
entries.description:
It was the followers of Armadyl who enjoyed the greatsword so much, in defiance of the bows that were more the more traditional choice. They said that it reminded them of the legend of the godsword, and would lament not knowing the secrets of forging one, as it would be quite useful against the godeater, Kuldra, and her call for humanity’s death.

Sadly for the villagers, the art of godsword creation was never discovered, so they turned to steel instead. Whilst significantly less flashy, and almost certainly not going to terrify any deities, a steel sword will do significant damage to anything not divinely attuned.

entries.name: Steel Mace
entries.description:
The priests of Emberwood village were not as militant as their fellows back in Brynmoor. They saw little need for weapons, when a dragon watched over their flock. Still, they carried steel maces by their side as a symbol of office, each one ornately engraved with the symbol of their chosen deity.

Although the Saradominist priests had first insisted that different faiths could only turn on one another, they found an odd sort of kinship in their fellows and would regularly enjoy debates of the merits and flaws of each other’s faiths.

entries.name: Steel Scimitar
entries.description:
It is said that the origins of the scimitar come from Al Kharid, where skilled swordsmen would wield them in a dazzling manner akin to a dance. Travelling dignitaries would be wowed by the spectacle, applauding great choreographed sword clashes that dramatized legendary battles of history’s past.

They were brought to Ashenfall by a noble family during the god wars, who had taken up the scimitar as their weapon of choice, in service, of course, of the mighty Saradomin. This family was proud and pious, which made them all the more concerned when their daughter was one of the first to show signs of Amalgamation.

Love, for once, triumphed over prejudice, and the family scorned their wealth and prestige in order to protect their child and they joined many others who fled the growing unrest in the village of Bramblemead and travelled north to Fellhollow. There, they taught the secrets of the scimitar to the local blacksmiths, and the weapon found itself a great deal of popularity in the times to come.

entries.name: Steel Sword
entries.description:
Atilius Rasmodel was a proud and powerful knight. Her skill with the sword was without compare and her bravery seemingly infinite against the dangers in Fellhollow. She was chosen by Imaru as one of her guards, not that a dragon needed such a thing, and she was made responsible for the defence of the dragons when they fell into the weeks long torpors they were known to suffer.

She called herself the Dragon Knight, even though such a title was unofficial and self-proclaimed, it soon stuck among the village people and they would bow and nod in appreciation of her skill as they passed her.

When Kuldra descended on the region, demanding humanity’s destruction, Atilius climbed on Xikotal’s back in hope to drive her steel blade through the Godeater’s heart. She died beside the dragon she had sworn to protect, free of all remorse, in the line of duty.

entries.name: Steel Warhammer
entries.description:
Lionel wasn’t good at much in life, but he could swing a hammer and he could swing it hard. As one of the Amalgamated, born with hair of metal and skin of stone, Lionel worried that he would be as hated as the Amalgamated in Brynmoor had been, but Fellhollow proved a kinder place.

Instead of being feared and shunned, his unnatural strength became a source of much pride in his family and friends. Locals would challenge him to heft heavier and heavier things, cheering and lavishing him with praise as he did so.

Life had been good. He was happy. So, of course, it all had to end.

When the dead began to rise, arrows and blades seemed less effective than before, but crushing force still got the job done. His family and friends escaped to the Silverthorn Keep and Lionel waited at the guardhouse, standing as a wall against the tide of the undead. Countless zombies and skeletons fell to his hammer, reduced to little more than powder in a few careful swings. He could have stemmed the tide if that were all, but when the Zogre descended upon him, even Lionel’s Warhammer eventually broke against the strain.

entries.name: Stone Dagger
entries.description:
One of the first weapons ever created, the stone dagger has a sinister history. At first it allowed early humans, dwarves, elves and other intelligent species to thrive. They could take down prey and feast on the spoils, using the dagger to pare down the kill, making it easier to eat. It created the gap between animals and people, the first step toward civilization. 

It’s also the first tool to lead to murder. 

A young man whose name has long been forgotten once created a dagger of glittering black stone. Pleased with his work, he proudly displayed it, earning admiration and envy from those around him. 
So proud was he of the dagger that he would whisper to it, acting as though it would whisper back. On the day he slit the chieftain’s throat, he claimed that the dagger had told him to do it. 

Fortunately most stone daggers are pleasingly silent.

entries.name: Subjugation Staff
entries.description:
Anyone who worked with Alric knew about the Subjugation Staff. It would thud, thud, thud on the cobblestone floor as he approached. It was a welcome warning that Alric was arriving, but it came with notes of dread. 

The power of the Subjugation Staff came from what was rolled up and inserted into its middle. It was a demon pact, but one that had been defaulted on. A demon, not a human, had failed to keep their side of the bargain, and that gave the contract a radiating power. Alric captured that power within the staff. While he held it, it was as if all of demonkind owed him something.

entries.name: Sword Chieftans
entries.description:
Mouldfinger never wanted to be chief, unlike the other goblins she aspired to be just a background character – happy and forgotten while she worked on her own things. She enjoyed working with wood, bone and, on those special occasions, metal.

She crafted a sword, a simple blade that was sturdy and strong, and the other goblins went wild because of it. Seeing its sharpness, they became convinced it was magical, or imbued with the power of their draconic overlord. It wasn’t, it was just very well made.

She was made chieftain after the others challenged her, and her sharpened blade cut easily through their defenses. A fate she had never wanted, and a fate she could never escape.

entries.name: Titan's Wrath
entries.description:
Lord Rasmodel has been put to rest at last.

He rarely knew quiet. His family pushed and cajoled him to further the Rasmodel name. Then he was beset by nightmares, as two malevolent beings grappled over his mind. When the Dreaming Stone shattered, they all took him. He was their spoils. 

We can only hope that, when death came, there was quietus. He felt it for a moment as the Dreaming Stone fell, and - perhaps - he feels it on the journey over the Noumenon. 

The part of him that was a titan - that part remains. You hold it in your hands. Unleash its wrath.

entries.name: Ulv's Longbow
entries.description:
Ulv was always the silent hunter, in more ways than one. While it was true that no word ever left his lips, his footsteps, breath and, most importantly, his arrows, were all equally devoid of sound. The Wild Knights would jokingly call him the Silent Killer – though over time the crueler members of the order called him the Silent But Deadly, knowing he lacked the capability to argue back. The boy took these insults with quiet grace, never biting back, never reacting. He was used to those little cruelties, having faced them all his life. 

He had carved the bow himself and once walked Ravanna through the process. The two of them were as true a friendship as could ever be hoped for. No lingering romantic tensions. No transaction or debt. No honour chained them together. They were friends simply because they were. Because two lonely people found each other and found a comfort in each others eccentricities. The wolf and the bat, platonic soulmates to the end. 

For one of his birthdays, Ravanna enchanted the bow with a simple spell. She took animal bones, skulls and hides and wove necromantic magic through them, wrapping them around the limbs and grip of the bow, imbuing them with just enough of the underworld to strip them of their sound and a little of their substance. Like ghosts, the arrows would sail silently through the air, dropping targets before they ever knew what hit them. 

It would have been the perfect birthday gift. If only Ulv had lived long enough to receive it. 

The garou can be brutal in their assaults, considering notions like mercy to be the domain of the weak-willed, or the cowardly. Ulv was simply in the wrong place, at the wrong time, and was ambushed by a patrol of young garou, looking for the bloodmark that would grant them adulthood. There were six of them in total, but Ulv reduced them down to four, before the claws entered his throat and silenced him forever. 

When Ravanna found his body, she went mad. An anger unlike any other, a rage more powerful than any storm, waged a war inside her between the light and the dark. The darkness won. Using the souls of slain garou, Ravanna's necromantic curse tore through the Highlands, twisting the clouds into screaming things, filled with a fraction of the rage she felt. As the ghosts of the dead garou crashed about within them, the clouds unleashed lightning and thunder upon the populace below, destroying countless settlements in an instant and countless more over the centuries that followed.

entries.name: Wolfbane Dagger
entries.description: Vannaka knows this dagger only too well, for it was used against him every time he tried to prove his mettle against the other slayer masters. Although he would never willingly transform to prove his might, the unsettling sight of the dagger broke his morale enough to make him falter, and that was enough of an edge for his defeat.

entries.name: Wooden Club
entries.description: Sticks and stones may break your bones and this club is proof of the first bit. A large stuck that can be swung with impressive heft, capable of crushing bone with surprising ease. Popular by every warrior ever, when they're abandoned in the woods and need to defend themselves.

entries.name: Wooden Training Sword
entries.description:
In the village of Bramblemead, children grew up knowing battle. The God Wars hadn’t reached them yet, but the priests always knew that the danger was coming. So children were taught combat in the form of a game.

Carpenters were encouraged to make little wooden swords, so that the children could emulate the noble paladins that would wander the village. These soldiers were held up as the peak aspiration, young men and women daydreamed through school, about taking up those glittering swords and running off into adventure.

These weapons clicked and clacked against one another, harmless it seemed to the adults that watched. But wood in Bramblemead was hardened and preserved by druidic magic, and it soon became clear the damage these swords could deal. Injuries were common, bruises and broken bones were the rite of passage of every child.

It was fortunate, perhaps, that these weapons were so painful – because the children of Bramblemead grew up with a better understanding that war was no game.

entries.name: Zombie Arm
entries.description:
Let us dwell, for a moment, on the original owner of this club, a man named Mort. Mortimer Grimm had the sort of name adored by those who believe in nominative determinism. Mort Grimm, his parents effectively cursed him at birth to become an undead monstrosity, and their curse came true. 

The undead were rare in Ghornfell, but not unheard of. Some druids, who spent too long in the Whispering Swamps, apparently learned strange rituals that would raise a corpse as a mindless servant, doomed to wander the world in search of delicious, delicious brains. Mort was one of these, though he resurrected with somewhat less all-consuming-hunger than his cohorts. As the other zombies were herded towards human encampments, Mort wandered off into the poisonous Bloodblight Swamp, in search of mysteries. There he encountered a strange scientist who did not immediately attempt to set him on fire –  an improvement over the response from most people. 

This would begin a truer friendship than Mort thought possible. Whilst, yes, the scientist could never remember Mort's name and insisted on calling him Igor. And, yes, Mort would spend much of his time listening to lectures on why everyone else is stupid, whilst carrying large and disturbingly-shaped bags of unknown contents, for the scientist. Still, they would laugh and they would watch the sunsets together, and for the first time in a long time, Mort was happy. 

Until the scientist asked Mort to build the lightning conductor. One flash of inspiration later,  and Mort's tragic existence reduced itself to this somewhat sinister club. 

Still, waste not want not, I always say.

entries.name: Zombie Axe
entries.description:
Captain Artorius Flamhanger was a brave man, who stood against the rampaging forces of the damned even as his defences crumbled around him. He never wavered, never faltered, and he never left a man behind.

In a better world, there would be songs about him. But Fellhollow scorns legacy, leaving only ruin and despair where hope might take root.

He held the line against the encroaching horde far longer than anywhere else in the region. Days turned into months and months grew into years. As the rest of the region vanished into death, despair and rot, Captain Flamhanger stood strong. As his children died and rose again, the captain returned them to the earth with sombre compassion. When his wife joined them in death, he gave her a final kiss of polished silver that cleaved her head from her shoulders.

In a better world he might have held back the darkness, stood as the single ray of light in a world of shadow. But this is not our world.

There are no sagas of this man. No great texts telling of his heroic deeds. The only sound he made in the time after his death, is the bubbling song of digestive acids within a zogre’s belly.

History is penned by the survivors and the victors, yet the deeds of the dead echo across time. This axe, simple as it may appear, is infused with vengeance against the dead that had taken so much from  a good man.

entries.name: Anima-infused Tome
entries.description:
The Harmonic Resonator may be my greatest work. It is poetry forged into metal and wire, driven by a divine geometry that none of my kin have dreamed of before. Even Kerapac, the self-proclaimed genius, could not conceive of such technology.

The Roakin turned this place into a glorified wasteyard, venting their unwanted “tainted” anima back into the atmosphere so that the resonance might fade and it could return “pure”. They are fools, of course, for it is these resonances that allow anima to perform wonders. The green False User whom these mortals worship - he found a way to trap this resonant anima into stones and unleash them as magic tricks. With the Harmonic Resonator, we shall bind the magics into our very souls, allowing us to transcend the limitations of the Roakin’s curse.

Alas, our mortal shells are too frail to absorb a range of anima, so we must focus on a single attribute to embody. I have settled on the primal elements, earth, fire, water and air, rather than the more conceptual catalytic properties, as these will allow us the greatest ability to reshape Ashenfall to a glorious new Dragonkin empire.

All shall know the name of Rasthin, the first empress of the Dragonkin.

entries.name: Avisk’s Experiment Log
entries.description:
Experiment 17

I used some of the crystal on one of the insects. Took a little effort, but I stitched it into their skin as close to their nervous system as was possible.

Focusing my will upon the creature demonstrated limited results. A few controlled twitches here, a mandible click there, but nothing substantial. I  will need to consider more carefully.



Experiment 32

I embedded the crystals in the eggs this time. It occurred to me that the best way to bind the creature to the crystal was in this gestational period. The embryos grow around the shards and the energies infuse them from an early stage.

When I focus my will, I can control the movements of one of them for a limited time. I can almost see through their senses, not quite full transference, but the start of it. As they age, however, growing in size, they resist my efforts. So this is a short-lived solution at best. Still, interesting enough.



Experiment 42

The helix! This will be the answer, my means of subsuming the Kalphite consciousness beneath my will. A perfect blend of crystals, designed to resonate and redirect the mental energies of the hive, so that my will may replace them. It's like a series of mirrors, redirecting a single source of light to multiple places. Once installed, the helix shall turn my mind into the origin of all Kalphite consciousness! 

I just need the time to get it all in place. 



Experiment 59

The dragons have turned against us and I run out of time to perfect my experiments with the Kalphite hive. Yet, I believe I have a breakthrough that might lead to my apotheosis, the Dreaming Stone. With great effort, and alchemy, having stolen much of Lacrussa’s resources – well she won’t need them now she’s dead – I have created a crystal large enough to house my full consciousness. From there, I shall project my mind into the Kalphite queen and then connect her thoughts to her offspring via the crystals embedded in each of them.

It may not work, but I have little time for iteration. The dragons are at my door, and that red-scaled imbecile will soon find a way to feed me to his mother. Well, they can have the shell, but my mind, my genius, shall live forever!

entries.name: Avisk’s Musings
entries.description:
The kalphite are creatures of the desert, so they are at home here. It was trivial enough to steal a royal egg from their hive on the mainland, and bring it back here for study, and with each iteration of the brood I find myself more and more intrigued.

At first I thought they were a hive mind, the pinnacle of my research, but the more I learn, the more I realise that it’s not a singular consciousness, but a singular consensus. The queen demands and the hive obeys. They serve her because to serve her is right. The hive comes first and without the queen there is no hive.

This makes it annoyingly difficult to gather tissue samples from her, however. The soldiers, feeble as they are, gather around her like a protective wall and I must expend far more effort than is reasonable just to take a little blood, or a few of her eyes.

It’s fine, they grow back.

entries.name: Battered Diary
entries.description:
He’s dead, the black-scaled guardian. As he died it was as if the wind stilled in mourning, a great silence spread across the land dragging away all motion and noise. Leaves stopped, as if frozen in the moment. Clouds halted staring down at it all in horror. Everything was silent… except for her sorrow.

The lament of a dragon is primal, perhaps even primordial. Our lizard-brains bow their heads in mournful empathy for her suffering. It is as if a wave of misery crashes against all of us, drenching us to our bones in grief.

The writhing heads of Queen Kuldra, the Godeater, laughs from the sky. Her echoing mockery felt by every living creature in Fellhollow, as if we’re all a joke to her. A passing diversion, before she destroys us all.

She doesn’t, because that would be kind. She does not end Imaru’s pain, not yet. She leaves her with the agony of loss and the dissolution of her dreams for the future. A cruel punishment, for the simple crime of peace. She dared to shelter the lost and wandering humans, rather than put us to the flame.

Empathy, her only sin, and for that she must endure a loss so deep we may never understand it. How do you survive eternities together, ripped away in an instant?

entries.name: Bug Catcher’s Diary
entries.description:
Today is the day I catch one of them bugs. I’m gonna lure it in with some vulture meat and then I’ll trap it with my net and force it to be my friend.

We will go on grand adventures, and maybe I’ll find other bug catchers, like me, and make our kalphites fight. Mine will win of course, she’s going to be the biggest and bestest, I’ll call her Chompy.

Dad says it’s silly to like bugs. He says a good cub should like hunting and fishing and I don’t know, climbing rocks? I stop listening after a bit. He’s all old and greying and doesn’t like adventure.

My new friend, who lives in the crystal, tells me that the bugs are awesome and tells me all about a great big hive where a really big bug lives. I’m going to go and find it and its going to be my friend.

Chompy and me will be bestest friends forever!

entries.name: Captain Rainer's Journal
entries.description:
Of all the horrors of the rising dead, none are quite so chilling as the enormous undead ogres that now roam the lands. While all the vile undead seem filled with a hunger they can never sate, these beasts have a hunger greater than any other, and a terrifying capacity to consume.

Some of the scouts first saw them near the village borders, trying to break through the barricades to gain entry. Ogres are terrifying at the best of times, even the peaceful refugees who settled here, and these are scarier still.

It’s like gazing up at a wall made of muscle, that wants, more than anything, to eat you alive. There is no malice behind their eyes. No cruelty. There is just emptiness and hunger and the understanding that you might be lunch.

What scares me most about these creatures, is that their undead nature defies the theories we’d been working under. Since it was the villagers who first began to change, we assumed that it must be something to do with the strange magic their dragon patron worked upon them. Since most of us had not undergone this so-called “Blessing”, we thought we were safe from this terrifying transformation.

Yet, these… zogres… throw that theory out the window. They received no blessing, so how can that be the source?

And if they can be affected, then surely so can we?

Perhaps that would explain why I’m getting hungrier, no matter how much I eat. If that’s the case… then we’re all doomed. Fellhollow will fall.

entries.name: Chewed Doodle-Covered Journal
entries.description:
This journal is the property of Tazyn – age 9. DO NOT READ IT MUM!



I don’t know where mum is. I looked and I looked, but I couldn’t find her. I wandered only a little bit, just wanted to follow a pretty beetle I found, and now I don’t know where I am, or she is.

It’s scary out here. The wind keeps howling and there are things in the sand that wriggle and chase me. The vultures circle overheard as if waiting for me to fall.

Where’s mum? Why can’t she find me?





It got dark, then light again, and still no sign of mum. I slept under a big rock, it was cold and insects crawled all over me. I got spiders in my fur, I just know it.





I don’t know where I am. My mouth is so dry. I still can’t find mum. I’m so tired. Maybe if I sleep, all of this will go away and I’ll just wake up in my bed.





There was a voice, singing. Not like mum’s singing, this one was in tune. I followed it to a great river that wasn’t there yesterday and there was this woman just singing on a rock. She was the prettiest garou I ever saw. Eyes that sparkled like stars and silver fur like the moon. She wore this headdress that seemed to turn into water that dripped down into the river below.

She bade me drink, and it was delicious! Like fish soup and cactus juice, all rolled into one. I sat with her and she sang to me, banishing the shadows with her music. I fell asleep on her knees as she stroked my hair and promised I’d soon be home.

When I woke up, mum was fussing at me, brushing the sand from my fur. There was no river, nor silvery lady, but I was safe and found and could finally go home.

Thank you, weird singing moon lady! You’re the best.

entries.name: Child’s Storybook
entries.description:
Once there was and once there wasn’t, long long ago, a cub called Aydahn, and he was always found where trouble brewed.

The baker he tricked with salt disguised as sugar. A hunter he tricked with animal noises stolen from the shaman’s magic bag. The elder he tricked with warnings of monsters, when none were around.

One night Aydahn found a cave in the desert, lit with flickering flames.

He called out to the cave, yet no reply did he get. Twice, then thrice, did he call to the cave, and on the third time it answered.

“Are you lost, little cub?” the cave called back to the boy. “I have sweets and secrets, if you just come inside.”

“Who lives in this cave?” Aydahn replied, tempted by treats but wise enough to doubt.

“I am the sun,” said the cavern, “resting for the night. Look to the sky and see my sister ride by. When she and her foxes race through the sky, I come to this cave and enjoy treats and triumphs, won’t you share them with me?”

Aydahn was savvy, Aydahn was quick, but when else in his life could he target the sun with a trick?

He stepped into the cave, with a smile on his lips. A sparkle in his eyes and a swagger on his hips. In the cavern he found nothing, but the flickering flame; a flash of claws later and he was never the same.

His fur turned black, like the soot of a fire. His eyes turned gold like a funeral pyre. When asked by the elders what he saw in the dark, he whispered of light, of embers and sparks. A crown like corona and horns wreathed in flame, the most beautiful thing he could ever claim.

The demon of embers, reached into his heart, took hold of his future and tore it apart.

So beware, my cubs, of lights in the night, and promises and secrets that burn far too bright.

entries.name: Dragon-embossed Journal
entries.description:
I have seen what love looks like, and it spirals through the clouds. Serpentine patterns entwined together as they dance in the sun’s rays and share the sky with one another. For such large creatures, you would think them incapable of grace, yet I have never seen a dance so beautiful as the two of them together.

My grandmother speaks of their dance with a smile on her wrinkled lips. Telling stories of how the villagers danced the same, hand in hand, around the dark fires of winter. Bringing love and hope and joy in a musical war against the dark. Yet, there is a knowing sort of sadness when I ask where the dragons' children are.

Because I have never seen them.

Perhaps that’s why they are so kind to us. So gentle. Why they crush the bandits as they ransack our villages, or why they toss the dragon wolves out into the cold. Because we are their children, in a strange sort of way.

Gran says that’s what the Blessing is, that little dragon magic in our bones. An enchantment woven over each of us, as part of the dance. It makes us healthier, makes us heartier, makes us better than before.

I can’t wait to learn a dance of my own. Perhaps I can spiral through the clouds like they do, wouldn’t that be a wonderful thing?

entries.name: Dragonkin Journal
entries.description:
The Aughra creed have long been focused on escaping the curse by escaping our physical selves. They seek to project their consciousnesses into new forms, shapes and species. At first we considered the dragons, but they were still, in their own way, afflicted by the curse and so we cast our nets wider and wider seeking new forms to take.

Yet each of them is so limited in their ambitions. They seek a single form. A single mind. A single will locked into a singular vessel. While I would argue that we can be so much more.

Insects have long fascinated me. They are a collection of individual minds, small and unimpressive, true, but they work in such harmony that they act as a cohesive whole. Ants, bees and so forth, rally together creating micro-civilisations acting for a greater good. Imagine, for a moment, if you could turn that cooperative system to something bigger.

One mind, guiding a swarm. One soul as an endless wave of limbs, each pushing toward the same purpose. Why, with the right bodies, I could build a city in a day. I could put Braka’s loftiest ambitions to shame.

If I could just find the right swarm to become, I’m sure I could make even the Roakin tremble at my potential.

entries.name: Dragonscorched Ledger
entries.description:
The beast that cast us from our homes is a fickle sort, laughing as he torches our settlements and watches us flee. He’s like a child, holding a crystal to ants and watching them burn. We are the ants, and now I find myself apologising to the anthills as I pass.

It would be enough to assume the dragon is reckless and cruel, yet there is something else I have noticed as I follow him across the dunes. In moments where he thinks no one is watching, he raises his claws to the heavens and sings to the sun.

If I were a different person, one with less anger in his heart, I could see faith in his actions; hope in his heart. As if he praises the sunlight, our villages some sacrificial offering to his god in the sky.

Could it be true? It makes a twisted sort of sense. This creature, this beast of flame and fury, could be setting fire to our villages, burning down our homes, as some dread act of worship for his nameless god.

It brings to mind legends of the demon of the suns. As my grandmother told them to me, the demon would appear to people and offer them everything they had ever wanted, only to change them into mindless creatures of worship. 

How does one look into a fire and see only the light, not the flame, or the ashes.

entries.name: Dusty Tome
entries.description:
I was visited once, by a strange creature who spoke as if witnessing a time that wasn’t now. I was lying in my bed, when they appeared out of the dunes and told me this tale as if I were someone else.

They referred to me as an adventurer, but I have never left my home. Still, it was a strange enough event that I felt I should record it.

It was on the subject of the lava-creatures that we see shambling around under Fuzan’s direction – the KotHaar. These creatures, they claimed, were here long before the dragon. Long before anyone set foot on Ashenfall, perhaps even Gielinor itself. When the ancient ones - the elder gods, as they called them – settled on this world, they brought with them servitors who watched over the secrets of this place, and the treasures within it.

They had no name at the time, and no need for one, for each was defined by their purpose. A taskworker with a soul.

My narrator explained that they were guarding some sort of device, a powerful tool that kept the sun shining and brightness that let the world thrive, rather than burn. A device, they claimed, has now been perverted by the dragon into some monstrous device that is destroying the region.

Adventurer, if you read this, as I suspect my narrator predicts, please find a way to relinquish the dragon’s hold on this device, this Lens, so that the world may not come to fear the light of day.

Long before anyone set foot on Ashenfall, perhaps even Gielinor itself. When the ancient ones - the elder gods, as they called them – settled on this world, they brought with them servitors who watched over the secrets of this place, and the treasures within it.

They had no name at the time, and no need for one, for each was defined by their purpose. A taskworker with a soul.

My narrator explained that they were guarding some sort of device, a powerful tool that kept the sun shining and brightness that let the world thrive, rather than burn. A device, they claimed, has now been perverted by the dragon into some monstrous device that is destroying the region.

Adventurer, if you read this, as I suspect my narrator predicts, please find a way to relinquish the dragon’s hold on this device, this Lens, so that the world may not come to fear the light of day.

entries.name: Entomologist’s Journal
entries.description:
The bugs fascinate me, even if my husband thinks I’m bonkers. He says “Niamh, I love you, but you can’t pin one of those things to the wall and call it art. At least wash it first, it stinks.”

Well! I mean, you absolutely can, though it takes quite a while and you need a particularly sturdy nail, but it CAN be done!

Anyway, where was I? So, I followed the bugs to their hive and, wow, just… just wow! They may be dumb, brainless crawly things, but they can make some wonderful structures. There’s an artistry to them that’s all the more impressive considering they have the aesthetic sensibilities of… well… insects.

Perhaps its their nature? They are so colourful after all. Their shells are so sparkly, and their wings reflect myriad colours in the noonday sun. Creatures as beautiful as these must be born with artist souls, surely?

I found some old notes in that horrible pyramid thing. Some madman talking about crystals and helixes and other such nonsense, but what I did find was that these bugs aren't from around here. They were stolen from another bug hive, really far away. On another continent, perhaps the one my people fled from thousands of years ago. I wonder if the bugs there are as fascinating as these, or did the journey change them somehow? Would two hives look identical to one another? Are their queens connected somehow? Can they talk to each other across continental differences? Would they get on with one another? Would they go to war? 

So many questions!

I need better notes. 

I think I’ll try and get a bit closer. I wonder what the hives look like on the inside? I’m sure they’ll welcome me in.

entries.name: Everburning Book
entries.description:
Our city is lost to embers, great monuments crumbling beneath the scorching heat of the sun and the claws of the dragon. We were peaceful, we were no threat to him, yet he brought such a fury down upon us that we could not stand against him.

Our archers fired so many arrows that it blotted out the sun. Our mages hurled spells that shook the very foundations of the earth, and our warriors readied their blades so sharp that they could cleave a mountain in two.

All for nought.

As he razed our cities, and shattered the monuments that recorded our past, he sang. Sang a song to the heavens, a great hymn to the sky. A song that burned in our hearts, igniting our souls like we were kindling on the fire just waiting for a spark.

We ran. What else could we do?

How do you fight a foe that threatens to set your spirit aflame?

We wander now, disparate tribes, keeping far enough away from each other, in the hope that he cannot chase us all. Families separated. A culture buried in the sands.

I only hope that we can find ourselves again, free from Fuzan’s flames.

entries.name: Experiment Log
entries.description:
Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 7

It is not easy splicing reptile and mammal together, their very nature fights against their biology and they would rather perish upon emergence than live with such a hybrid nature. It’s a shame really, the little pups are quite cute. I think Viika would like one as a pet, it might keep my sibling grounded and anchored a little more to our frame of reference. Wishful thinking perhaps.

The wolves have proved remarkably durable, considering. While they all die seconds after birth, they do hold on longer than expected. I attempted to combine kebbit and dragon and… well… that didn’t go well. Chinchompa and dragon, that was a mistake that will take some time to repair – I liked that lab.  Yet wolf, there’s something here, I can feel it. They’re resilient, dangerous and there’s something in the pack mentality that fascinates me.

Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 56

I have decided that a rapid hybridisation approach will not work. Mammals, while fast breeders, are weak and lack the resilience needed to survive the experiment if I go too quickly. Instead I shall engineer a slow breeding process, spreading the development out over the generations.

Tedious, yes, but at least it will allow me to focus on other project while this progresses.

Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 219

The changes are gradual, yet viable. Scales here and there, some improved musculature and reflexes, yet nothing approaching the power of a dragon.

Is this all they can be?

Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 2307

I’d forgotten about this failure of an experiment. The dragon-wolves have proved inadequate for any useful purpose. I was going to incinerate the remaining members, but Viika in a fit of strangeness released them all.

So, now we have it. Dragon-wolves running all over the region, lovely. Honestly my sibling can be so vexing sometimes.

entries.name: Farmer Fred's Journal
entries.description:
I had always wanted neighbours, out here in the sticks, but these weren’t exactly what I imagined. Refugees, so they claim, from the Bandosian forces, escaped the violence of their people in hope of peace.

Followers of the war god, looking to settle down. I didn’t believe it, until they turned in their weapons. There was this great pile of them outside the village, built up into a pyre and then set to the flame.

We danced as they burned, it was beautiful. I drank with a few of them and… well… I don’t remember much of the evening anymore. Just hazy moments of laughter and stories, nothing more than that.

Now I bring Golbor and Klom baskets of pumpkins and in exchange they help me plough the fields before we can sow the soil anew. Good people. Full of laughter and big emotions so large they create a gravity that draws all of us in.

These weren’t the neighbours I imagined, but I couldn’t ask for better.

entries.name: Flame-licked Journal
entries.description:
It is strange, to be one with an element - to feel it coursing through your veins, your cells, your very thoughts. Fire illuminates and strips bare. It cleanses and it scours, and it reveals parts of the universe I had never dared to gaze on before.

There are gaps, cracks if you will, in the skein of the universe and, through those gaps, wonders gaze back at us. Or horrors, perhaps, if you’re more prone to fear than joy. I have seen the crawling pests of the Void skittering at the edge of reality. The Aughra’s other shells gaze back at us from the Abyss, and - further, beyond that - are beasts so colossal that thinking on them gives me a headache.

Yet, of all the worlds I gaze at in wonder, this one is still the brightest of all. Gielinor, by the monkey’s tongue, is a perfect world. Not just by the measure of its creators, but in its possibilities. It is ripe with magic, filled with potential and the spark within me burns with inspiration at what it could become.

I need but the right tools to turn it toward greatness. I need an army strong enough to keep the rabble in check. Lacrussa can create them. It was easy enough to inspire her to do so, the spark of creativity is so very easy to ignite.

In Avisk I did the same with his obsession with the mind, for if I am to have an army of unstoppable beasts, I must be able to control them.

The world can be reshaped into something wonderful. A glorious regime, burning bright as a star.

Rasthin, Empress of Gielinor. Yes, I very much like the sound of that.

entries.name: Gold-plated Tome
entries.description:
She came to us in our time of need and taught us the ways of the sand. A lost people, guided by her light into a new promised land for the garou. Not the forests of our homeworld, nor the roots of Ghornfell, but a world of dunes and  glittering nights, beneath the blazing sun.

She plucked a star from the sky and planted it in the sand, and where the silver light shone there sprouted crystal clear water that reflected the heavens above. She bade us drink from the waters and we were renewed, our past sins erased so that we could start afresh.

Stone, she taught us to twist and shape so that we could build houses, temples and monuments that would survive the sands long after we fell. Far sturdier than the wood and weave that we had relied on before. We tilled the dunes, finding the places where life could flourish and we planted seeds and crops at her directing, and from this desolate wasteland came life.

She was the moon and the river and the chance to start again. A mother to the garou when we needed guidance most.

To guide our way, she gave us the mirrors and the shards at the heart of them.  Silvered shards of moonlight, in physical form. They would act as beacons in the desert night, pointing the way to each of the settlements. A guiding light to banish the evils in our path.

Praise be to the moon.
Praise be El…

[The page has been damaged beyond repairing, obscuring the name]

entries.name: Hate-filled Tome
entries.description:
She is here: the pinnacle of dragon creation, the queen, fused with divine blood and now housing the elemental power of my kin. Kuldra stands at my gate and with each passing second she weakens the defences. She will kill me, I know this, but I will not go down without a fight.

The Resonator is charged, primed with the perfect discordance. If I had more time, I could build a shockwave strong enough to rip the entire continent apart, but I will settle on taking Kuldra with me.

Viika visited me earlier. How they are alive I do not know; they arrived to give me their standard cryptic prophecy and then left, just like always.

“She will turn the Veil against the world,” they said, as if that means anything.

If I had more time, I might try to care, but now… now I see no way out, except to end things on my terms. I shall ready a cataclysm that will fracture Ashenfall and take Kuldra and her brood with me.

With any luck, the backwash of the explosion will poison the anima of this planet, killing the Roakin and their eggs. Unlikely, true, but one can dream.

Curse you, Kuldra! You could have been the herald of a glorious new age for Gielinor, yet you fall to mindless vengeance like the beast you are!

I will spit my last breath upon you, wishing that it will be your last breath as well.

entries.name: Laboratory Note
entries.description:
I wonder, sometimes, whether we are too limited in our focus. Is the cold-blooded nature of the reptile, more useful than the mammalian warm-blood approach? I watch the creatures of this region, the kebbits, the cows, the sheep and I see how they multiply and spread at a pace that far exceeds our own.

By contrast, the dragons I birth are a slow and laborious effort. Each one must be carefully managed and maintained with focused precision. Even those capable of spawning their own young, do so slowly. Often brooding no more than a single viable progeny in a century of practice.

Even my prize specimen produced only a single heir, a red-scaled whelp, no less, unlike his mother’s multicoloured hues. Perhaps the fault lies in the father. I should dissect him and see where the problem begins.

But I lose my train of thought. Mammals. Noisy, smelly, but they are everywhere, breeding like rats – which are also mammals, now I think about it. Perhaps I should turn my sights on them instead.

There are a pack of dire wolves that wander near my laboratory, it would be simple enough to procure a few of their number. Some adults, a few children, I’ll need a large and diverse sample size for my experiments.

Perhaps there’s a place where reptile and mammal can meet, to create a superior creature. I shall investigate further.
