entries.name: Lacrussa's Diary
entries.description:
Avisk is a snake! I am not surprised by this discovery, he’s never been subtle about his ambition, but that he would dare to attempt an experiment on Viika, well that’s unforgivable.

He attached tubes, crystals and all sorts of nonsense to my sibling’s head and attempted something with rune essence that caused a lot of explosions. Viika was hurt, burned across their temple and one of their wings is damaged enough that they might never fly again.

I have never felt anger like I did in that moment. Even the rage from the curse never struck me as hard. In that instant I dragged blades of ice from the aether, and I would have torn Avisk to pieces of only my sibling hadn’t said “no”. Always too gentle Viika, not like the rest of us.

Maybe that’s why they never partook Rasthin’s discovery. Because they knew what monsters we’d become.

Avisk won’t get away without consequences. My sibling may be gentle, but I am not. I flow like the river and wield the patience of glaciers, and Avisk will learn that water always wins.

entries.name: Lacrussa's Journal
entries.description:
Viika is silent today and I don’t know if that’s a good sign. How do you relate to your sibling when they’re seeing a different “now” to you? Are they staring back at the door to our home as our parents wave them goodbye forever? Or are they enjoying tomorrow’s dinner today instead?

I wish they could tell me. Share how they feel. The scientist in me would give anything to know the mind of the timeswept. The sister in me would give anything to understand my sibling.

Dragonkin don’t normally do family. We’re all so focused on our own problems, our constant pain, that we sometimes lack the empathy to care for someone else. Romance died the day of the curse, I swear, and family became a necessary act of survival, rather than a nurturing thing.

Yet I choose to defy traditional values. Viika deserves better, after all. So if they do not know what day is today, I will keep them grounded. I will be the shield against the horrors of the present, so that they will see the tomorrow they’ve already lived.

And perhaps, if I’m lucky, they will find that special moment when their now and my now coincide together.

entries.name: Lacrussa's Memoir
entries.description:
Avisk keeps trying to sneak into my laboratory, convinced that the secrets within will grant him the knowledge to transcend his mortal frame. I’ve told him time and time again that it will do no such thing, but he’s convinced I conceal my discoveries, hoarding knowledge and sharing it with none.

Have my advances not brought this little group to the heights of success? It was my work that allowed Rasthin to complete her device. My work that created armies of dragons to serve at our beck and call. Yet, despite all this, he’s convinced that I keep the really good stuff to myself.

The irritating part is, of course, that he is correct.

So, I seal it away behind locked doors shielded from even dragonkin magic. A mechanism that will stand for eternity, barring him access.

The best part is that I based the lock not on a key, which he could steal, nor on a phrase, which he could overhear, but upon a riddle posed to me by the priest Kranon, all those years ago.

“What does the charitable priest offer, the illuminated sage seek, and the ignorant forsake? Walk their paths and what do you discover?”

He will go mad knowing the answer, for it is obvious, yet it is the steps one must walk to get there that will unbar his path. I bet he’ll even think the damaged statue is accidental wear and tear.

It will drive him mad. Just thinking about his frustration makes me giddy with delight.

entries.name: Lacrussa's Notes
entries.description:
Dragons are a useful tool, but little more than that. They are powerful, yes, strong and dangerous, excellent beasts of burden or disposable troops in a fight. Yet, they lack the grace, poise and power needed to be new dragonkin hosts. I always knew that was a failed plan.

Still, what experiment cannot be perfected? What hypothesis cannot be refined? There is something in dragons, some key to our apotheosis, that I feel driven to explore further still.

And Rasthin has the blood that may be the key.

“Gods”, they call them, what a nonsense affair. Leave that to the waning priest caste, like that mewling fool Kranon, and the primitive spirits these lesser beings follow. They are powerful creatures, formed of a changed and ascended essence, as if flesh and soul merged into a single construct and solidified into form.

One of them bleeds. Perhaps all of them, but this one for certain. She calls herself a goddess of the moon and the primordial hunt. Nonsense, of course, moons are rocks floating in the emptiness and there’s nothing spiritual or metaphysical about a predator seeking lunch.

Still, if I can refine this power? If I can merge it with a dragon, perhaps… just perhaps… I can turn these worthless dragons into something we can use.

“Gods”, they call them, what a nonsense affair. Leave that to the waning priest caste, like that mewling fool Kranon, and the primitive spirits these lesser beings follow. They are powerful creatures, formed of a changed and ascended essence, as if flesh and soul merged into a single construct and solidified into form.

One of them bleeds. Perhaps all of them, but this one for certain. She calls herself a goddess of the moon and the primordial hunt. Nonsense, of course, moons are rocks floating in the emptiness and there’s nothing spiritual or metaphysical about a predator seeking lunch.

Still, if I can refine this power? If I can merge it with a dragon, perhaps… just perhaps… I can turn these worthless dragons into something we can use.

entries.name: Lacrussa's Ravings
entries.description:
Avisk is like the scales behind my wings, irritating and in desperate needs of a good scratch. He keeps coming to me and trying to explain to me how I need to do X with the dragons, or Y with their eggs, as if he, an Aughra, has the slightest understanding of real science. Imbecile.

His obsession with crystals is growing increasingly tiresome. 

He’s already messed with some of the brood, tried to use that strange rune essence in ways that would cause energy to flow in certain ways. I can see the concept he’s going for, but his clumsy nonsense just leads it to ruin. Trying to create some sort of enhanced mind for the dragons, as if they could exist like a swarm. 

All of them, of course, died. All but one, and she’s turned out strangely.

I encourage the growth of a single head for the dragons, keeps them sane and stable. There’s no good that can come from multiple brains in charge of one body, yet she proves me wrong. All the minds work as if connected, as if part of the same whole. A single consciousness spread across all of them. A single personality.

Because that’s what it is, a personality. A will. A mind of her own. She is enraged, yes, like all dragons are, but she spreads it across herself, weakening the effect. I have encountered curiosity, reason, even wit. A most curious creature, I look forward to studying her more.

entries.name: Lacrussa's Writings
entries.description:
There is a crack in the heart of the world and it whispers. Smoke rises from it unlike any I’ve encountered before. There is no magma vent. No burning coal line underground. There is just emptiness softly smoking, chill as the grave.

Smoke should be warm, yet this is colder than ice. A sort of strange frost that seeps into your bones. Though it strangles the air in my lungs as I stare into this fissure, I see only darkness and shadow, all the way down.

There is a power in it, unlike any I’ve seen before and I must harness it.

It started with the claw-bones of one of the failed dragon whelps. Exposed to the smoke it twitched and writhed, as if there were still muscles and sinew contracting in motion, not polished bone with no nerves attached.

There is a song in the whispering smoke. Discordant and strange. Words I don’t understand, I’m not even sure it’s language. Still, I feel a connection there, like a promise, offering me more. I am not fool enough to listen, the angler fish lure of power is all too familiar to my kind, but still perhaps I can make use of this.

After all, one must risk everything in the pursuit of knowledge!

entries.name: Lavish Dragonkin Tome
entries.description:
We are not normally creatures of ceremony, we Dragonkin, yet I feel the need for it in our great endeavour. Perhaps the old priests, like that fool Kranon, have a point, for what better way to acknowledge something’s importance, than to dress it up in ritual?

Candles. Music. Well-tailored robes: these are the tools that I craft for my companions and myself, so that we may give this moment the reverence it requires. Even Avisk, with his constant sarcasm and flippancy, succumbs to the gravity of the moment.

We will not be gods.

We will not be False Users, claiming the power of the Roakin’s artifacts.

We will be something else, something more. We will be the earth, the wind, the blaze of the sun and the crashing waves of the ocean. We will be primordial forces incarnate.

There is music, a song from the old world, before it was lost in the Great Revision. It speaks of the passage of time, the solemnity of the stars and the eternity of creation. Nonsense, and proved terribly wrong, yet… fitting, all the same.

I wrote it. It is some of my best work.

The Harmonic Resonator builds into a great orchestra of anima. Dazzling threads of colour dance and writhe according to my grand design. I watch them spiral overhead, swirling in a scintillating circle and I smile at my last moment of mundane mortality, as fire and I become one.

entries.name: Lazilly-penned Diary
entries.description:
You’d think they’d be cruel landlords, given that they’re dragons and all. After them beast people turned on our Southern neighbours and wiped them all out, you’d expect these dragons to do the same. They was working together after all.

But, no, that’s not how it goes. Or at least not how it’s going. The two of them kept their distance at first, pretending we weren’t here. We watched as the flight of dragons swept over us and ignored us altogether, fearing the side eyes from our two new friends.

Then, when it were all over and done with, here they were. Talking to us, as though we were neighbours. Speaking to us as though we were friends.

She were… kind. There’s no other word for it. Great big blue thing made of teeth and claws, and she were singing to the children who couldn’t sleep at night. He and her, helped us build this city. Helped us find the best places to fetch water, or plant crops.

Her magic brought rain and his calmed the winds, so that our harvests were plentiful, and our population bloomed. All it costs is a few sheep or cows, every once in a while, a pretty good deal if you ask me.

No gods watching over us here. No priests, nor nobles. We got dragons watching out for us, aint that a nice thing?

entries.name: Madrafola's Scraps
entries.description:
It's brimstone! That's the smell. It was tickling the edge of my brain, but now I've got it. Brimstone!

Marthanóir expelled Dìoghail from the scouting party, but it hasn't made a lick of difference. Dìoghail is still with us, quiet as a boulder, grabbing yew branches from our fire and forming his own little satellite camp. Bless him, the old cat is broken.

The smell is getting stronger. My guess is that we'll find the smell's maker tomorrow. Perhaps I'll apply some gypsum warpaint to my face, just like Dìoghail! If you're going to go mad, then why not go mad with company?

entries.name: Marthanóir's Scraps
entries.description:
It's as feared. There's no shortage of clues and tracks, even in the sandstorm. They're the ones you worry about: the foes who don't give a hoot about tracks.

Blood and bone leads us east. Madrafola says that she can smell something on the wind. Dìoghail says nothing and just leads us at a pace that we struggle to follow.

I haven't got a clue why Hedric sent us out with Dìoghail. No garou should be included on a scouting party for their own daughter.

entries.name: Mould-covered Journal
entries.description:
I fled, like the coward I am, back toward Bramblemead, back to the hatred. Yet, the way is closed. A great wall bars my path. I am a prisoner here among the damned.

We all tried so hard to stem the tide. The Wild Knights to the east pushed back against the horde as much as they could. They walled themselves away in their keep  until no one remains alive to guard it.

Emberwood sealed itself away behind a barrier, priests working together in unified cause. Faith locks everyone out, and everyone in.

As for the tower, and those who dwelled beside it, it’s shattered. The dragons’ disciples lost in a great lake of sorrow and grief. Damned by their own devotion.

And here I am, clawing at a wall, mere metres of stone between safety and despair. Despair always wins.

Perhaps it is like those doors? I see them sometimes, out of the corner of my eye. Strange and ephemeral, inviting me in. Yet, if I focus on them, I see nothing. Only when I feel myself slipping away do they show themselves again. Perhaps a wall is not always a wall, like a door is not always there?

It doesn’t matter. I am lost. Fellhollow is lost.

It’s all her fault.

entries.name: Priestly Journal
entries.description:
Scripture says that all gods other than Saradomin are false, and their cultists are not to be trusted. Yet, I don’t see it that way today. As the village has fallen to the shambling nightmare that is the withering, the other priests and I have worked together to save who we can.

There are dead buried deep below the soil and their bones carry the power of prayer in them, like all do. So we priests prayed together, a union of faith, to erect a barrier of belief to keep the withered villagers contained.

Our prayers bound to the icons, and only together will the village be re-opened once more.

A tragic loss, truly. Emberwood could have been the great human utopia. Faiths working side by side. Amalgamated and not – villagers who do not let their differences define them. Two great dragons, to watch over us and keep us safe. It could have been perfect.

But belief needs adversity, or it becomes complacency. This will be a trial for each of us that we must strive to overcome.

entries.name: Rasthin’s Journal
entries.description:
I did not believe it possible, but Lacrussa’s genius continues to impress me. She has, to her great credit, managed to create a queen dragon of our own, a progenitor for our future army. The creature is chimeric in capability, with multiple heads, each able to absorb different aspects so that she might more easily create the required brood.

Lacrussa’s sibling, Viika, seems both enamoured and terrified of the creature in equal measure, but I have long since given up trying to work out the meaning of their strange mood shifts.

The queen has grown much over the last few centuries and has even taken a favoured broodmate - the two of them producing plentiful offspring for both experimentation and labour. While many are flawed, less than they could be, there are least three of note that promise a more powerful army once we iron out the kinks. I shall suggest the broodmate be dissected for study, I’m sure the weakness lies with him.

The timing is most convenient, as there is growing unrest among the talking mammals that wander these lands. One faction stands on the brink of extermination, and they have a deity fighting with them.

I wonder what I could do with a deity to study. Whilst they are false divinities, their powers are undeniable. I shall see if I can inspire them to our service, so that we might test our dragon army against her foes.

Oh, this shall be fun.

entries.name: Ravanna's Fifth Journal
entries.description:
Things are so much worse than I thought. The River Noumenon, the way to the Afterlife, is blocked. Imaru has somehow wedged herself in there, using the curse I gave her and her own, sheer, bloody-minded rage to stick her in place.

She claws at the edge of the Underworld, creating rifts that bleed the Noumenon’s waters into our world like some deadly poison that rips out the soul. She uses her “Blessing” as an anchor to her people, dragging their souls to her so that she might feast and grow stronger.

So focused on strength and power, on beating Kuldra, that she doesn’t think about what happens to everyone else. My soul is protected, warded by the curse that rages inside me, but the other villagers aren’t so lucky.

I see tendrils of their spirits being dragged from their chests like a ragged cloak billowing in the wind. They don’t see it, of course, but they can feel it. They know something is going on and it’s leading to blind panic. The once peaceful chatter of Fellhollow is now turning to stifled screams.

This is all my fault. I need to try and find a way to fix it.

entries.name: Ravanna's First Journal
entries.description:
The odd thing about life is it’s surprisingly easy to maintain. For all the work of alchemists and scheming sorcerers, continued existence is child’s play really. All it takes is hate.

Hate is a fuel that can burn forever. Pure rage is a force that can drive anyone forward. Grief is a power source that can last until the end of time. You just need to know how to use them.

There’s a morality in vengeance that society shuns. They say it won’t solve anything. That it never makes things better. Yet, I picture the suffering of those monsters and that’s all I need. Knowing they suffer, die and weep for their loved ones, that’s enough to drive my bones forward and keep the skin stitched in place.

Unreasonable, yes, but at least hate is honest in it’s hypocrisy. I choose to turn the wheel of the vicious cycle round and round, grinding garou bones beneath it.

I will never forgive them for the death of my friend. Never. And as long as I curse them, my soul will not fade to the world below.

Someone will tell me that that’s not what Ulv would want, but I knew my friend and, if he could speak, he’d tell me to make sure they hurt.

So, I do.

Those same people tell me that grief fades, but that’s a lie. It’s been so long now, so many years, yet that pain and that hate still burn inside me more ferociously than the sun, and I wake each day smiling because I know they suffer in return.

Perhaps I need a hobby?

entries.name: Ravanna's Fourth Journal
entries.description:
I am guilty of mistakes, I admit this. I let things get to me and I don’t think them through as well as I should. When I lost Ulv I tried to bring him back and… well… the result of that is better buried, I confess.

I visit him from time to time. There’s nothing left of my friend there, hasn’t been for some time, but I don’t want him getting lonely.

She was my next mistake. Imaru. After the death of her mate she came to me seeking a way to bring him back. Necromancy doesn’t work like that, at least not yet and certainly not within my skill set. Yet, still, I thought I could offer her something almost as good.

I offered her revenge.

I created a curse within her, using her grief and rage as a focus, so that it might strengthen her against Kuldra. She was to become a devouring force that would feast on the Godeater’s very soul.

It did not work.

Kuldra is stronger than I imagined. Her essence more powerful than either of us could have guessed. As Imaru raged at her Kuldra simply laughed and rebuffed her, barely even registering the unholy force hurled against her. She is a monster, and I use that word very rarely.

So Imaru died. Fell to the ground in a crumbled heap… and I wish that were the end of it.

entries.name: Ravanna's Second Journal
entries.description:
So this is what the people who left Bramblemead are up to. Honestly, it seems like a pretty nice life. There’s amalgamated and, for lack of a better word, normal people working side by side. Shops are well-stocked, and fields are filled with delicious looking vegetables. The entire landscape is a dazzling display of vibrant colours and … oh, yeah, they have dragons.

Not dragons like we had – the ones that burn villages to the ground and stomp on people for fun. No, these dragons watch over the villagers, help them with construction, farming, all sorts of stuff. They even give them this weird little thing they call a Blessing, which somehow binds them together in a way I’m seriously going to need to study later.

The people don’t worship the dragons either. There’s nothing like the goblin shenanigans down south. No, the traditional religions line up in a multifaith community with one another. Saradominists greet Zamorakians and no one starts a fight. I assume, anyway, no one really wears little badges or anything, but there are shrines to more than just Saradomin here, so I like to daydream.

I set up a little shop. Can you imagine? Me, with a shop! Just selling little potions and salves, and services for those that need to speak with the dead. Simple stuff, nothing too taxing, but enough to put a roof over my head.

I think I could be happy here. Well, as happy as I get.

entries.name: Ravanna's Seventh Journal
entries.description:
The seals are in place, but I’m not sure what good they’ll do. A desperate attempt to try and mitigate some of the damage I’ve caused by binding Imaru to that curse. I have taken the essence of her curse and bound it to the plinths, in hope that someone stronger than me might yet claim them.

Doing so will bind them to her curse in the same way that she is, but only for a while. Strong enough to challenge her. Strong enough to harm her. Without the curse she’s invulnerable, but the very same thing that makes her powerful, makes her weak.

I have split them across the region, so that someone will not stumble on them by mistake. It will require dedication, focus and skill to overcome this monster of my own making, I’m sorry I cannot be the one to do it.

But, at least, I can help the one who can.

entries.name: Ravanna's Sixth Journal
entries.description:
Fellhollow is doomed, there’s no other word for it. Imaru’s wedged herself in this part of the underworld and her mouth is wide and consuming all the souls that flow down the river Noumenon. With each soul she devours she grows stronger and her grip tightens. Her hunger grows, she craves more and more, and she’ll never stop.

The necromantic energies of the Underworld then wash back through the Blessing and into her subjects, animating their bodies and filling them with an unquenchable thirst for more souls. They’re nothing but withered husks of themselves, all humanity drained away and all that’s left is a terrible, clawing, need.

I’ve seen this before, in the forbidden texts that my master kept hidden from me. Only the source of this evil isn’t some nebulous power that dwells in the shadows, but an undead dragon. An evil of my own making.

So, one I must undo. I cannot break the curse. I cannot end her wrath. For all my skills I am nowhere near a match for her in battle.  All I can do is protect the rest of Ashenfall, and Gielinor, by keeping her locked away.

It’ll take some work, but the one thing I have in abundance is time.

entries.name: Ravanna's Third Journal
entries.description:
I have a new customer, and she won’t fit through the door.

Odd to empathise with a dragon, but I do. We all saw what happened. I watched as the great multi-headed dragon queen pulled Xikotal’s heart from his chest and ate it in front of his mate.

You don’t just get over something like that. It’s visceral and cuts you deeper than you ever thought possible. It’s not just grief. It’s not just rage. The two forces combine into something new, something stronger than the sum of its components. That sort of feeling is powerful – strong enough to change you into something other than what you were.

I have lived for longer than I can say on that feeling alone. It’s a fuel that rages within you, burning you from the inside to keep you warm. I can only imagine what it’s doing to a creature like her.

She asks me to bring her beloved back, but that’s beyond my power, always has been. I’ve never been great at animating the dead, I can do a few bones, sure, but nothing stronger.

Curses, though, that I’m good with those.

Imaru’s rage makes her the perfect focus. The beating heart around the darkest magics. She can be a weapon against the Godeater, if I hone her right. The rage of a dragon, combined with the power of a grief-curse, such a thing could be the blade needed to slit Kuldra’s throat.

I will forge her carefully.

entries.name: Red-stained Diary
entries.description:
There are strange visitors to these lands, people I never expected. Unsettling, pale elves who arrive in the night and stay for an evening asking us very unusual questions. I don’t even know why we let them in. It was as if they belonged here… as if they had a right to be here.

We spoke of travel and family, of loss and of love. They asked me about the scar on my lip and the way I hold my sword at an angle. I told them about my first crush, even though I’d never shared his name with anyone.

Then there was the talk of loss. Loss, like it was happening right then. A bottle spinning, fingers pointing, a choice we never chose to make. We lost someone that night, didn’t we? I don’t remember who, but there’s a hole there where a person should be. A shadow over my memories.

A locked room, where no one has the key.

I remember laughter, dancing and eyes like perfect rubies sparkling in the dazzling night. I remember his lips on mine, cold and tasting of metal, and then… nothing.

Their names. I don’t remember those elven names. You’d think you’d remember something like that. It’s not like we see many elves, not since that bard passed through a while ago. I feel like I should know them.

But, like all those empty rooms, somehow, I forget.

entries.name: Rot-covered Journal
entries.description:
I am lost in these treacherous ruins, with all hope of the outside world lost to me. I sought to escape the horror of Fellhollow, but this place is worse. Rotting from within. 

Yet, as I wither… as these bonds of flesh are broken, another world reveals itself. 

Walkways, doorways, entire new paths to travel. This prison is filled with ways to run that were not there before. 

Still, as I explore them, I feel her gaze upon me. I feel her hunger grow. Imaru is watching, and there is no escape. 

Saradomin have mercy, because Imaru most certainly will not.

entries.name: Sand-scoured Diary
entries.description:
I found one of the rock people lying in the sand. He, if I should give them a gender, was only faintly glowing, as if the magma within him were cooling, turning into rock.

Should I have left him there? Perhaps. Certainly father would tell me so. They are the reason so many of my kinfolk are dead; their raids, against our caravans, are the reason so many starve in the fallow seasons. Yet, I found I could not just leave him alone in those last moments. No one should die in silence, without at least a chance to confess their fears.

His eyes - strange and shimmering, like they were carved from rock and placed upon his features – were somehow full of feeling, as if he were flesh and blood. He was afraid. Sad. Lost. I felt sorry for the creature, how strange is that?

The magma cooled around him, seeping out in some places as if he were wounded and bleeding out into the dunes. His limbs lay cold and useless by his sides, his entire existence locked in place at his torso as the cold spread slowly up his body, snuffing out his light.

A sound scratched from within him. The sound of it was like rocks scraping together. A hollow, cold thing, carrying with it a single word that I thought they didn’t even know.

“Sorry,” he said, as the last embers went dark.

I buried him in the sands, and left a marker for his kin to find. If they even look for their fallen. I’m not even sure they bury their dead.

entries.name: Sand-weathered Book
entries.description:
Grandmother died today. She walked out into the desert, into the scorching sun and let the sands take her.

She was always smiling, was grandmother, always had a story to tell. She loved us dearly, even with her last breath. It’s a lesser mentioned part of the bargain with the dragon, this sacrifice at the end of our days. To burn in the sunlight. To vanish into the storm. We sacrifice our last moments, so that our loved ones get to enjoy far more of theirs. The Mark, this symbol of Fuzan's that we carry as protection against his wrath, it compels us to the wilderness. Makes us an offering to the storm. 

In doing so the rest of us are spared and benefit from Fuzan's mercy. He turns his flames away from us. Protects us against some of the dangers of the desert, in exchange for the Mark. Grandmother's last thoughts would have been of the rest of us. As was always her way. 

It still hurts, though, this grief. She could have had years, at least, her fur had barely greyed in her age. The village feels so silent now, without her cackling laughter.

But we live on. Her sacrifice guarantees that.

Perhaps, one day, I will walk out into those sands. I wonder if I will be as brave as grandmother was?

entries.name: Sand-worn Leather Tome
entries.description:
We had honour once, long, long ago. On a world of emerald leaves, we hunted our prey without blade nor bow, and took only what we needed. This Lougrim taught us, may her memory never fade.

The abomination slew Lougrim, not for honour, not for the hunt, but for the love of power. She enslaved our people, turned us into footsoldiers for wars we should never have been a part of. Took our young and trained them to be killers, murderers, not the hunters we should be. Honour stripped out in favour of bloodlust, and too many of our kin agreed.

So, what could we do but leave?

We passed through forests, mountains and lost many along the way. Those of us who chose to follow the guidance of the moon, rather than the dragon queen’s willow-wisp firelight. We shall preserve the honour of our people, well, what little is left.

I am old now, the ache in my bones tells me that my time comes to an end. This great desert before me shall be my tomb, yet, I will die free. I will die as a true garou, a hunter, not a killer. When my body rests beneath the sands, let it begin a healing cycle for my people. Let this land flourish, and my people with it.

Let us be the children of the moon again.

entries.name: Scorched Tome
entries.description:
I have underestimated the queen we created. I thought her a mindless, cowardly beast, yet she is a cunning and vengeful creature. She waited. That’s the most terrifying thing. She waited! When we were distracted. When we were not expecting it. She waited and then she turned her brood against us and forced us into hiding.

She ate Brakka first. I won’t mourn him. He was an arrogant narcissist with little to offer beyond his masonry. Avisk has vanished into the aether, which isn’t a concern, but Lacrussa’s silence worries me. Of all my fellow Dragonkin, she is the only one worth my respect. It would be a genuine tragedy if the world lost her genius.

The garou goddess, this Lougrim, chooses to fight beside her people, believing she can stand against a queen dragon with divine blood in her veins - Lougrim’s blood! She will learn how well we make our dragons.

I will seal myself away here, within the heart of the Harmonic Resonator. I alone know the full capabilities of this device and I know how to weaponise it. If Kuldra is to kill me, then I shall take her and half of Ashenfall with me!

entries.name: Soot-stained Journal
entries.description:
I found an egg today, buried in the earth. Looks like it fell out of one of them there ruins, you know, the ones under the ground with the glowy blue flames? Well there was this egg that was just sticking out of this weird little pot and so I took it, you know? Thought it might make a good omelette or something. Scarius says that I’m being stupid, but he just wants to omelette for himself.

…

OK, so, right, omelette is a no go. Tried to crack the egg, no dice. Smashed it with a hammer. Still nothing. Sword? No chance. So I figured it might make a nice ornament or something, keep the barracks nice and decorative like.

…

Egg hatched today. Coincidentally, on the same day I lost two of my fingers. I get it though, poor thing was hungry, can’t begrudge a baby the occasional nip. Little green thing, scales and all, reckon it’s a dragon. Seems like a nice one though.

Captain wants me to kill it, but I’m not gonna do that. Poor thing just needs some love and some steak from the kitchen and they’ll be a good little beastie.

Need a name for them. Maybe Fang because they’ve got enough of them.

…

Captain acting strange today. Came back from the town all shaking and weird, says there’s some sort of infection or other, people going weird. I’m sure it’s nothing to worry about, I’ll just focus on keeping Fang well hidden. Don’t want anyone to know what I’ve done.

entries.name: Sun-scorched Recipe Book
entries.description:
Snake, I’ve always wanted to try snake. My grandmother told me once of a stew that used it, how the venom gave a spicy little kick when you chowed down on the meat. Yet, I cannot find a single snake in the desert, no matter how hard I try.

I know they’re here. I’ve seen their tracks. I’ve discovered the remains of their kills. I’ve even seen the bite marks on the ankles of foolish garou who slept out in the sands. They’re real, they’re just hiding away from us, as if scared of something.

There is this old legend about snakes. I heard it from my father, who heard it from his mother, who heard it from, well, you know how all of this goes. The story goes that the desert once teemed with snakes. You couldn’t move for fear of fangs in your sandals when you weren’t looking. Poison killed more of us than anything else. It was a dark time for the clan.

Then, she came. The moon goddess, who moved like river water. She danced and danced, and the snakes danced with her. With each undulation, the snakes dug themselves into the sand, their writhing movements burying them deep. When the dance was done, the snakes had vanished beneath the dunes, never to threaten the people again.

It’s a nice story; I’ve always liked it.

Oh, but anyway, where was I? Ah yes, the recipe for the perfect cactus stew, all you need is…

[The rest of the page has been torn off]

entries.name: The Tale of the Ghost Wolves
entries.description:
There once was a girl with a pet she adored.
He had fur like silver, eyes like ice.
The gentlest of natures.
He was ever so nice.
But there were things in the forest,
Full of shadow and hate.
When the girl found her friend,
It was sadly too late.
Eyes like glass.
Skin cold as stone.
The girl wept for days.
She’d never felt more alone.
Smoke rose through the woods,
Clawing and thick.
When the girl breathed it in,
It made her feel sick.
Yet in the choking and coughing,
There whispered a voice
Beautiful and terrible,
And it gave her a choice.
She could live as she was,
Alone in the night-black,
Or make a pact with the smoke,
And get her friend back.
She didn’t wait for a second.
She agreed with glee.
So the smoke told her to wait.
Where her best friend could see.
Eyes like embers.
Fur like fog.
Her last words uttered.
“You’re a very bad dog.”

entries.name: The Wolf and the Goddess
entries.description:
Dearg Due was loved and so was rewarded
Night would not fall on her mortal life.
But Dearg Due felt guilt for a gift undeserv-ed.

Cruel verse, cruel verse, the gift meets a curse.

Dearg Due bore her gift to a many-headed fiend.
She jumped into its maw – an immortal strike.
She tore and she rent, but fortune forsake her.

Cruel verse, cruel verse, the gift meets a curse.

The dragon cursed the wolf within its own gullet.
Dearg Due was doused in eternal unlife.
Spat back to Manafem, she stalked the sand, listless.

Cruel verse, cruel verse, the gift meets a curse

entries.name: Ulgo's Diary
entries.description:
Duneday

Ulgo made friends with man in the woods. Could not see face but they were very friendly. Made lots of pretty noises at Ulgo, though Ulgo does not know their words.

Tomorrow Ulgo is going to go and see if they want to play catch with him. Papa says that everyone loves playing catch, even though the villagers need to stand very far away so that the ball does not hurt them.

Threw stone once, because had no ball, and villager wouldn’t talk to me again after. Ulgo very sad. Villager never spoken to Ulgo again, so Ulgo cannot even say sorry.

Twiblick

Ulgo’s friend was in the woods again. Got a better look at him, his skin was all shiny and special. Maybe he got paints? Ulgo will ask Papa if he can get paints.

Friend in wood played very rough. When Ulgo threw him the ball, he did not throw it back. Instead he ran at Ulgo and tried to wrestle. Ulgo only ten, but Ulgo very strong, Papa always says so, and Ulgo push friend away.

entries.name: Weathered Diary
entries.description:
It is a strange thing to leave one’s home. All those old comforts, those familiar sights, smells and memories, just left behind. Stranger still, is leaving because you just don’t recognise it anymore.

Were we always so cruel? So callous and so shortsighted that we turn on our own just because they’re a little bit strange? So Jenna has seaweed for hair and eyes of literal sapphire. Isn’t that something to love about her, rather than hate?

Home is changed now. Those familiar sights are stained in horrid crimson. Those sentimental scents are tainted with a worrying touch of iron. Memories incinerated by rising flames, burning hope just as old neighbours burn away the homes of everyone different.

So we leave. We go north. Past the garou who snarl even though we have a treaty, and then down into the deep dark of the earth in search of a new home. One we pray will stand longer than the last.

A home we can be proud of.

entries.name: Weathered Journal
entries.description:
I have heard about the God Wars, in the stories that Grandfather gives. He passed them down from his father and his father before that, tales of epic battles and destructive forces beyond reason. This must have been what clashes between gods felt like.

Imaru and Kuldra, raging against one another using Ashenfall as a weapon. The wind became knives, the rocks hurled as cannon-fire, and the rain turned to hail, falling like great-hammers on everyone caught in their path. Cataclysmic powers crash against one another and each blow feels like it might tear the continent apart.

She feels different this time, Imaru. Changed. Like her grief and her rage have been forged into weapons and she slams them against the Godeater with unbridled hate. In response, Kuldra laughs, even though her armour shudders against the force of it, scales falling to the earth like the beginning flakes of winter snow.

There is a sensation in my chest -- strength being leeched from within me as Imaru presses the attack. I see old Mrs. Mossfoot stumble, hand across her chest, as each of the other villagers feel it too. The Blessing, a source of strength, now feels like a hole in each of us, draining us dry.

But for Imaru we’ll endure it. Against Kuldra we’ll stand.

Fellhollow does not fall this day!

entries.name: Withered Diary
entries.description:
I am still here. I am still here.

I am still me. I am still me.

I am withering and I cannot hold it back.

It begins with silence behind the eyes, as if there’s nothing there but the most basic of needs – the need to feed. More and more of us, ever since Imaru’s defeat and death at Kuldra’s claws, feels part of ourselves slipping away. I am dragged outside my being, I am drawn beyond my skull, my skin, myself.

And the world changes the more I am pulled away.

I see things that were not there before. Flickers, out of the corner of my eye. Doors that were not doors before. I see a great river undulating and flowing but rising and flooding as though something is blocked within it and forcing it to overflow.

But the worst is that feeling, of eyes upon me. As if something is not just watching me but focused on me. A predator waiting to strike.

I’ve seen what happens to those consumed by it. They walk still, but there is no life there, only hunger. A need to grab, claw and rend the living, desperate for a piece of the soul that seems lost.

In my bones I feel a tug, a current, drawing the part of me that’s… me… away.

I don’t want to become one of those monsters.

I am still here. I am still here.

I am still me. I am still me.

entries.name: Withered Journal
entries.description:
Death leaves its mark on the world. You feel it around graveyards, mausoleums and on the remnants of ancient battlefields that claimed hundreds of lives. It’s a pressure that presses against the air and weighs you down. Here the air is crushing, I feel myself being dragged to the floor by the grief and the rage attached to these bones.

Xikotal, Imaru’s mate, lies here dead and gone. His soul long since passed to the Afterlife, leaving Imaru alone and angry. Perhaps he was lucky to pass before seeing his mate like this. See the monster she has become since her death.

Still, this grief makes a powerful fetter. A thread of connection strong enough to forge a seal. I’ll lay it here, in this vault, protected from the dead by the dragonkin guardians. Hopefully that will keep it safe enough that no one can set this dread dragon free.

entries.name: A New Pestilence
entries.description:
Can't focus in my quarters. There's three of us in there. Too crowded. I can string thoughts together here. Not many - a few gems on a necklace.

We are afflicted by not one, but two diseases. They tussle, fighting. A cure needs to kill them both. 

I thought, maybe, if I poison one - the weaker one - then the other will eat it. Wither. Die. 

I think I know where the weak one resides. I hear it whisper in my left ear. I will dropper the toxin there. Let it feed. Yum. Let the toxin spread.

Shush! The chicken and the master come again. I must look busy.

Busy busy busy busy busy.

entries.name: Alric's Journal
entries.description:
Is it regret or hubris that banishes my dreams each night? I cannot remember the last time I dreamed a dream of my own, and not that of… the other.

Perhaps it is the foolishness of an old man, clinging to the sharpness of his youth. The passage of time curses me with a dullness that is not my own. My flesh feels alien to me, as if I am a skin worn by something else. My insides writhe and burn like snakes of fire. Even touch feels strange to me, as if there were layers of strange cloth between me and the world.

Is this age? Foolishness? Or something worse?

Our demons have said nothing for some time. The voices tell me to ignore it, that I am overthinking things and just need to try to sleep. Yet the others whisper threats and curses from the corners of the room, the cracks in the ceiling, wishing me naught but harm.

I have made this place better, stronger, more powerful. It was by my hand that we brought the demons through. They should bow in adoration of my power, yet they laugh at me from behind the curtains and pretend they’re not really there.

All will come to respect me.

All will come to despise me.

The whispers are wrong: I am not mad.

The whispers are right.

entries.name: Alric's Plan (Part 1)
entries.description:
The thought came to me as I slept. Should I worry that my genius rises when I am defenceless? Rasmodel would do much with that information.

You see, nothing enthralls a demon more than other demons. They despise and bicker, drawn into a game of spite.  It may seem like repulsion, but in truth they are drawn to one another. They live - should you call it living - to be in each other's company.

Knowing this to be true, I think on my skills of possession. I am still mastering the art, but there have been breakthroughs. I am able to siphon a soul from the living and store it in the inanimate, just for a moment. My goblet gained the soul of a slave (and filled with tears! A delightful discovery). My mirror reflected only my last, sycophantic apprentice, for a time, at least.

If I could bottle and transpose the soul of a demon - or whatever makeshift thing they have as a soul - could I infuse a demonic gateway? My theory, my hope, is that the gateway would enthrall others of their kind. They would be drawn, consciously or subconsciously, in numbers that we could barely contain. A portal like that would need an incredible number of demonic souls to keep powered, but, in that respect, I am not worried. The infernal gate would supply itself.

entries.name: Alric’s Plan (Part 2)
entries.description:
If I were to weigh Rasmodel, he would have one ounce of value. That ounce is his leadership, or, more specifically, what I have learned from it. 

He has taught me that when you make a mistake, you do not run from it. Instead, you claim it was your intention all along. If a scouting party is killed, they were traitors that you sent on a suicide mission. If the sewers flood and illness spreads, you were building the troops' immunity. Admit nothing, own everything.

My infernal gateway is no longer a gateway. The tens of thousands of demon souls are no longer powering it. It seems that they have been quietly bleeding into the fortress itself. Each brick now whispers with the avernic. They are in the walls. Demons now summon themselves, at their own whims, from any room.

I do not run from this. It was my intention. I claim it.

This is what I tell my magi: there is no corner of Dowdun Reach that is safe from us now. If you connive against us magi, a demon may be listening. If you walk without a partner, an avernic may digest you. This is the rule of the keep now. 

All that remains is to find the voice beneath the voices. I know it is there - I can hear it. Once it is identified, I will claim it, too.

entries.name: An Acolyte's Guide to Demon Handling
entries.description:
I'm out of here - being transferred to the Library. These are my handover notes. Don't worry, you'll get the hang of demon-handling in no time.

1. 'Demon-handling' is a turn of phrase. Avoid touching 'em.

2. Marrentil round the nostrils helps with the sulphur smell.

3. Demons don't like it if you copy their gruff voices.

4. While they may not cover up their nethers, you would be wise not to stare.

5. Awfunctious has learned to copy Alric's voice. Alric'll only talk to you if he wants a cup of tea.

6. Alric likes white tea, no sugar. 

7. Always look at what you're signing. Requisition forms have a habit of being swapped for demon pacts.

8. You can tell it's a demon pact because it reeks of sulphur - even the marrentil won't stop it.

9. When locking up, make sure to test your binding spells. Festilius has a habit of finding flaws and unwinding them. 

10. If you lose Festilius, he'll be in the chicken coop.

entries.name: Archmage’s Note to Students
entries.description:
Apprentice - a word, if you will.

I see that you are eager to progress. That's good. Eagerness will get you far under the gaze of Zamorak. Eagerness needs two partners, however. Power and knowledge. 

Power is easy. It is everywhere, as long as you take off the blindfold of morality. Power does not bring corruption, but freedom. Only with power - true power - can we rise to the heights that we deserve to reach.

But knowledge, that is a harder path. That journey starts here, in the books of the library.  

First, build a THRONE, a place to sit in cold detachment. Then construct an unbreakable PHILOSOPHY, one that describes you. On that structure weave SORCERY, the light that guides. Only then, finally, can you CONQUER all.

entries.name: Hall of Heroes
entries.description:
Dowdun Reach isn’t just the home of warriors. It is the birthplace of legends. Those who refused to follow the limited, vapid doctrines of the Saradominist faith and come to understand that freedom itself is a virtue worth fighting for.

Within these halls rest the pathbuilders and wayfinders for a new world order. One born of personal choice and freedom, rather than tyranny and oppression. They are not interred in nearby graves, nor scattered as ashes across the firmament. No, they rest within these very walls, each statue housing what is left of their earthly forms.

There is Isla, known as the Blood Witch, or the Lady of Screams. She was the first to prise the secrets of runecrafting from the blue robed wizards, passing that knowledge on to our own mages so that we might tear open the veil of reality and make bargains with the infernal realm.

Gregor Volrath, the Mountain Lion, defended these mountains in the days before the keep was tall enough to defend itself. The mithril lined crags were too tempting for the neighbouring villagers and Gregor held them back with hammer and shield.

Each statue houses a legacy. Each stone stores a soul. Each footstep that echoes through these walls is a reminder of the great heroes that walked here before.

entries.name: Quartermaster's Journal
entries.description:
Am I the only one that works around here? Because it seems like I am. Each day, I log the incoming supplies and assign where they’ll go in the keep; and each day, everyone forgets that I need money to secure them.

Instead, they bicker and fight among themselves like pups.

We were great once, weren’t we? The mighty Children of Shadows, reborn as Zamorak’s knights of black! We were magi with the power to call a legion of demons to serve at our command.

Now, I have to explain to the cook why we’ve got three cabbages between us, and find a way to make it last a week.

I would leave, if the Shadows would let me. But they tell me I have work to do, and must stay here to keep it going. I try to ignore them as best I can, but they can be so very cruel.

Deny what is written.

Take what is offered.
Give nothing back.
Deny what is written.

Repeto.

entries.name: Armadyl
entries.description:
The aviansie deity, Armadyl, is know as the god of justice. Though young, by god standards, and naïve by many others, Armadyl has a devoted following due to his care for his people.

In the god wars, he perhaps most of all, suffered at the hands of Zamorak, for when Zamorak destroyed Forinthry, it took Armadyl’s people with it. Whole settlements were wiped out in a single sweeping motion, thousands of the aviansie reduced to ash. Including Armadyl’s own husband.

Since the edicts, Armadyl has had a change of heart. While he will fight if he has to, he prefers a more peaceful path. He returned to Gielinor to put a stop to Bandos’ warmongering, preventing him from turning the planet into a war-torn wreck. Though Armadyl holds peace as the highest virtue, he was not afraid to kill the god of war.

On Ashenfall, Armadyl and his people did not take part in the dragon conflict. They disappeared deeper into the mainland and have not been heard of for centuries. Though Armadyl has left Gielinor and returned to the world of his people, there are rumours of winged beings living further into the continent.

entries.name: Bandos
entries.description:
Few deities are responsible for as much death and destruction as the self-styled “big high war god” Bandos. On his own world, he brought destruction and became the last one standing in a planet-wide war. When he ascended, he brought this war to other planets, wiping out countless civilisations for the Grand Sport of war.

He came to Gielinor for the God Wars, delighting in death and destruction between entities as powerful as him. He aligned with Saradomin and Armadyl to battle Zamorak, helping corner the lord of chaos and forcing his hand.

entries.name: Cathan
entries.description:
Cathan is the first to tell you that he was raised in privilege. Wealthy family. Loving parents. Everything a growing boy could need. Yet, like for so many of us, it wasn’t enough. He craved excitement, exploration and adventure, yearning more than anything to discover the wonders of the world. 

As a child he slipped away from his family, in search of adventure and monsters to slay. He found more than he bargained for, and the lesson for his hubris cost him a leg. 

In the months that followed, the boy fell into a deep darkness. Life offered little meaning when he could barely walk a few steps. His parents, in response, hired him a tutor, so that he might rekindle that spark of adventure that had once burned so brightly. 

It worked. In Vannaka he found someone that could push him out of his melancholy. Who taught him how to wield a blade and target the weaknesses of his foes. Vannaka brought in others, who helped train him further. In Zanik, young Cathan, learned how to survive in the wilds. In Doric he learned to craft weapons and armour to take down his foes. Finally, the Wise Old Man taught him a little bit of magic, and young Cathan’s curious excitement burned brightly once more. 

When the opportunity came to explore a new land, Cathan was the first to sign up and convinced his mentors to join him. As they sailed to Ashenfall he stood at the bow of the ship smiling at the adventures ahead. 

In the chaos that followed, he’s keenly aware of that age old phrase “be careful what you wish for”.

entries.name: Doric
entries.description:
Doric is a master smith who trained in the dwarven capital of Keldagrim. He owns a smithing shop in Asgarnia alongside his son Boric. The two of them have a strained relationship because Boric took it personally when Doric sent him to Keldagrim to complete his training. 

To rebuild trust and show his son that he has the uttermost faith in his abilities, Doric has left the running of the shop to Boric in his absence. Now, Doric comes to Ashenfall in search of new metals, lost smithing techniques, and the blueprints of ancient weapons. 

Not much of a fighter himself these days, he prefers to stay out of harm’s way, but he knows how to wield a hammer if push comes to shove.

entries.name: Saradomin
entries.description:
Saradomin is known as the god of order. Once human himself, he is perhaps the most popular deity on Gielinor, especially among other humans. He preaches tradition, education and righteousness, and prizes human well being above almost everything else.

During the third age, he was part of the God Wars and waged a holy campaign against the usurper, Zamorak. These two deities remain in eternal conflict, both considering each other their greatest foe. This hatred has spread to their followers and has been the cause of many conflicts across Gielinor’s past.

The church of Saradomin watches over much of the mainland kingdoms, with priests and the faithful advising the leaders of entire nations.

He is depicted as a bearded man wearing a crown, often carrying a staff. His symbol is a four pointed star.

entries.name: Vannaka
entries.description:
The mysterious warrior, Vannaka, is regarded as one of the premier slayer masters in the world. He trained under the legendary Duradel, and the two even duelled one another once. Duradel won. Something Vannaka has never entirely managed to get over. 

Vannaka’s origins are mysterious. He claims no nation as his homeland, nor does he speak of family or friends. Conversations lead only to talk of combat and the slaying of dangerous creatures. Yet there is something about Ashenfall that creates a silence in him. He stares out across the continent as if searching for something.

entries.name: Wise Old Man
entries.description:
Dionysius was once a legendary adventurer. In his youth, he single-handedly defeated the troll invasion of Keldagrim. He crushed the enemies of one of the mountain tribes and taught the people of Karamja how to use powerful herbs that might aid them in battle. He committed great deeds throughout his life, and the world is a better place with him in it.

Or it was.

After he settled down, finishing his book on destructive magic, Dionysius began to feel that the world was a little unfair. He had tirelessly given his youth for the betterment of the world, and he had nothing to show for it. Even his devout faith in Saradomin wasn’t making his life more comfortable.

So, like so many do, he turned to crime. He targeted the nearby bank, his magic making quick work of their security, and he lifted himself a great deal of gold as well as a snazzy blue party hat. Content to consider this repayment for saving the world so often, he now sits back and enjoys his well-earned wealth.

The Temple Knights consider him an ultraviolet archangel threat and watch him very closely... from very far away.

entries.name: Zamorak
entries.description:
The god of chaos, Zamorak, is often associated with evil. In truth, it is more complicated than this, as Zamorak promotes freedom and self-improvement, rather than relying on tradition. Needless to say, he and Saradomin have been in conflict across the ages.

Zamorak is one of the Mahjarrat, the mysterious creatures from the world of Freneskae. He was recruited to serve under the Empty Lord, Zaros, but he found Zaros’ methods too hands-off for his tastes. Using two of the Elder Artefacts, Zamorak betrayed Zaros and drained him of enough of his power to allow Zamorak to ascend. Zaros, presumed defeated, disappeared into the void where he might rebuild his strength.

News of his usurpation of Zaros is what began the God Wars, the greatest and bloodiest battle in Gielinor’s history. An alliance of Saradomin, Bandos and Armadyl, pushed Zamorak to the brink and caused him to destroy the entire region of Forinthry in a last desperate ploy. This act awoke Guthix from his slumber, and caused him to enact the Edicts that would banish the gods.

Zamorak has tried repeatedly to reclaim Gielinor, using the legions of demons at his beck and call. He has been pushed back by alliances of heroes, yet is always scheming to return and finish what he started.

entries.name: Zanik
entries.description:
Few have lived a life as rich with adventure as the cave goblin Zanik. She was the first of her people to brave the sunlight, the first cave goblin to meet humans and the surface goblins, the first to learn about the gods and their influence on the world, and the first cave goblin to stand side by side with the World Guardian in defence of creation.

It cost her her life. Twice. 

She was once the Chosen Commander of the war god Bandos, who tried to use prophecy to put her under his thrall. She died; he resurrected her and then used magic to seize control. She resisted, fighting off his influence. Bandos’s lingering affliction on her soul would claim her life after the War God’s demise, but even death wouldn’t stop her.  

She became the emissary of the Underworld, resurrected once more by the god Icthlarin, and brought back to the surface to join the fight against the Elder Gods. 

Now, she comes to Ashenfall in search of a lost and forgotten tribe. Hoping to stop history from repeating itself.

entries.name: Place Bleakfields Valley
entries.description: This was the first settlement in Fellhollow. The humans that fled Bramblemead and its cruelty set up the first tents, cabins and early homes here. They would farm, forage and do their best to survive, until gentle Imaru and Xikotal took them in and brought them to Emberwood, where they might found a stronger settlement.

entries.name: Place Bloodblight Swamp
entries.description:
Once these lands were fertile plains. Great fields of wheat and barely were sewn by the garou that made it their home. It was a resting place for a people that had been hunted for too long, a sanctuary at last.

But General Velgar put a stop to that dream. He was injured in battle with an arrogant god, flesh scarred in conflict, with wounds weeping. His blood, warped by the magic gifted to him by his queen, became a terrible toxin that cursed the region forever.

Now, poison mists float out of the soil. All the water is corrupted by this toxic blood. The air alone is dangerous, tinted green by the vengeful cruelty of Ghornfell’s master.

The garou here have grown resistant to the poison, though their minds are addled by constant exposure. They are more dangerous, more violent and more filled with hatred, with an entire settlement that seethes with rage.

Monstrous creatures roam this region. Ancient nightmares from another work prowl in the shadows, hunting any that might foolishly enter unprepared.

entries.name: Place Bramblemead Valley
entries.description:
Bramblemead valley is home to the village of its namesake, a once tranquil location bustling with life. It was founded in the first age by the god Guthix and his followers, and converted to the worship of Saradomin sometime in the third age.

The Keep of Blue Flames, was built in the popular style of the Saradominist faithful. The ordered shape a symbol of the god of order’s will. Powdered metals were cast into the braziers, so that the flames would burn in the hue favoured by Saradomin. Here the lord of the region would watch over the village and surrounding areas, under the careful guidance of the high priest of the church.

To the northwest stands a symbol of mankind’s thirst for knowledge, a great guild dedicated to uncovering the secrets of the runes that had been first discovered on Ashenfall by Guthix himself. Here, powerful wizards learned spells and enchantments, pushing the boundaries of mankind’s knowledge.

Ashenfall is rife with danger and the need for heroes has always been strong. A guild was created, to the east of Brynmoor, where heroes and champions would gather together to seek out the deadliest monsters and slay them where they stood.

Once this valley was the hub of human activity, but now it sits silent, and overrun with monsters. Goblins spread across the region claiming it in the name of their new god. Rats swarm through the ruins with sharp and deadly fangs. Soil that was once fertile farmland, is now soaked to the roots in blood.

entries.name: Place Coalridge Pass
entries.description: I wish I could tell you a detailed story about Coalridge Pass, but alas it’s name is far too simple. There is a ridge, you see, and it’s full of coal. That’s it, that’s the lore. I know, I know, I’m as disappointed as you are.

entries.name: Place Ddr Approach
entries.description:
Looking upon Dowdun Reach, you would struggle to find anything that doesn’t scream “we worship the god of chaos!”. The walls are adorned with the red flags of Zamorak, the windows bear his mark, and everything is decorated with just a little more malice than any normal architect would attempt.

This place once served as a warning, reminder and invitation, depending on who approached. To the villagers of Fellhollow, it was a warning that they were straying too far from the comforts of home. To those wishing to proselytise their faith, it was a reminder that the residents within the keep were not interested. Finally, those to whom chaos had a place in their hearts, the flags, the décor and the sinister sensation was a welcoming invitation, bringing them home.

entries.name: Place Ddr Bastion
entries.description: For all its bluster and self-assured strength, Dowdun Reach is a fortress designed to keep everyone out. There were no armies at their doors; the armies of Saradomin were too far to the south and dragons have no need for infantry when they can burn a kingdom from the skies. Yet, despite there being no need for safety, these walls stand strong and sturdy, weathering centuries of quiet neglect.

entries.name: Place Ddr Cathedral
entries.description:
As the god of chaos and rebellion, you’d expect Zamorak to discourage churches, yet hypocrisy is chaos too, so he’s always pleased to see a temple in his name. Especially one with expensive windows, carefully crafted sculptures and an adoring army of priests, chanting his name.

One must have an ego to be a god, and Zamorak has more followers than most.

The priests of the Cathedral spend their days and nights in quiet contemplation… well they did, before everything went wrong. Now they wander the rooms muttering to themselves and hurling deadly spells at anyone who approaches.

Zamorak enjoys all this chaos just as much.

entries.name: Place Ddr Courtyard
entries.description:
Even worshippers of the so called “god of evil”, a moniker levied on Zamorak by the Saradomin worshippers, have a need for green spaces. Nature is soothing, grounding and calming, it can do wonders for our mental health, and sometimes even those who follow the lord of chaos need somewhere to relax.

This was the courtyard once, long ago now: a place of gentle contemplation and relaxation, before the corruption took hold.

Now, it is a wild and overgrown place, infected by chickens and chincompas alike. A good place to set up camp, for those with decent survival instincts, but not somewhere you’re likely to find much of a chance to relax.

entries.name: Place Ddr Grand Hall
entries.description:
Contrary to the name, this isn’t just a great big corridor. Indeed, this is the place where the knights would gather to discuss battle tactics, hold religious debates and unleash exceedingly angry chickens upon the new recruits.

We have tried to work out what the point of the chickens was, but so far the historical documents have been annoyingly sparse on answers.

entries.name: Place Ddr Library
entries.description:
It will surprise no one that the library was the favourite hangout for many of the Zamorakian mages. They would read up on ancient mysteries, learn about new spells and they would work through the finer points of demonic contracts in a bid to avoid accidentally selling their souls.

There are rumours of a secret set of books detailing the sordid romances of the ancient Mahjarrat, but if anyone has found the hiding place of such grimoires, they have yet to share them with me.

Not that I care. I wouldn’t read them. Honest.

entries.name: Place Ddr Pastures
entries.description:
There is a phrase “to put them out to pasture” which is used to describe someone being discarded, or perhaps even left to die. In Dowdun Reach, this was depressingly literal. There’s a reason that the rats are everywhere in the Pastures - a reason why the grass is so alive, despite the dilapidation of the rest of the region. 

It is because the soil is nurtured by the bodies of those cultists that were not able to keep up with the rest of the fortress.

entries.name: Place Deaths Temple
entries.description: A temple, to a long forgotten god of man. This place is abandoned, fallen into ruin, with no remnants of who it was dedicated to before. Sometimes even places can die, as the last memories of their purpose fade into nothingness. Now, it has become the property of Death and he resides here on the edge of Fellhollow, waiting for someone that can assist him with his problems.

entries.name: Place Emberwood
entries.description:
Emberwood was the perfect village, at least for a time. After years of monotheistic rule turning them against one another, the villagers sought strength in variety. They created churches to each of the four major gods - Saradomin, Zamorak, Guthix and Armadyl - and each had a voice at the table, whenever discussions were had.

Amalgamated walked side by side with those who had not been touched by the anima of Ashenfall. Whilst it would be naïve to claim there was no prejudice, it was much more frowned upon and the Amalgamated could find themselves rising to any height of society, with only a little more effort than their peers.

It was far from perfect, but it was trying to get there. It could have been a wonderful place to live.

Kuldra’s cruelty put a stop to that, and Imaru’s grief-filled rage corrupted it all into a nightmare of fear and pain.

entries.name: Place Fractured Plains
entries.description:
The anima of Ghornfell is less table than that of Brynmoor, and the anima twist’s effects are more pronounced. Plants take on the hues of dragonfire, making the entire region dance like an inferno when the summer wind blows.

Towering in the distance is a great tower, shattered now yet still imbued with ancient dragonkin magic. A terrible roaring can be heard from this structure and a shadow passes over it when General Velgar returns. The dragon makes his lair in the remains of a dragonkin’s hubris, a monument to an architect long since dead.

Garou make their homes across this region, sending out hunting parties to slaughter anything that crosses their path.

Atop the mesa, something glistens in the moonlight and a mournful sound carries on the wind. A sorrow that resonates in shimmering crystal.

entries.name: Place Hopes Fall
entries.description:
Grief is a physical thing, a weight upon the world that puts gravity to shame. It’s a web of chains that wrap around more than just a single person, but everything they touch. It can be all-consuming, all-encompassing, if we don’t keep it in check.

Grief is the shadow of love, and sometimes it can be poisoned, twisting from something beautiful into something ugly and full of hate.

This land hates. It has been warped and twisted, Imaru’s grief has become so heavy that it has dragged the place down into the Underworld and let the land of the dead bleed through.

Xikotal’s corpse lies here, the love of Imaru’s life, and each time she looks upon it, the chains of grief tighten and strangle the land just a little more.

entries.name: Place Lake Of Lost Souls
entries.description:
The water here is filled with the torn fragments of souls, the victims of the Withering and Imaru’s boundless hunger. The waters of Noumenon have seeped in through cracks in the world and infected the great lake that once lay here.

In a forgotten time, great dragons would bathe in the lake alongside villagers and the populace would gather round to relax in the warm springs that fed the lake bed.

Grief and rage had poisoned the waters, turning it into a danger best avoided.

entries.name: Place Sw Scorned Wilderness
entries.description:
Rasthin’s built a device that would harness the power of the Wellspring, attuning an individual to one of the runic elements, granting them power beyond reasoning without any of the pesky limitations of godhood. Selfishly, she hoarded this power for herself and her allies; using what gifts were granted her to manipulate, control or destroy her enemies.

When Kuldra broke free of her chains and rose up against her dragonkin masters, Rasthin refused to allow the queen to gain access to the power of the Wellspring and turned her device into a weapon. In one great act of defiance, her device exploded and tore the region apart, shattering it into floating islands in defiance of the laws of gravity. The damage is felt across all of Ashenfall, but none so intensely as here.

Now, Kuldra has made this place her palace. She sits on the remnants of Rasthin’s technology and works to transform it into a weapon that threatens all of Gielinor. If she is not stopped, she will unleash shockwaves of pure anima that will rip the mainlands into fractured islands, just like the ones she calls home.

None will survive the process.

Place Vaults
entries.description:
Hidden across Ashenfall are the Vaults, the ruined remains of Dragonkin research. Each contains lost knowledge or riches, sealed away so that none but their jealous masters might possess them.

Paranoid and wary of intrusion by the “lesser races”, the Dragonkin of Ashenfall filled each of the vaults with an array of deadly traps and they created servitor guardians to watch over them.

Although time has whittled away at most of the mysteries, the cruel claws of entropy rending secrets to shreds, there still remain pieces of powerful knowledge that bold adventurers might be able to salvage.

entries.name: Place Whispering Swamp
entries.description:
When war broke out between humans and garou, it was the swamps that formed a buffer between the two factions. The muddy water was difficult to fight in and neither side enjoyed the idea of drowning on the battlefield.

Now, the swap retains the memories of that conflict, swallowing down the remnants of that battle into its murky depths.

Yet, among all the ruin and the decay, the swamp is rife with ingredients for crafting. Herbs grow between the weeds and the caves that run along the swamp’s edges are filled with ore.

Still, one must be ever careful. Goblins roam these regions, hunters keeping an eye out for northern invaders. The garou watch from Ghornfell, ready for any foolish trespasser that might enter their domain.

And in the darkness of night, an ancient horror walks the region, offering only death’s embrace to any it finds.

entries.name: Attacking
entries.description:
Unfortunately, conflict is inevitable on Ashenfall. You will need to hit things with clubs, stab them with daggers and impale your foes with a volley of carefully crafted arrows.

There are three main combat styles, magic, ranged and melee, each one has its strengths and its weaknesses.

Magic attacks are capable of generating powerful side effects, air magic can knock something back, fire magic can burn your enemies to a crisp. However, you will need a steady supply of runes to keep casting spells.

Ranged attacks can snipe enemies from afar, but you’ll need to make sure you don’t run out of arrows.

Melee attacks get up close and personal, but you won’t need to worry about ammunition to lay the smackdown on that uppity little goblin – not Zanik – who’s been giving you lip.

When engaged in battle, keep an eye on your stamina, as each attack will cost you some of it. As you level up your combat skills, you’ll be able to deal longer combo chains to more efficiently use your stamina.

entries.name: Cosiness
entries.description:
Home is where the heart is. Which is a horrifying statement when you think about it.

Still, home has its advantages, and cosiness is one of those. When you build a home and claim a bed, you’ll find that life just feels much easier to manage. Specifically, you’ll find that your Hydration, Endurance and Sustenance bars become much easier to manage.

While you remain within the comfort of your home, you’ll need to eat less, drink less and rest less. Meaning that you can craft to your hearts content, without worrying about little things like starving to death.

entries.name: Defending
entries.description:
Armour will make life easier, reducing the damage you receive. The better the armour, the greater the damage reduction. Be sure to upgrade your gear at every opportunity. 

You may also want to avoid damage from time to time. A well-timed block will  parry the attack, negating all damage and staggering the enemy granting you a window to perform a visceral counterattack. While, if like me you prefer to avoid a knife in the stomach, you can always dodge an attack and get out of the way.

Perhaps the best way to protect one’s most precious internal organs, is to get out of the way of an attacker before they can stab you. Dodging is the key to this. Dash, roll and scream incoherently as you whiz away from an enemy’s attack before I can reach you. You can dodge in multiple directions, so make sure to keep an eye on your surroundings so you don't dodge off a cliff or anything. 

I did that once. Not fun.

entries.name: Durability
entries.description:
Nothing lasts forever, just ask my knees. Time was they were spry and full of life, now they grate together like an angry pair of hedgehogs getting in a fight. Equipment is similarly affected. Weapons, armour and tools have a limited amount of durability before they stop working. Think of it like hitpoints for inanimate objects.

You can repair an object at a crafting bench, or you can use certain spells to recover durability. Once an item breaks, it won’t be destroyed, but it won’t be useful until you can repair it. So make sure to keep an eye on your gear’s durability.

entries.name: Endurance
entries.description:
We all need to rest from time to time. Sometimes everything just gets too much, we get tired, stressed, and just generally beaten down by the world, and it’s no different on Ashenfall.

Rest represents your overall state of resilience. Your ability to overcome to mental trials of the wild. It will deplete over time if you’re not resting, as well as every time you suffer lethal damage. Certain environmental effects will also take their toll.

The lower your Rest, the less functional you’ll be. You’ll find it harder to lug everything around. It becomes more draining to swing an axe, or a sword. Even magic will become more difficult as you tired yourself out.

There are four levels of Rest:

Well-rested - this will leave you functioning at your best

Tired, you’ll start to suffer penalties to your Stamina, as well as your Carrying Capacity.

Knackered - everything is really starting to get to you. You’ll suffer penalties to Stamina, Carry Capacity and even find yourself thirstier and hungrier.

Exhausted- you’ll suffer heavy penalties to Stamina and Carry Capacity, as well as finding spells more expensive to cast.

Fortunately you can recover your Rest with a nice long rest in bed.

entries.name: Food
entries.description:
We are all slaves to the beast within the belly. Its gurgling roar urges us ever onward to consume, consume, consume. At least that’s the excuse I use when people ask about my ever-expanding midriff.

Still, we need food to survive, even the most restrictive (sane) diet plans acknowledge that. Ashenfall has a wealth of options, some delicious and others… well… less so. Food will increase your Sustenance meter, which makes you healthier and heartier. Some food will also provide special benefits, such as resistances to poison.

The higher quality the food, the longer its effects last, so make sure you’re always making the best meals you can.

entries.name: Hydration
entries.description:
Water is the most basic necessity for all known life on Gielinor. Dehydration is deadlier than the strongest monster, guaranteeing death in its victims if they suffer it long enough.

Your Hydration meter tracks how well hydrated you are. The higher your meter, the better your rate of stamina regeneration – allowing you to perform more actions. Skill longer. Fight better.

Should your Hydration meter reach zero, you’ll start to suffer constant health loss until you can refill your meter by drinking a source of water.

Dirty water can be found in ponds, lakes and other bodies of water around Ashenfall. Dirty water can be purified by boiling it at a campfire.
